closed_issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
closed_issue_source_snapshot.body:
Deterministic (reproduced across 4 independent full-suite runs by two sessions, 2026-07-04): `components/d5-chat-turn-render.test.ts` > "the fenced code block's content survives intact" FAILS in a full `bun test` run but passes 6/6 when the file runs alone. Independence proven: the failure reproduces with the newest (b17) test files removed from the tree entirely (2593 pass/1 fail/138 files), so it is not caused by the current change set.

Hypothesis: shared terminal/render singleton state (Ink pipeline or a module-level screen buffer) bleeding across test files in the same worker — the failing assertion sees a polluted render surface. The suite output also shows raw ANSI cursor-position escape sequences leaking into the test log from some earlier file, consistent with a shared-screen singleton not being torn down.

Fix spec: (1) identify the state carrier — bisect by running d5 paired with each earlier test file (binary search over the file list) until the minimal failing pair is found; receipt = the pair + the shared module/singleton named; (2) cure = proper per-file teardown/reset of that singleton (never a test-order band-aid, never skipping the test); (3) acceptance = full suite green AND the minimal failing pair green AND a regression note in the test explaining the carrier. Standing rules: error-free not silenced — do not mark-flaky or retry-loop it; suite line re-run after final edit, before any binary hash.

comments.author: wordingone
comments.body:
Root cause found — a real production bug, not a flake (d5 was correctly never flaky-marked). Singleton carrier: `process.env["EMBER_SYNTAX_HIGHLIGHT"]`. The entrypoint seeds it `??= "0"` on import, and the render gate read it as `!!value` — `!!"0"` is `true`, so any test file importing the entrypoint flipped highlighting ON for the rest of the shared test process, inserting per-token ANSI codes into d5's fenced block and breaking its contiguous-substring assertion. Side-finding: every real launch to date has therefore run with highlighting ON despite the documented "0" default.

Resolution (maintainer ruling): the gate becomes `=== "1"` (matching the entrypoint's 0/1 string convention), a per-file `afterAll` clears the four import-time-seeded env keys (each layer independently proven sufficient against the minimal failing pair), AND the seeded default flips to "1" — the live default remains highlighting ON, because the field exemplar this surface is gated against renders code blocks highlighted and every shipped build has too. The bug delivered the intended experience through the wrong mechanism; the fix keeps the experience and corrects the mechanism, with a new test locking the entry-path default and the unset-env fallback. Suite goes 2698/1 → 2702/0.

closed_issue_source_snapshot.body:
## Finding (2026-07-07 attestation sweep, receipts in PR #348's body)

receipts/ember-preloop-resident-gate/reference-uiux-ax-observation-20260622T151722Z.json is the single decisive-claim receipt left uncoverable by the attested spend annex, for three independently verified reasons:

1. Its own cited evidence file (real-reference-uiux-ax-observation-...-adapter-trace.log) does not exist on disk under the cited name.
2. The similarly-named file (without the 'real-' prefix) that does exist has a hash that does NOT match what the receipt claims.
3. A direct content re-scan of the receipt found openai/api_key pattern hits (content-dirty under the paid-surface scan).

## Why this is disposition-worthy, not just coverage debt
A receipt whose evidence pointer is nonexistent and whose near-name evidence hash-mismatches is the fabrication class the 2026-07-07 VOID chain exists for (cf. the C-BASE degenerate-receipt VOIDs). It dates to the 2026-06-22 preloop-resident-gate era and currently blocks C(-1) at 1/262 — honestly, and it should keep blocking until disposed rather than be laundered into coverage.

## Proposed disposition (per VOID discipline — supersede, never delete)
Write a VOID receipt superseding it (reason: evidence-untraceable + content-dirty; cites: the #348 verification trail), THEN let the spend scanner classify both files by its own rules on the next annex generation. If the scanner's decisive-claim set honors supersession, C(-1) resolves honestly; if it does not, the probe's treatment of VOID'd receipts is the follow-up question, answered by its own code, not by hand-editing anything.

## Bar
No file edits, no deletions. The original stays on disk untouched; the VOID + annex regeneration + consumer-path verification are the only moves.

closed_issue_source_snapshot.body:
## Scoped follow-up from PR #350 (its body documents the mechanism)
spend_annex_scan.py now excludes VOID-superseded receipts from the decisive-claim set ((basename, sha256) match against every VOID receipt's supersedes list) — but test_c_neg1.py's own _decisive_claim_files() does not mirror that exclusion. Result: the probe counts a superseded receipt as undeclared+uncovered even though the annex correctly emits no row for it. Live instance: C(-1) reads RED 1/264 where the 1 is exactly reference-uiux-ax-observation-20260622T151722Z.json — formally disposed via the #349 VOID, excluded by the scanner, still counted by the probe.

## Cure
Factor the supersession-exclusion logic into a shared helper (the scanner's implementation is the reference — same (basename, sha256) semantics, same 'VOID receipt itself stays in-set' rule) and have BOTH the scanner and test_c_neg1 consume it. Regression tests: (1) a superseded receipt is excluded by the probe with the exclusion disclosed in the reason text (never silently); (2) the VOID receipt itself is still counted; (3) a supersedes entry whose sha256 does not match the on-disk file does NOT exclude (the cbase VOID receipts record checkpoint shas, not receipt-file shas — they must not match; PR #350's body documents this live case).

## Bar
The probe's exclusion must be as disclosed as the scanner's (an excluded_superseded list or equivalent in the reason text) — an exclusion that just makes the number smaller with no trace is indistinguishable from laundering.

C-CUSTODY currently reports counts only ('untracked=9 unparseable=0 cited_missing=10') — the violating paths are not enumerated anywhere, so every consumer must re-derive them with its own (approximate) logic; the coordinator's independent sweep found 51 candidate cited-missing against the probe's 10, and the true set is unknowable without re-implementing the probe's citation extraction exactly.

Acceptance: test_c_custody.py gains a machine-readable detail emission — either (a) a --detail flag printing the three violation lists as JSON to stdout, or (b) (preferred) an always-written sidecar under scripts/ember_totality/receipts-custody/ carrying {untracked:[], unparseable:[], cited_missing:[]} per run, named with the run timestamp. comments.author: wordingone
comments.body:
Live confirmation from board receipt ember-totality-20260708T043327Z (post-#403-merge): C-CUSTODY RED with `18 violations; untracked=8 unparseable=0 cited_missing=10` — and the row carries only these counts, so nothing is actionable without re-running the probe by hand.

**Root cause located, cure is small:** `test_c_custody.py:192-206` BUILDS a full `receipt_obj` with an `offenders` enumeration (untracked / unparseable / cited_missing lists) and then never writes it — dead code; only the count string survives into the emit. The cure is to dump that object to a sidecar (e.g. `scripts/ember_totality/receipts-custody/custody-<ts>.json`, fsync'd) and reference the sidecar filename in the emit line so every RED names its offenders.

**Second finding for the same acceptance (design ruling needed):** custody violations are structurally perpetual under current semantics — every board run mints new untracked receipts (the totality receipt itself + milestone/publication/disconfirmation writes), so the tree is custody-dirty the moment the board finishes, and a same-hour snapshot chase (as #403's straggler list demonstrated: six new stragglers were minted between snapshot and merge) can never converge. The sidecar's enumeration should therefore tag each offender with its mtime relative to the last landing, and the probe needs ONE of: (a) an age-window (receipts younger than the last master commit touching receipts/ are 'pending-landing', counted separately, not violations), or (b) a standing land-the-receipts step in the post-board loop. Preference: (a) for the probe semantics plus (b) as the operational loop — the pending-landing count then trends to zero on every landing instead of oscillating RED forever.

## Defect

`scripts/ember_totality/test_surface2.py` line 114: `DEFAULT_EXEC_ROOT = os.environ.get("EMBER_EXEC_ROOT", "<local-exec-root>")` — the default is a **redaction placeholder**, not a path. A placeholder string can never be a directory, so the probe emits `UNEVALUABLE: execution root <local-exec-root> not found` on every machine, unconditionally. The board's C-SURFACE2 row has been structurally UNEVALUABLE since the redaction landed.

Same defect class, same day, second instance: the tracked `tokenizer/tokenizer.json` was made non-loadable by the same redaction pass (see #531 comment). Class: **redaction placeholders inside FUNCTIONAL artifacts** — receipts are records (placeholder fine); code is executed (placeholder = broken default).

## Stale premise (first-principles)

The probe docstring's root note says surface-2 telemetry lives on a "physically separate EXECUTION tree" (frozen spec v1). That was a pre-consolidation convenience: since the single-tree consolidation, the contract repo IS the execution home, and the old execution tree holds no `receipts/ember-surface2-telemetry/` dir at all (verified on disk this session). The separate-tree premise is dead; the redaction placeholder just exposed it.

## Frozen AC

1. Root resolution becomes: `EMBER_EXEC_ROOT` env override (retained) → else **the contract repo root itself** (same resolution the sibling probes use). The placeholder literal is deleted. No new env vars, no config files.
2. Expected board transition: UNEVALUABLE → **RED** (`receipts/ember-surface2-telemetry/` absent in-tree = real, looked-at absence per frozen spec clause (a)). RED is the cure working. Do NOT create the telemetry dir, do NOT seed fixtures, do NOT weaken clauses (a)-(c) — faking aliveness is the failure state this probe exists to catch.
3. Docstring root-note updated to record the consolidation + this issue as the deviation record for the spec-v1 "verbatim" root note (one paragraph, no history rewrite).
4. Regression list: probe still always exits 0, one line; UNEVALUABLE remains only for a genuinely unresolvable root; synthetic-rejection (`_synthetic_control_fixture` / `synthetic_event`), verb-schema clause (b), and `metrics_delta` clause (c) byte-untouched.
5. Unit check: run the probe once post-fix from a clean env and paste its one-line output (expected RED receipt-absent) in the PR body.

## Rails

CPU-only; never `--live`; touch ONLY `scripts/ember_totality/test_surface2.py`; PR stop-at-open, refs-only body (never closes/fixes keywords).

## Class extraction (for the redaction utility, tracked on the landmine thread)

The redaction/landing utility must hard-fail (block the landing) when a replacement target sits inside a string literal of a tracked `*.py`/`*.ts` file, instead of silently landing a placeholder. That half rides #502/#525 — one comment there references this instance.

## Empirical result (boardrun46, receipt `ember-totality-20260710T000016Z`)

C-BASE rendered RED — "no owned from-scratch checkpoint receipt ... names a checkpoint whose on-disk [bytes verify]" — in the same window where PR #607 landed a receipt citing a hash-verified on-disk checkpoint (`models/cbase-smoke-run/checkpoints/step-00000610`). This settles the open question flagged in the #607 merge gate: **board renders executed from worktrees cannot see the checkpoint bytes**, because `models/` is gitignored and exists only in the operating tree. The receipt is honest; the probe's root resolution is the defect.

## Class

Probe-root mechanics, not receipt content. Any C-condition whose CHK verifies on-disk artifacts outside tracked content (model weights, checkpoints, large caches) is silently coupled to WHERE the board runs. Today that means: a main-tree render can flip C-BASE GREEN, a worktree render flips it RED, with zero disclosure of the difference — a nondeterministic condition color keyed to runner location is a self-deception surface.

## Fix (frozen; builder implements exactly this)

1. `test_c_base.py` (and an audit sweep over other probes with on-disk-artifact clauses) resolves artifact paths against an explicit `EMBER_ARTIFACT_ROOT` env var when set, else falls back to the probe's repo root (current behavior).
2. The board runner (`ember_totality_spec.py`) sets `EMBER_ARTIFACT_ROOT` to the OPERATING tree root when invoked from a worktree render — passed explicitly by the render lane, never guessed. When unset and the artifact is absent, the probe's RED reason must SAY "artifact root not provided / bytes not visible from this tree" rather than "no receipt names a checkpoint" — a visibility failure and an absence failure are different verdicts.
3. The rendered row for any condition that consulted `EMBER_ARTIFACT_ROOT` carries a `artifact_root_source` field (`env` | `repo-root`) so a GREEN earned via env-root is auditable.
4. Regression: two executed runs of the C-BASE probe on the same receipt set — one with the artifact root visible (expect GREEN), one without (expect RED with the visibility reason) — both pasted in the PR body.

## Sweep scope

`git grep -l "models/" scripts/ember_totality/test_*.py` at implementation time; every probe that dereferences untracked artifact bytes gets the same treatment in the same PR or a filed sibling issue per probe.

## Frozen spec: C-OBS operator surface — REPL rendering overhaul + ambient watch mode

### Defects found (operator-visible, all reproduced)

1. `monitor` dumped each board condition's FULL forensic verdict paragraph raw (some rows ~500 words) — no hierarchy, no color, no sort. Unusable as an observatory.
2. Header printed `pct_complete=0` beside 23 GREEN rows — field-read bug: adapter read `summary.pct_complete`, real value lives at `summary.completion_math.pct_complete`.
3. The REPL never called `rl.prompt()` — zero input cue after boot; surface looks hung.
4. Banner lines hard-wrapped mid-word at terminal width (`<of ferId>`, `proof-p ack`).
5. `commands/world-state.ts` (not-yet-live slash surface) duplicated defects 1-2.

### Contract (landed on the local workbench; lands here as a PR once seed branches merge)

- Pure renderer module `core/monitor-render.ts`: 2-line header (board ts, N/30 GREEN + true pct, incident count), one aligned line per condition `[idx] [G|R|A] NAME reason-first-sentence…` (sentence-aware truncate ≤110 chars), not-green rows sorted FIRST, ANSI color with NO_COLOR/non-TTY plain fallback; full forensics stay behind `evidence <surface> <n>`, index-consistent with the sorted view via one shared `sortMonitorConditions`.
- Prompt: `ember> ` (cyan/TTY, plain otherwise) after boot and after every command, never after `quit`.
- ANSI-safe word-boundary wrap routed through a single print choke point (escape codes never split, colors reset+reopen across breaks, multi-space column padding preserved).
- Compact 4-line banner; membrane/proof-pack prose relocated behind `understand` (verbatim, not deleted).
- `--watch [--interval N]` mode: non-interactive auto-refresh observatory — fresh state re-read per cycle, same board renderer, newest-3-receipts tail with ages, refresh-error resilience (never crashes the window), clean SIGINT exit.
- Both surfaces (REPL + slash command) consume the same renderer module.

### Acceptance criteria (all verified)

- Full ember-cli suite green with zero regressions; every contract item above carries dedicated unit tests (baseline 2340 pass → 2399 pass / 0 fail at item-5 completion; watch-mode tests additional on top).
- Piped end-to-end run against real contract-tree data: compact board with correct pct, prompt count = boot + 1/command, `evidence monitor 0` resolves the same row the sorted list displays.
- Subprocess-spawned E2E tests (the REPL calls `process.exit`; in-process module mocking corrupts the shared registry — spawned-fixture pattern is the mandated test shape for this surface).

## Frozen contingency spec — 8l mechanism-redesign ladder (result-blind, pre-registered BEFORE A20's verdict)

**Why now, before A20 lands:** issue #36 rung 2 (A19's shape reproduced at 1.7× params) REFUTES the capacity hypothesis and BANS further C14 GPU windows until a mechanism-redesign spec "8l" is frozen. Writing 8l after seeing the result invites post-hoc rationalization; this spec is authored while A20 is mid-flight and blind to its outcome. **Execution precondition: A20 verdict = rung 2.** If A20 lands rung 1 (held-out ≥1/3 anywhere), this issue CLOSES UNEXECUTED with a comment recording that capacity was the binding constraint — that closure is itself evidence.

**Frame (from the A15–A19 synthesis + 0/16 seed invariance):** the protocol reliably builds a train-set lookup and never transfers. If 1.7× capacity doesn't move held-out, the remaining suspect class is the MECHANISM: where the adaptation lives (locus), what the objective rewards (outcome-only), and how the rule is presented (exemplar-conditioned). One arm per suspect, single variable each, all against the SAME substrate A20 used.

### Arm L1 — adapter locus (head-only → interior)
LoRA currently attaches ONLY at the head linear: the trained delta can at best re-map output logits of representations the frozen base already computes — a lookup-shaped inductive bias. L1 moves the same rank budget to interior FF projections (mid-depth layers, up+down proj), head untouched. CPU toy validation first (same TinyPolicyTransformer path as the seed study, 3 seeds); one GPU window only if the toy shape differs from head-only. Kill: toy held-out still 0/3 across all 3 seeds AND train acquisition unchanged → locus alone is not the lever.

### Arm L2 — objective (outcome reward → train-internal transfer pressure)
iGRPO rewards single-state outcomes; nothing prices generalization. L2 adds a train-internal transfer term: per batch, reward is granted only when the SAME adapter state answers correctly on a train state whose exemplar context omits that state (train states only — held-out remains untouched and unseen, the firewall is unchanged). Pre-registered risk: reward sparsity collapse; mitigation = anneal the transfer-term weight 0→λ over the first 256 steps. Kill: degenerate-resample trips >3× A19's rate OR train acquisition never reaches the seed-band floor (2/5 by step 320).

### Arm L3 — presentation (exemplar-conditioned → internalized)
k=3 exemplars in every training presentation mean the rule is always available in-context; the adapter can pass training without ever internalizing it. L3 anneals k 3→0 across training (schedule pre-registered at fire time from the corpus generator's existing knobs, no new mechanism). Eval unchanged (held-out protocol identical). Kill: train acquisition collapses to 0/5 at k=0 and never recovers by step 768.

### Discipline
- One arm per GPU window, order L1→L2→L3 (cheapest-inference-about-mechanism first); each arm's fire requires the previous arm's receipted verdict comment here.
- Same substrate as A20 (grown step-00000766, sha 58e8e989...), same envelope v2.2 otherwise, same seed-study interpretation bands, `EMBER_GATE_AUTHORIZED=1`, `EMBER_VRAM_FRACTION=0.80`, receipts to `receipts/ember-c14-owned-run/`.
- Held-out set is NEVER touched by any arm's training or reward computation — L2's transfer term reads train states only.
- No arm combines with another until one shows held-out >0 alone (no un-registered compositions).
- 3 arms exhausted with held-out still 0 → escalate to the operator with the full negative trail; the next hypothesis class (corpus/task structure) needs operator-level scope judgment.
issue_source_snapshot.title: 8l contingency: mechanism-redesign ladder (adapter locus / objective / presentation) — fires only on A20 rung 2

issue_source_snapshot.body:
## Frame (from #36/#37 adjudication, receipts-only)

Fires 1-4 + the 5-seed CPU band establish: memorize-don't-transfer is invariant to seed, parameter count (0.18B → 1.222B), the full anti-collapse envelope (v1.7), exemplar conditioning (corpus-v2 k=3), and mid-run distribution refresh (corpus-v3 resample). Per the pre-registered ladder, GPU is BANNED for v2.2 shapes; the next fire happens only on a frozen spec that names which mechanism defect it attacks.

One under-examined fact from fire-4 sharpens the frame: the C arm plateaued at **2/5 ON TRAIN** — this is not clean memorize-vs-generalize; the objective failed to fit 3 of 5 training mappings at 1.222B over 1024 steps. Whatever is wrong is upstream of generalization.

## Attack surfaces on the table (each named by a receipt)

1. **Reward/credit pathway** — arm rows show sparse binary reward (0.0 everywhere on A); if the verifier emits pass/fail only, near-miss trajectories carry zero gradient signal. (fire-4 arm_scores)
2. **The prior the objective fights** — the UNTRAINED core emits a systematic state+2 action offset at zero reward; the objective never recruits this structure, it collides with it. (fire-4 A-arm rows)
3. **Heldout never load-bearing** — deletion_drops_count=0: nothing the training wrote was consulted on heldout inputs. (fire-4 gate_predicates)
4. **Onset dynamics** — seed-band onsets 64–320 (mean 196), static peak 1–3/5: whatever learning occurs saturates within ~300 steps and never composes. (#4 comment 8j seed study)

## Deliverable 1 (dispatched): mechanism design dossier — read-only recon

Extract from scripts/ember_c14_owned_run.py + the fire-4 receipt into a single dossier: (a) exact task semantics (state/action space, the target rule, train/heldout split construction); (b) the reward computation end-to-end (verifier → scalar → update); (c) the update path (which params, what loss, iGRPO coupling); (d) per-checkpoint evolution of WHICH train tasks passed/failed across fire-4's 16 evals (are the same 2 always passing? oscillation?); (e) what the model actually emitted on heldout tasks at final eval (the failure MODE, not just the count). No design proposals in the dossier — facts with receipt/line citations only.

## Deliverable 2 (mine, after the dossier): the frozen redesign spec

Names exactly ONE attack surface, states the mechanism change, pre-registers the outcome ladder, and defines the cheapest CPU falsifier BEFORE any GPU request. GPU stays banned until that spec exists and its CPU leg has run.

## Rails
Recon lane is read-only outside scratch; CPU-only; no probe/spec edits; receipts for every claim; api_spend_usd fields in any receipt produced.

issue_source_snapshot.body:
Compiled from docs/design/scale-architecture-frontier-20260703.md (action 2) — the regime table's conclusion: R3 (quantized-frozen majority + trained sparse slice) is the only regime satisfying "training AND inference, >27B total, on the 4090, not taking years." This issue is the first evidence leg: prove co-residence empirically, numbers not arithmetic.

## Deliverable

One receipt (`receipts/r3-feasibility/r3-feasibility-<ts>.json`) proving, in a SINGLE process on the 4090:
1. a ~27B-class base loaded 4-bit frozen (NF4/bitsandbytes-class, NOT a GGUF inference-only path — the slice must backprop),
2. a trainable LoRA-class slice attached (target ~100-300M trainable params, exact count recorded),
3. ONE verified training step on the slice (loss computed, backward, optimizer step; grad-norm > 0 recorded; frozen-base assert: zero base params with grad),
4. ONE inference pass (greedy, >=64 new tokens) WITHOUT unloading anything,
5. VRAM peak (torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated + nvidia-smi sample) under the 0.80 governor fraction with the margin assert, tokens/s for both legs, wall-clock.

## Phase A — CPU prep (dispatchable NOW, no GPU touch; the duration keystone owns the GPU until its 24h crossing)

- A1 dependency probe: bitsandbytes + peft + transformers import cleanly on this Windows box; record versions. NO CUDA calls in phase A — import/metadata checks only.
- A2 local model inventory: enumerate candidate 24-32B dense bases already on disk (paths, formats, sizes, shas). If none exists in a trainable format, name the smallest suitable candidate + download size in the phase-A report; download only after maintainer ack (disk courtesy, resumable, sha-verified).
- A3 harness script (`scripts/r3_feasibility_probe.py`): all five receipt legs implemented behind asserts that FAIL CLOSED (governor fraction read from the standard config, margin assert before and after load, frozen-base grad assert, receipt written only if every assert passed). Deterministic, one-command, `--dry-run` mode that exercises everything but the CUDA calls.
- A4 pre-registered interpretation (frozen here): PASS = all five legs green under governor -> R3 regime EMPIRICALLY OPEN on this hardware (frontier doc's conclusion stands on a receipt). FAIL-VRAM = co-residence exceeds budget -> record the exact overshoot; the cure lane is slice-size/base-size sweep, not abandonment. FAIL-DEPS = kernel/library wall on Windows -> the wall gets named precisely (op, version, error) and broken (WSL2 fallback leg, source build, or kernel substitute) — never resolved to "unsupported."

## Phase B — GPU execution (maintainer-launched, post-crossing; ONE GPU job at a time)

Maintainer runs the harness in their own background with failure-signature monitoring; the builder never launches GPU work.

## Rails (verbatim-binding on any lane taking this)

- CPU-only until phase B; zero CUDA calls before the keystone crossing.
- No edits outside scripts/ + receipts/r3-feasibility/ + a scratch subdir.
- Builder self-report is a claim; the maintainer re-runs the dry-run + reads receipts before any verdict.
- Resource governor + headroom rules apply absolutely in phase B: fraction cap, margin assert, pacing; a headroom violation kills the run — no fix-forward.
issue_source_snapshot.title: R3 feasibility receipt: 4-bit frozen 27B-class base + trainable slice, one train step + one inference pass co-resident on the 4090

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
Found during the b14 gate's editing-regression smoke (disclosed by the build lane, reproduced twice in independent windows): submitting a prompt while the model endpoint is unreachable renders a garbled frame — an overlapping duplicate welcome panel plus a raw object dump shaped like `{ tryGenerate: too_few_turns ... count: 0 }` bleeding into the terminal.

This is user-reachable, not just a test-harness artifact: an owned-server crash or port conflict puts a real session in exactly this state. The CLI's bar for error states is the same as for happy paths — a designed error surface, never raw internals.

## Scope
- Root-cause the render path when generate fails at the transport level (connection refused) vs the in-band `too_few_turns` guard — the dump suggests the guard object is being rendered as transcript content.
- Error surface: one clean, styled error line/block in the transcript (family: existing status-bar styling), no duplicate panel, no raw objects.
- Regression tests: (1) transport-refused submit renders the styled error and NOTHING else new; (2) welcome panel never re-renders as a duplicate on any error path.
- Rails: rendering-layer only; no changes to generate/transport logic beyond what error propagation requires; suite green; real-window re-proof under the same unreachable-URL condition.
issue_source_snapshot.title: ember-cli: unreachable-model submit renders garbled frame (duplicate welcome panel + raw tryGenerate dump)

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
Side finding from the #49 investigation (disclosed by the build lane while fixing the error-surface garble; not fixed there because it is a correctness bug, not a rendering one).

`executePromptSuggestion`'s call site passes the REPL's `SessionMessage`-shaped messages (`{id, type, content}`) into `tryGenerateSuggestion`, whose guard chain filters by `.role` — a field `SessionMessage` does not carry. The "too_few_turns" guard therefore always counts 0 assistant messages and always fires, so the prompt-suggestion feature most likely never generates in production, at any conversation length. Post-b15 this failure is silent (its console noise was routed to a no-op sink as part of the #49 console-hygiene fix), which makes it easy to forget — hence this ticket.

## Scope
- Confirm the shape mismatch with a failing test that feeds real `SessionMessage[]` through the public path and asserts the guard's turn-count sees the actual assistant turns.
- Cure at the boundary: one adapter (or a shared message-shape type) so the suggestion module receives the shape it filters on; do not fork a second message type.
- Regression tests: (1) N>=threshold assistant turns → guard passes and a suggestion attempt is made; (2) the five existing guard branches still behave per their current tests.
- Rails: suggestion module + its call site only; no rendering changes; suite green; disclose in the proof pack whether the feature was EVER live (check the guard logic against git history of the shapes).
issue_source_snapshot.title: ember-cli: prompt-suggestion guard filters by .role on SessionMessage-shaped input — feature likely silently dead

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
Recon finding (verified by maintainer at both cited paths): ember-cli's model display identity is a fiction. `src/model-config.ts:6` hardcodes `LOCAL_MODEL_ID = 'qwen-3.6'`, and prose elsewhere extends it to "qwen3.6-27b" — but the managed server behind that label is ember's OWN from-scratch C-BASE checkpoint (`configs/v0-pretrain-config.json` → /model/params_estimate = 368,354,304; largest local artifact is the grown rung1 checkpoint at a receipted 1,221,633,024 params). No Qwen-family weights of any size exist on this machine.

This is an honesty-surface defect of exactly the class ember exists to get right: the label misled the OPERATOR into believing a 27B QAT+MTP Qwen was running locally, and that belief nearly misdirected a base-model decision for the R3 feasibility probe. A cockpit that displays a false model identity fails the same bar as a probe that self-attests.

## Scope
- Replace the `qwen-3.6` display identity with the truthful one, derived from the SERVED artifact, not hardcoded: family name (ember C-BASE / C-GROW), receipted param count, checkpoint step, and QAT/MTP flags read from the serving config or manifest.
- The canonicalize/`isLocalModel` logic keeps working (the label is load-bearing for routing — migrate, don't just rename).
- Sweep ALL surfaces that echo the fiction: welcome panel, status bar, any docs/GOAL.md prose citing "qwen3.6-27b" as a local turn (fix the prose to name the owned model).
- Regression: a test asserting the displayed model identity matches the serving manifest's family+params (no hardcoded third-party names for owned artifacts).
- Rails: rendering + config only; no serving-stack changes; suite green; real-window re-proof showing the truthful identity line.
issue_source_snapshot.title: ember-cli: model identity displays 'qwen-3.6' while serving ember's own C-BASE checkpoint — truthful identity from serving manifest

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
Follow-on from #50 (disclosed by the build lane during the adapter cure, correctly held out of its rendering-only scope).

The REPL's transcript entries (`SessionMessage`) only ever get `id/type/content` populated at creation. The prompt-suggestion guard chain also reads `stop_reason` (guard: last-assistant-is-error) and `usage` (guard: cache-budget) — with the #50 adapter in place those fields pass through as undefined, so both guards run permanently in "no data" mode: they can never trigger, which silently disables two of the five suppression conditions.

## Scope
- Thread the engine's `ModelResponse` metadata (`stop_reason`, `usage`) onto the assistant transcript entry at the point the result event is applied (the #49 `applyResultEvent` seam is the natural place — the error subtype already carries `errorMessage` through it).
- Failing tests first: (1) an assistant turn created from a completed generation carries its stop_reason/usage; (2) guard 3 actually suppresses after an error-terminated assistant turn; (3) guard 4 actually suppresses when cumulative usage exceeds the budget threshold.
- Rails: metadata threading only — no new rendering, no guard-logic changes, no engine control-flow changes; suite green; disclose in the pack whether usage accumulation semantics match what guard 4's threshold expects (per-turn vs cumulative — read the guard, don't guess).
issue_source_snapshot.title: ember-cli: transcript entries never carry stop_reason/usage — suggestion guards 3+4 permanently data-starved

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
Frozen runbook spec for today's post-crossing GPU window. The window must convert the C11 24h crossing into up to three condition-bearing receipt sets without a mis-launch burning GPU hours; the launch knowledge currently lives as prose across #48, #47, and the paired protocol — this issue freezes it as ONE numbered, pre-flighted sequence. Maintainer executes every launch; the builder lane's job is the READ-ONLY pre-flight of each step against the live tree (the fixture-vs-live coverage rule: fixtures prove mechanisms, only the live target proves coverage).

## Sequence (strict order, one GPU job at a time)

**S0 — window entry gate.** C11 runner's own state shows cumulative >= 24h; runner is left RUNNING (it never pauses). Predicates: state JSON cumulative field >= 86400 (exact field name verified by pre-flight); `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process` shows exactly one C11 runner. Abort criterion: crossing not reached → window does not open.

**S1 — C11 board flip.** Run the frozen C11 probe against the crossing receipts; verdict read from the receipt's verdict line in a SEPARATE call (probes exit 0 on RED). Flip-pair PENDING_AUTHORIZATION.json, board re-run, tally receipt. Predicates: probe verdict line == GREEN-equivalent; tally count increments by exactly 1.

**S2 — E2B GATE-1 (attach recon on the real weights).** Per protocol v1.1 clause 1's named prerequisite: LoRA attach at the E2B head linear + one zero-lr backward on the REAL local E2B module graph (9.6GB weights), non-mutating wrapper, gradient-isolation assert. Cheap, fail-fast, gates GATE-2. Predicates: attach succeeds; exactly the wrapper's params trainable; zero-lr step leaves param hash unchanged; VRAM margin assert per governor (fraction 0.8) before AND after load. Abort: any assert → window continues to S4 (R3), E2B escalates with the wall named.

**S3 — E2B GATE-2 (the one real training job).** `ember_c_e2b_paired_run.py --live` per #48: 1024-step iGRPO/LoRA at the E2B head, 16 checkpoint evals, wall ceiling 12768.6s, owned arm CITED from fire-4 via the cured loader (base-identity assert per protocol v1.3), founder_likeness 3-part session BOTH arms (300s continuation windows), provenance pin, api_spend 0. Launch requirements: PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1, stdout unpiped to a receipt-adjacent log, tree-quiescence check first (`git -C B:/M/ember status --short scripts/` clean-or-owned — builder lanes have uncommitted GATE-0 edits there: pre-flight must enumerate them and confirm they are the RUN'S OWN files, not mid-edit foreign WIP), CPU builder lanes capped at 2 for the duration. Monitoring: alternation covering progress AND failure signatures (loss lines | Traceback | CUDA | OOM | assert), GPU util as liveness fallback, receipt path as completion signal. Verdict: from the assembly receipt's own falsifier fields, separate call.

**S4 — R3 phase B (only if S3 receipt landed or S2 aborted, AND the A2''' download verified).** `scripts/r3_feasibility_probe.py --model B:/M/models/Qwen3.6-27B` (no --dry-run): NF4 load, rank-64 slice attach, frozen-base grad assert, one train step + one inference pass co-resident, VRAM/nvidia-smi legs live, receipt to receipts/r3-feasibility/. Pre-registered branches: PASS / FAIL-VRAM / FAIL-DEPS — all three are valid publishable outcomes.

**S5 — window exit.** Process-visibility receipt refresh (landings occurred); board tally re-run if any flip; kill nothing — C11 runner and :8080 server survive the window.

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
Operator report (2026-07-04, live b16): "the fire/flame animation still looks like shit. not sure why it jitters left and right."

## Defect

The flame/fireball animation exhibits frame-to-frame HORIZONTAL displacement (left-right jitter) — the flame's visual center is not stationary across animation frames. Separately from the jitter, the overall art quality is below the operator bar even when stationary.

## Root-cause hypothesis (verify before fixing)

Most likely class: **per-frame width variance + per-frame centering**. If each ASCII/glyph frame has a different intrinsic width (trailing spaces trimmed, or art drawn with different margins per frame) and the renderer centers each frame on its OWN width, the centroid shifts every frame -> horizontal jitter. Same class if the frame strings mix wide glyphs/emoji with narrow chars so measured string width != rendered cell width on some frames (string-width vs terminal-cell mismatch).

Second candidate: Ink re-layout on content change — if the flame Box's measured width changes per frame, flex centering recomputes and shifts siblings too.

## Fix spec (frozen)

1. **Diagnose first, receipts:** dump each animation frame's raw string with per-line lengths + measured string-width; verify whether widths vary across frames. One JSON receipt with per-frame {frame_index, max_line_len, string_width} — the defect is proven when these numbers vary.
2. **Fix = fixed-canvas invariant:** every frame is padded/composed onto an IDENTICAL WxH canvas (fixed columns, fixed rows) at art-authoring time or load time; centering happens ONCE on the canvas, never per frame. The canvas width accounts for terminal cell width (use the same string-width lib the rest of the CLI uses; no raw .length on glyph art).
3. **Regression test:** unit test asserting all loaded flame frames have identical rendered dimensions (fails on any future art edit that breaks the invariant).
4. **Art quality (the "looks like shit" half):** stationary is the floor, not the bar. After the canvas fix, re-judge the art against the field-ux-map sec8b bar + the operator's fireball spec (the living-mark directive) — this half stays open under the #44 design-overhaul lane and its mockup-first flow; do NOT close this issue on jitter alone. Split art rework into the #44 lane if it exceeds a surgical fix.

## Acceptance
- Per-frame dimension receipt (pre-fix showing variance, post-fix showing identical dims).
- Unit test in the suite (suite line re-run AFTER final source edit, immediately before binary hash — standing pack requirement).
- Live capture: 3 full-frame captures >=2s apart at the operator's real viewport size (currently 1720x1440 snapped left half) showing the flame stationary (same column extents in all three).
- Pack per the b-series template; maintainer re-runs everything (receipts-only).
issue_source_snapshot.title: ember-cli: flame animation jitters horizontally (per-frame width variance suspected) + art below bar

| inference technique | what it buys at inference | training-side analog (existing or synthesizable) | field maturity of the analog (shipped / papers-only / absent) | our status (in stack / receipted / absent) | candidate experiment |

issue_source_snapshot.body:
**Incident (2026-07-04).** The CLI-owned model server (ember_owned_model_server.py, port 8090, grown checkpoint) was found orphaned: 9.7GB resident, ~0 CPU for hours, port LISTENING with zero connections, no ember-cli/ember-brain process alive anywhere. The parent CLI died without its teardown leg firing, and the server has no self-defense against that. Cost: ~20% of the box's memory held by a corpse while a real corpus job fought allocation failures (numpy _ArrayMemoryError on 2GiB allocs). Receipt-first killed per kill-discipline.

**FROZEN CURE SPEC.** (1) The owned server gains a parent-liveness tether: the spawning CLI passes its own PID at launch (--parent-pid); the server polls parent liveness every ~10s and exits cleanly (logged, receipt line) when the parent is gone. Poll-based, not handle-inheritance, so it works across the spawn boundary used today. (2) Grace window: two consecutive missed polls before exit, so CLI restarts within ~20s can reattach-or-not without a flapping server. (3) Selftests: parent-gone → server exits within the window; parent alive → no exit; --parent-pid absent → server refuses to start in owned mode (fail-closed; a standalone/manual mode may exist behind an explicit flag with its own teardown documented). (4) The CLI's existing teardown leg stays — the tether is the backstop for unclean death, not a replacement.

**Sequencing.** Belongs to the ember-cli lane's current R0 work (the same process-entry code owns spawn/teardown).

The system's point is that the ember agent eventually runs its own goals, loops, and error-correction. To date this has never happened: no prompt has ever been issued to the agent through its own surface by the maintainer. That silence is the gap.

## Spec

1. **Interaction surface**: the live ember-cli window (the visible cockpit) — never a hidden headless bypass. Input via the focus-safe console mechanism; replies read from the same surface.
2. **Operator session receipts**: every session logs prompt/reply/next-action to receipts/operator-sessions/<UTC>.jsonl — the same process-visibility bar the repo enforces elsewhere. C-SURFACE2/C-OBS inherit these as live-provenance evidence.
3. **Goal injection first**: session 1 sets the agent's goal frame through its own surface (the equivalent of the goal-mode injection that governs the maintainer session) and responds to what returns.
4. **Cadence**: every work-loop window includes an operate-the-agent leg (prompt → observe → correct), mirroring the human→maintainer cadence one level down.
5. **Autonomy ladder coupling**: operator-session receipts become the R-rung evidence stream (issues #104/#109) — rungs claim when the agent needs FEWER operator interventions per window, measured from these receipts.
6. **Prerequisites prioritized because they gate this**: brain-server supervision (#122) and surface ports (#119).

## Acceptance

First operator-session receipt exists (prompt visibly issued in the cockpit, reply captured, next-action recorded); the operate-leg appears in the standing loop; ladder coupling documented in the R0 machinery.

The directed research tracks (inference-to-training optimization transfer, iGRPO/RLM, BitNet, and the contract components) were not relayed as try-and-abandon hypotheses. The bar is: make them WORK at a field-level contributing / breakthrough standard. A negative early result or absent prior art is the START of the work. Self-resolved kill verdicts are retired: a kill requires operator word; the only legal self-verdict is PARKED-pending-wall-break with a named next mechanism move.

## Audit result (full table: maintainer state, research-kill-audit-20260705)

27 rows: 4 KILLED-self-resolved, 4 RE-STAGED, 5 ACTIVE, 4 WATCHING, 6 COMPLETED-positive, 0 operator-word kills.

## The inversion this queue encodes

Two tracks were skipped BECAUSE no prior art exists: FP8 pretraining on consumer 4090-class cards ("zero published 4090 FP8 pretrains") and encoder-free multimodal at sub-1B ("zero published prior art"). Absence of prior art was scored as risk; under the field-contribution bar it is the prize — those gaps are exactly where a breakthrough-class receipt is possible.

## Re-open queue (GPU work, CPU-decontam runs concurrently — no serialization conflict)

1. **MTP auxiliary at ≤1B, local receipt** — killed on one published negative (≤1B). Wall-break: matched-budget MTP-vs-baseline on the owned core; our stack (owned core + Muon + QAT) is not the paper's stack. Contract component 5.
2. **BitNet 100-300M ternary pilot** — re-staged to ≥3B on a crossover claim never measured locally. Wall-break: measure the quality gap at v0 scale ourselves; the crossover number is someone else's curve.
3. **FP8 consumer-card training stack** — the field gap itself. Wall-break: width-conditional fp8 routing (own receipt already shows 1.15x on K1024→N4096) + attack the torchao/TE fallback layer; a working 4090 FP8 pretrain recipe is publishable on its own.
4. **SubQ/GDN-hybrid 340M pilot** — re-staged on an attended-token-floor argument at v0 context. Wall-break: run the pilot; it also carries the sleep-consolidation substrate (component 6).
5. **Fused-Muon NS chain** — killed by a Triton/MSVC environment bug, not by the algorithm. Wall-break: env fix + retry (cheapest re-open in the queue).
6. **iGRPO/RLM leg** — WATCHING → schedule the first structured pilot rather than waiting on external evidence.

## Ordering + receipts

Post-restart: fire in the order above (cheapest wall first where GPU contention forces a choice: 5 → 2 → 1 → 4 → 3 → 6). Every leg pre-registers its outcome implications before launch; every verdict is a receipt; no leg may end in a kill verdict — terminal states are WORKING, PARKED-pending-named-wall-break, or operator-word.

## Frame (operator thread, 2026-07-05 — previously deferred WITHOUT a trigger, which GOAL.md's own disposition rules call invalid)

The current split — pytorch for training, llama.cpp for inference — was adopted as convenience, then deferred as 'native engine later' with no trigger, pilot, or kill/promote condition. This issue converts that silent deferral into machinery.

## Why the split is load-bearing pain, not neutral plumbing

1. **Perpetual parity tax**: two graphs of one model; the export→quantize→parity chain is standing maintenance and a standing defect surface.
2. **It architecturally blocks a directed research track**: inference-optimization→training-optimization transfer dies at the engine boundary. Receipts already exist: FP8 was skipped citing 'TE silent-BF16-fallback; torchao tensorwise-only on sm89' — that is pytorch's abstraction refusing an optimization the hardware supports. The wall named in the kill phrase IS the framework layer.
3. **The resident-training gate's end state needs training INSIDE the serving process** (fast-weight/sleep-consolidation updates while resident). llama.cpp has no backward pass; pytorch cannot serve at footprint. Neither engine alone can ever satisfy it.
4. **Self-growth target**: a system that grows itself cannot ship a frozen vendor training stack; the training loop must be part of the owned artifact.

## Trigger ladder (machine-checkable; any firing FORCES the corresponding rung)

- **T1 (parity tax)**: a pytorch↔gguf parity defect blocks a board condition twice, or the export/parity chain exceeds a measured hours/window budget → forces rung 2.
- **T2 (framework wall on a directed track)**: a #155 leg is blocked or degraded by the framework layer itself (receipt citing framework fallback/refusal, hardware capability proven separately) → forces rung 0 for that kernel. **Status: PARTIALLY FIRED (FP8 receipts above).**
- **T3 (resident training)**: the resident-training gate requires weight updates inside the serving process → forces rung 1. **Status: on the current blocker path by design.**
- **T4 (ship the trainer)**: any C-SCALE/product surface requires training capability inside the shipped artifact → forces rung 3.

## Rung ladder (walls broken smallest-first; never a big-bang rewrite)

- **Rung 0 — owned CUDA kernel seam**: custom kernels callable from BOTH engines (pytorch extension + llama.cpp hook). First kernels = the #155 legs that are already re-opened: width-conditional FP8 matmul (own receipt shows 1.15x on K1024→N4096) and the fused-Muon NS chain. The research re-open queue and the engine thread are the same work at rung 0.
- **Rung 1 — owned resident training step**: minimal C++/CUDA forward+backward+optimizer for the fast-weight/adapter subset (GDN/LoRA-class, not full autograd), embeddable in the serving process. Feeds the resident-training gate directly.
- **Rung 2 — unified weight substrate**: one mmap-able layout both engines read (turboquant export becomes the canonical format, not a conversion).
- **Rung 3 — full native engine**: full owned autograd+kernels; taken only on T4 or operator word.

## Acceptance for this issue

Trigger table adopted into the floor-contract ledger as a row with disposition preserved_trigger_gated + this trigger set (curing the invalid trigger-less deferral); rung-0 kernel-seam spec written and coupled to the #155 FP8/fused-Muon legs; T2/T3 status reviewed at every board audit.

## Bar (operator verdict, 2026-07-05)

The internal predecessor CLI ran with ZERO CLI-side crashes — hardened and battle-tested. Today's operator session showed ember-cli is not at that bar: boot crash on unresolvable backend path (ENOENT, no operator-facing error surface — #122), silent agent-loop stall with no final message (#157), Glob tool constructor crash (#156), and a version-skew launch from a stale tree. Four distinct failure surfaces in one session.

## Required harness (CI-run, receipts per case)

1. **Boot matrix**: missing models.json / bad binary path / bad model path / port in use / backend already running — every cell must produce a clean operator-facing error and exit (or recover), never an uncaught exception.
2. **Tool-failure injection**: every registered tool forced to throw — agent loop must always emit a final assistant message (ties to #157's regression test).
3. **Backend lifecycle**: llama-server killed mid-session — CLI surfaces the loss, offers/attempts supervised restart (#122), never hangs.
4. **Terminal abuse**: live resize storm, tiny viewports, rapid input during generation — no crash, no layout corruption (extends #114's axes).
5. **Version pin**: launcher asserts the running tree is the canonical master sha and shows the sha in the UI (prevents today's two-versions incident class).

## Acceptance

Harness in CI; all cells green with receipts; a crash reproduced by any cell is a release blocker. The predecessor's zero-crash record is the floor, not the target.

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
## Trigger (receipts)

The #115-fixed run terminated honestly with a research finding: **0 of 192 candidate windows clean** under the v1 convention (any single 13-gram match anywhere in the ~7B-token training corpus excludes the candidate). Receipt: run-20260705T225127Z.err, 6 rounds, 494 heartbeats. v1 is a false-positive machine by construction: a 2048-token candidate contains ~2036 13-grams; against billions of tokens of same-distribution natural text, common-idiom collisions are near-certain (birthday arithmetic), so v1 measures corpus size, not leakage.

## Frame

The bar's purpose is that held-out windows measure GENERALIZATION, not memorization. The correct quantity is how much of a candidate is RECONSTRUCTIBLE from training text — sustained overlap — not whether one idiom collides. (Plagiarism analogy: one shared idiom is not plagiarism; a sustained matching passage is.)

## Field grounding

- GPT-3 (Brown et al. 2020, App. C): 13-gram overlap used for dedup/cleaning with document-level treatment, not single-window exclusion.
- PaLM (Chowdhery et al. 2022): contamination = high FRACTION of 8-grams seen in training (70% threshold).
- Llama-2 (Touvron et al. 2023): token-level contamination via matched n-gram fraction thresholds (skip evals >80%).
- GPT-4 tech report: sampled 50-char exact substrings, 3 per example.
Common shape everywhere: FRACTIONAL/sustained overlap with thresholds — never any-single-n-gram.

## Pre-registered convention v2 (BEFORE the next batch run; falsifiable)

A candidate window is CONTAMINATED iff:
(a) it shares a CONTIGUOUS matching run of >= 50 tokens with any training shard (near-duplicate passage = true leakage), OR
(b) > 10% of its 13-gram windows match training text (sustained diffuse overlap).

Both statistics are computed and PUBLISHED for every candidate in the batch receipt (not just the verdict) — the distribution is part of the artifact.

Decision rule, pre-registered against threshold-sliding: if >= 16 candidates pass v2 at these exact values, the batch assembles — thresholds are NOT tuned to the sample. If ZERO candidates pass even v2, that is a design-level finding: publish the distribution and re-derive with the empirical null DISCLOSED (a new pre-registration, never a silent slide).

Dependency: the collision-statistics receipt over the 192 v1-checked candidates (in flight, also discharges #185's leg 1) lands FIRST and is linked here — if it shows the candidate pool itself is degenerate (boilerplate-dominated), pool re-draw happens before v2 is applied, and that is disclosed too.

## Acceptance

1. Scanner change implements (a)+(b) with unit tests: synthetic candidate with a 50-token planted run -> CONTAMINATED via (a); candidate with 5% scattered idiom hits -> CLEAN; 15% scattered -> CONTAMINATED via (b); equivalence suite still 3/3 on the v1 code path (kept behind a flag for comparability).
2. Batch run under v2 emits per-candidate stats in the receipt; terminal states remain complete-or-exhaust-honestly (#183 semantics preserved).
3. The W-arm chain (#121 onward) re-anchors on the v2 batch receipt.

Blocks #121. Feeds from #185 stats. Authored per the #155-class standing verdict: a wall gets re-derived, not abandoned.
issue_source_snapshot.title: W2 decontam convention v2: replace any-single-13-gram-match exclusion with field-standard fractional + contiguous-run thresholds (pre-registered)

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
Found via the #185 collision-stats investigation (receipt collision-stats-issue185-20260706T014050Z.json + match dump v0-00025-matches-20260706T014050Z.json, goalforge scratch): every matched 13-gram window recurs ~117x on average inside v0-00025.bin; 8.7M raw position hits from 192 tail-region candidates against this ONE shard while 25/26 shards show zero. This is a duplication pathology in the shard's content, and it sits in the TRAINING corpus — repeated text at 100x+ biases training loss toward memorizing that content, independent of any held-out concern.

Acceptance (investigation first, cure second):
1. Characterize: decode a sample of the dumped match positions — WHAT is the repeated text (document class, source, natural repetition vs pipeline duplication bug)? Was v0-00025 built differently (check the shard-build manifest/lineage)?
2. Quantify: shard-level self-duplication rate for ALL 26 shards (rolling-hash self-collision per shard) — is 00025 unique or just worst?
3. Ruling + cure path recorded: dedup/rebuild the shard, drop it, or accept-with-disclosure (training-side effects estimated either way). Any corpus mutation is its own pre-registered change — W1 control comparability must be addressed explicitly.

Blocks nothing immediately (decontam re-draw #193 routes around it); flags a data-quality debt the W-arms inherit.
issue_source_snapshot.title: Corpus hygiene: v0-00025.bin carries massively repeated content (~117x mean 13-gram recurrence) — training-data quality concern independent of decontam

# Research-core priority inversion — corrective record (2026-07-06)

The finding: the maintainer's own local-FM ceiling answer (~1-1.5B dense) was pure
standard-stack arithmetic (Chinchilla, dense transformer, standard optimizer states). A ceiling
answer containing zero program-native terms is proof that the research core — the field-level
breakthroughs that would make local foundation-model creation possible — had been effectively
avoided, simulated, or abandoned while machinery work consumed the windows.

The indictment is CORRECT and the receipts are the maintainer's own:
1. The ceiling derivation contained ZERO ember-native terms — no lever from this program moved
   any of the three binders (data, training-state memory, compute). A live research program
   would have answered "X under standard assumptions, but lever Y attacks binder Z, receipts W."
2. GPU at 0% utilization with 11.2GB parked (resident serving, training-idle) while machinery
   work (decontam harness, CLI surfaces, PR hygiene) consumed the recent windows. GPU-idle is
   the named smell (research-kills memo, 2026-07-05).
3. The research-lever tracks (inference-to-training transfer, igrpo/rlm, bitnet-class) were
   self-killed 2026-07-05 and already ruled illegitimate ("tested then killed" self-verdicts =
   #19-class scope collapse on the core). The kills were the avoidance.
4. The W-arm chain — the program's actual falsifiable research (W1 measured-watts control #121,
   G-arm growth #113, token-bill-collapse claim ladder) — has produced zero terminal receipts;
   its prerequisites (decontam) consumed days.

CORRECTIVE (dispatched this turn, mechanisms not promises):
- #205 unblock: independent test-runner lane on the pool-placement cure (critical path to the
  decontam receipt that gates BOTH #121 and #113's GPU leg).
- #113 G-arm runner CPU dry-run: builder lane dispatched against the frozen spec (buildable
  before any GPU window — was sitting unbuilt with no blocker).
- #121 fires in the next maintainer GPU window the moment the decontam receipt exists — it is
  pre-registered, claim-laddered (L0-L3, ratio <=0.5 generalizes / >=1.0 revokes), and carries
  the program's first measured-watts receipt. Nothing else rides the GPU before it.
- Work-loop priority edit: research-core receipts (W/G/R arms, energy-law points) outrank
  machinery/surface work in every tick's dispatch order; a tick that dispatches machinery while
  an arm-leg is dispatchable must state why in the tick output.
- Killed-track revival: the 2026-07-05 kill ruling stands — revival specs for the killed levers
  queue AFTER W1/G-arm terminals (one falsifiable leg at a time, not a fan of half-run tracks).

The ceiling question gets re-answered from receipts when arms produce them: until an ember
lever moves a binder with a terminal receipt, the honest public answer to "what can ember build
locally" REMAINS the standard-stack number. That discomfort is the point of the program.

# BOTTLENECK LEDGER — single-4090 full local FM creation (dispatch authority)

**Commission (operator, 2026-07-06, third documented push of the same mandate):** the energy law
was commissioned to ENCAPSULATE the bottlenecks that make full local foundation-model creation
impossible on one consumer GPU. Breaking them — field-level, receipts — IS the program. A 2B
standard-stack model is not a foundation model; any capability answer containing only
standard-stack terms (Chinchilla, dense states, 6ND) is the program's failure state.

This ledger is the STANDING DISPATCH AUTHORITY: every work-loop tick dispatches against the
highest-priority OPEN row here before any machinery/surface work. Rows close only on terminal
receipts or operator word. Kill history is part of each row — a row that was killed without
operator word is marked ILLEGITIMATE-KILL and stands revived.

---

## B1. DATA WALL — ~7B usable local tokens vs 20N Chinchilla demand
- Standard-stack wall: honest Chinchilla ceiling ~350M params; 4-epoch stretch ~1.4B. 10x corpus
  is collection labor, not a breakthrough — and still caps ~4B.
- Breakthrough class required: training signal that does not price as fresh tokens — growth
  curricula reusing small-model compute, self-generated verified experience (clean-room: NO
  teacher distillation), data-efficiency bends (MTP counts partially).
- Program lever: **P2 growth law / G-arm — LIVE and pre-registered.** #121 W1 control vs #113
  G-arm: token_bill_collapse_ratio <=0.5 GENERALIZES (the bend receipt), >=1.0 REVOKES. This is
  the program's one currently-live bend claim. Energy-law term: T_dense projection vs measured
  grown-arm tokens.
- Kill history: none. State (2026-07-07): W1 control TERMINAL — from-scratch control matched the
  grown lineage's target at 819,200 tokens vs the 12.55M-token lineage bill (fp32-confirmed;
  receipts on #355); W1b marginal discriminator TERMINAL — the unwidened seed already evals at
  the bf16 target with ZERO continuation tokens (ratio_marginal 0.0; fp32 margin -0.036 nats for
  the grow segment's 2.56M tokens). The lever's ECONOMICS are indicted at this rung/batch/
  resolution; interpretation frozen by #355, park gate = #339 §4.1 row-1 (K>=10 fresh-batch
  paired fp32 CI = W1c, prereg #372 FROZEN). L7: no park without operator word — decision
  package pending on #355.
- Next falsifiable leg: W1c paired eval (#372) — certification in flight (index re-spec after
  #374 unsound-index rejection + zero-new-code direct-scan fallback queued); then M1/M2 CIs.

## B2. TRAINING-STATE MEMORY WALL — 24GB caps dense full-rank trainable at ~2.5-3B
- Standard-stack wall: params+grads+optimizer states ~6-16 B/param; offload collapses MFU.
- Breakthrough class required: training-state compression that HOLDS at pretraining (not
  finetune): low-rank gradient projection (GaLore-class = field floor to BEAT, not reproduce),
  ternary/quantized states+grads, layerwise/streaming schedules. Field-level bar: a from-scratch
  pretrain leg on THIS 4090 at a size the standard stack cannot fit, loss-matched to baseline
  at compute parity.
- Program lever: NONE LIVE. bitnet-class track KILLED 2026-07-05 by self-verdict — RULED
  ILLEGITIMATE same day (research kills require operator word). Status: REVIVED by this ledger.
- Energy-law term: c_functional per byte of training state (the law must price memory, not only
  joules — amendment to energy-law-theory drafted when first receipt exists).
- Next falsifiable leg (small, honest): 100M-param from-scratch short leg, quantized/low-rank
  states vs bf16-Muon baseline, matched tokens/steps, loss-delta pre-registered. Queued AFTER
  W1/G-arm terminals (one falsifiable leg at a time on the GPU).

## B3. COMPUTE / WALL-CLOCK WALL — ~4.6e18 governed FLOPs/day => months per Chinchilla-B
- Standard-stack wall: 30d ~ 1B Chinchilla; 90d ~ 1.9B. Kernel speedups (fused Muon 1.3459x,
  receipted) are multipliers, not bends.
- Breakthrough class required: compute REUSE — the same P2 growth bet as B1 seen from the FLOPs
  side (small-model FLOPs inherited through net2net growth; if post-grow loss trajectory tracks
  the from-scratch big model at a fraction of cumulative FLOPs, the compute bill bends), plus
  MTP's per-step signal amplification (in stack, unquantified as a bend).
- Program lever: same W1/G-arm chain — the FLOPs-side readout of the SAME terminal receipts
  (projected_dense_tokens_to_base, T_dense FLOPS projections are already in #121's contract).
- Kill history: none. Next leg: identical to B1 (one chain, two binder readouts). State
  (2026-07-07): the FLOPs-side readout inherits W1/W1b's terminals — the from-scratch control
  undercut the lineage on the token bill at this rung; B3's bend evidence now also waits on W1c
  + any W2 G-arm rung the operator directs (L7).

## B4. INFERENCE->TRAINING TRANSFER — the killed bridge
- Claim class: the resident inference stack (turboquant, QAT paths) reused to cheapen training
  legs (quantized forward in the training loop, KV-free eval legs, etc.).
- Kill history: KILLED 2026-07-05 self-verdict — RULED ILLEGITIMATE. Status: REVIVED, queued
  behind B2's first leg (shares the quantized-compute machinery).
- Next falsifiable leg: quantized-forward training probe at 50-100M, loss-match window
  pre-registered before launch.

## B5. THE QUALITY BAR — "foundation model" is capability breadth, not param count
- The operator's bar: a TRUE local FM. Param count is the wrong axis to declare victory on;
  the honest axis is capability-per-local-resource bending past what the standard stack yields
  at the same budget — which is exactly what P1 (capability-energy frontier) prices. Every
  B1-B4 receipt lands a point on that frontier; the FM claim is the frontier moving, not a size.
- Program lever: energy-law receipts (#121 carries the first measured-watts point). C8
  remains the unfakeable field-level condition this ledger serves.

---

## Standing rules bound to this ledger (subordinate to GOAL.md, the constitution — PR #212)
1. Work-loop PRIORITY ORDER dispatches against open rows here FIRST (rail landed 2026-07-06).
2. No row dies without operator word — self-kill = illegitimate, auto-revived, disclosed.
3. Every ceiling/capability answer to the operator quotes this ledger's live rows — a
   standard-stack-only answer is the failure state.
4. EARNED COMPUTE (constitution L6): GPU-hours escalate only on receipts that earn them; idle
   time is capped (default 24h) — something small must always be earning within the cap. Current
   earned order: decontam receipt -> #121 W1 -> #113 G-arm GPU leg -> B2 leg 1 -> B4 leg 1.
5. This issue is permanent — never closed by keyword, only superseded by an operator-approved
   revision.

Constitutional directive (2026-07-06 interview): ember-cli implements goal mode as a native organ — a 1:1 copy of the codex mechanism, then improved. The maintainer's source-level mechanism map (from openai/codex @ rust-v0.135.0) is the spec floor and lands as docs/goal-mode-mechanism.md in the constitution PR.

Mechanism contract (all from the source map, none optional):
1. Persisted per-thread goal in ember-cli's state store: goal_id, objective (immutable to the model — status-only transitions), status machine Active/Paused/Blocked/UsageLimited/BudgetLimited/Complete, optional token budget, system-tallied usage.
2. /goal slash command: set/view/edit objective, available mid-task; edits inject an objective-updated steering prompt.
3. Model-side tools: get_goal / create_goal (fails if exists; never inferred from ordinary tasks) / update_goal (STATUS ONLY).
4. EVENT-DRIVEN continuation: every turn/task completion pokes maybe-continue-if-idle — semaphore (no double-fire), requires no active turn AND no queued user input (user always preempts), re-reads goal from store verifying same-id+Active before firing, then injects a hidden continuation prompt as a runtime-owned context fragment and starts an ordinary turn.
5. Continuation doctrine payload (adapt the codex continuation.md in spirit, ember terms): objective-is-data injection guard; anti-scope-shrink; anti-substitution; work-from-evidence; COMPLETION AUDIT that must PROVE completion requirement-by-requirement (never fail-to-find); BLOCKED only after the same blocker repeats 3 consecutive goal turns.
6. Budget governance: at token budget → status BudgetLimited + wrap-up steer (soft landing, never silent kill; budget-exhaustion never justifies completion claims).
7. Receipts: every goal transition + continuation fire appends to the receipt store (ember receipts-only law applies to the organ itself).

Acceptance: (a) unit tests on the state machine + continuation eligibility races; (b) live compiled-binary session: set a multi-turn goal, observe >=3 autonomous continuations with zero user input, a correct completion audit refusing a premature complete, and a clean update_goal(complete) on a genuinely-met objective — receipts + frame captures; (c) user-preemption test: queued user input suppresses continuation, always.

Depends on #197 (conversation budget — merged first so long goal sessions don't wedge). This organ is what makes the operator ladder (maintainer -> ember) executable: constant autonomous working mode inside the body. Addresses the constitution's goal-mode-organ section; relates #207, #154.

issue_source_snapshot.body:
Constitutional requirement (GOAL.md P-C, PR #212): the observatory IS the flame, and the flame must be animated by the organism's REAL internal state — runs, receipts, goal-mode status, intent — never keyframes. A keyframed/decorative flame is a fabricated receipt in visual form and fails the pillar.

Contract:
1. INPUT TRUTH: every visual parameter of the flame (intensity, motion, color temperature, flicker cadence, size) binds to a named live signal: active run state (training/eval/idle), receipt arrival events, goal-mode status (#211: active/continuing/blocked/budget), GPU utilization within the governed envelope, ledger-row transitions (#207). The binding table is checked in as code + doc; an unbound visual parameter is a defect.
2. IDLE HONESTY: when the organism is idle, the flame shows idle — a small, quiet, honest ember. Faking liveliness during idle violates receipts-only (L2) in pixels.
3. EVENT LEGIBILITY: a receipt landing, a run starting, a goal continuation firing each produce a distinct visible response — an operator watching the flame can tell WHAT KIND of thing just happened without opening a panel.
4. VERIFICATION: acceptance runs the compiled binary against scripted state transitions (idle -> run-start -> receipt -> blocked -> idle) and captures frames per transition; each capture must show the bound response. Includes a live-resize probe and the operator's half-screen default viewport. Experience leg mandatory: side-by-side with the current animated flame and with the field exemplar, wince-list included in the PR.
5. The current animated flame is the named failure baseline — decorative, state-blind. It gets replaced, not patched around.

## Incident (2026-07-05T19:00 -> 07-06T15:00 local)
The visible cockpit session spent ~20h retrying chat requests against an endpoint returning HTTP 400 (a leftover fixture server from #195/#196 model-URL testing). The UI showed a red error + 'Retrying…' and then kept retrying indefinitely with no backoff cap, no circuit breaker, and no degraded-state banner. Operator experienced it as a dead/static cockpit.

## Defects
1. Retry policy: unbounded identical retries on a 4xx (client error — retrying cannot succeed). 4xx should fail fast to a visible degraded state; only 5xx/timeouts merit bounded backoff.
2. No liveness surface: the session gave no heartbeat/last-activity indicator distinguishing 'wedged' from 'idle'.

## Acceptance
- 4xx from the model server -> immediate visible DEGRADED banner (endpoint, status, one-line cause), no retry storm.
- 5xx/timeout -> exponential backoff, capped attempts, then same banner.
- Status line shows last-successful-model-roundtrip age.
Relates #196 (routing cause class) and #211 (goal-mode continuation must respect degraded state).
issue_source_snapshot.title: cockpit: HTTP 400/error retry loop has no circuit breaker — 20h invisible wedge

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
From the P3 panel synthesis (#207 comment, 2026-07-06). Rung-3 currently FAILS the 19.19 GiB governed floor on the naive ledger (weights 7.90 + full bf16 momentum 7.66 + full grad buffer 7.90 GiB before activations). Two moves cure it:

1. **Per-layer grad-fuse into momentum** (momentum is a linear accumulator; fuse micro-batch grads in backward hooks, no model-wide grad buffer — mechanism per GaLore's per-layer update, optimizer-agnostic). Grad buffer 7.90 GiB -> ~0.08 GiB transient.
2. **Momentum precision**: (a) bf16 momentum -> total ~18.2 GiB, thin fit (~1.0 GiB headroom at <=2048-token micro-batches), FULLY covered by the existing D6 bf16-momentum receipt; (b) 8-bit blockwise momentum -> ~14.6 GiB with ~4.6 GiB headroom — requires the B0 A/B receipt first (8-bit MUON momentum is unreceipted; D6 template applies).

## Acceptance
- Implementation behind a config flag on the cbase grow chain (rung pins untouched).
- Ledger receipt: max_memory_reserved at rung-3 shapes under (a), against the floor, published per-term.
- Loss-trajectory equivalence at 718M via the D6 A/B harness before any rung-3 promotion claim.
- Pre-registered: variant (a) is the promotable path today; variant (b) promotes only after B0 passes.

Relates #207, #113. Frozen spec basis: docs/spec/rung2-grow-spec-v1.md conventions apply.
issue_source_snapshot.title: rung-3 (4.24B) un-fail: per-layer grad-fuse + momentum precision — two grounded moves, no new research
