issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
## Measured trigger (EXP-B bandwidth soak, 2026-07-06)
At the same instant: `torch.cuda.mem_get_info()` reported **~17.9 GiB free** while `nvidia-smi` reported **~0.8-1.3 GiB free** (resident inference servers holding ~22.8 GiB). Windows WDDM virtualizes GPU memory, so torch's self-report includes oversubscribable memory. Receipt: EXP-B soak comment on #207 (2026-07-06). This also **explains the previously unreconciled telemetry discrepancy** in `receipts/muon-ab-retry-20260705/telemetry-discrepancy-note.md`.

## Audit of the goalforge script tree (read-only sweep, 2026-07-06)

**DANGEROUS — sizing/gating decisions that fail open:**
1. `scripts/accumulation_law/run_accumulation.py:1348-1354` — preflight computes free as `total_memory - memory_reserved(0)`, which only sees THIS process's reservations. On a box with resident servers it reports ~24 GB 'free' on a fully occupied GPU and passes its own `>6000 MiB` assertion — the message even says 'Free the resident model first', i.e. the author intended a cross-process check and implemented a within-process one. **Fail-open launch into an occupied GPU -> WDDM oversubscription -> paging pressure on the resident servers.**
2. `scripts/c04_harness.py:437-443` — `SKIPPED-MARGIN` gate reads `mem_get_info()`; with WDDM inflating 'free' by ~17 GiB the margin skip can never fire when it matters. Same fail-open class.
3. `scripts/ember_phase3_c14/avir_resident_arch_spec.py:289` — spec TEXT prescribes a `memory_allocated()`-based cap assert, encoding the unsafe pattern for future scripts.

**Benign (direction-safe or telemetry-only):**
- `run_accumulation.py:531-545 eval_vram_fraction` — self-limiting governor (caps this process's own reservation fraction); within-process view is acceptable for that direction.
- ~55 further hits across c04_*/fp19/fp3x/density/cuda_graph bench scripts log `mem_get_info`/`memory_allocated` into receipts as telemetry. No gating, but any 'free_vram' field in those receipts is a WDDM-virtualized number, not ground truth — readers must not size from them.

## Fix contract
- Every preflight/gating read of free VRAM on this box goes through an `nvidia-smi` subprocess query (`--query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total`), never torch self-report.
- `memory_allocated/reserved` remain valid ONLY for self-accounting (own-process deltas, governor fractions).
- Receipts should record BOTH numbers labeled (`free_torch_wddm`, `free_nvidia_smi`) so the discrepancy is visible instead of silent.
- First-principles audit doc (docs/research/first-principles-audit-2026-06-10.md:341) already prescribes 'max_memory_allocated + nvidia-smi peak' — this issue extends that rule from peak-reporting to preflight gating.
issue_source_snapshot.title: VRAM preflight gates fail open on WDDM: torch self-report vs nvidia-smi ground truth (~17 GiB discrepancy, measured)

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
## Finding

repo-guard's `[names]` hashed-denylist scan does not detect founder-name references inside tracked files that are not UTF-8/ASCII-decodable. A non-UTF-8 text file (e.g. UTF-16LE-with-BOM, as in #245) sails through the scan clean regardless of its actual text content.

## Evidence

`scripts/ember_totality/ember_totality_spec.py` carried a founder-name-derived codename ("kai-converge") in a comment on line 56 for its entire life on master after landing via #234. `repo-guard`'s `[names]` check reported clean (`ok [names] none found`) on every commit that touched or left that file untouched, because the scanner apparently only matches its hashed denylist against text it can decode as UTF-8/ASCII — a UTF-16LE blob's bytes (each ASCII char null-padded) never match the same string patterns.

Confirmed reproducible: attempting to commit a byte-faithful UTF-8 transcode of that same file (#246) — zero textual content change, only the encoding — immediately caused `repo-guard` to FAIL on `[names]`, catching the exact string that had been present, unchanged, and un-flagged the whole time it sat UTF-16-encoded.

## Consequence

Any tracked file committed with a UTF-16 or UTF-32 BOM is a blind spot for the `[names]` gate (and potentially other repo-guard text scans that assume UTF-8/ASCII input — worth checking `[paths]` and `[path-frags]` for the same gap). A contributor (or an automated PR pipeline) could land founder-identifying content on master indefinitely as long as it stays non-UTF-8 encoded, with repo-guard reporting green.

## Fix contract

repo-guard must not silently skip non-UTF-8 tracked text files. Two options, in order of preference:

1. **(preferred) Fail closed**: reject any commit that adds or modifies a tracked file with a UTF-16/UTF-32 BOM outright. UTF-16-encoded Python/text source is itself a defect independent of this scan gap — #245 already demonstrates it makes the file non-executable. Failing closed is simpler than option 2 and removes the underlying defect class at the same time.
2. **(fallback)** Detect a UTF-16/UTF-32 BOM on any tracked text-attributed blob, transcode to UTF-8 in memory before running the `[names]` (and other text-based) scans, so the denylist actually sees the real content.

## Related

#245 (the specific instance this blind spot let through) and #246 (the fix PR whose attempted commit is what surfaced this gap).

## Class note

Same shape as #245/the #242 live-verification board rationale: a gate reported PASS without actually being able to inspect the artifact it was supposed to gate. The scan wasn't defeated by an adversary — it never engaged in the first place.
issue_source_snapshot.title: repo-guard [names] scan is blind to non-UTF-8 (UTF-16/32 BOM) tracked files

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
## Source
Operator-directed fresh-eyes audit (2026-07-06): 7 independent first-time-visitor agents (one per top-level area + branch census) + a senior-reviewer synthesis leg, all read-only against master. Full field notes retained maintainer-side.

## Finding
The repo has a **discoverability defect, not a care defect** — and it is concentrated in exactly two directories:

| Area | Grade | Key fact |
|---|---|---|
| scripts/ | WORST | **398/502 files (79.6%) loose at root**, organized only by filename-prefix conventions (ember*, c0X_, tN_, fpXX_, wN_...); no scripts/README.md; entry points not distinguishable from one-shot experiment debris without tribal knowledge |
| receipts/ | SECOND | **473/805 files (59%) loose at root**, timestamp-organized; 17 phase subdirs exist but hold the minority; **no claim→receipt index** — finding the receipt behind a specific board condition requires grepping 800 files |
| docs/ | minor | one live version ambiguity: gpu-math-multiplier-table v1 vs v2 (same date, conflicting citation from fp19-envelope.md); no docs/research index (80+ flat dated files) |
| root | minor | kernel-v1.0.manifest unexplained to visitors; README missing forward-link to docs/spec/conditions-v1.md; 2026-06-24 consolidation reset unexplained for `git log --all` users |
| branches | minor | 2 dangling branches without PRs (fix/ci-guard-debt-91, fix/leakgate-backup-exemption) |
| tools/, small dirs | clean | 9-10/10; zero slop signals |

Classic slop signals (v1/v2/final chains, orphans, dead symlinks, 0-byte files, committed build debris): **zero across all 1,935 tracked files.**

## Why it matters (paper-reception risk)
A skeptical reviewer verifying one number ("show me the receipt for C8") has no fast path. Reviewers who cannot quickly find evidence generalize to "maybe the evidence is thin" — an inference gap fully closable by additive-only indexing.

## PRE-PAPER FLOOR (must land before the paper carries the author's name; all additive, near-zero risk)
1. **receipts/CLAIMS.md + INDEX.jsonl** — claim→receipt map (board conditions, GOAL.md C1-C4, per-issue receipts → backing receipt paths), generated by a script from the ticket/claim/verdict fields already in the receipt JSON schemas. Reviewer finds any claim's receipt in <1 min.
2. **scripts/README.md** — the prefix taxonomy + canonical entry points ("which script produced Table 2" has a one-line answer).
3. **Root README gaps ×3** — kernel-manifest purpose sentence; forward-link to conditions-v1.md from the claims-limits section; one sentence on the 2026-06-24 consolidation reset.
4. **Disambiguate gpu-math-multiplier-table v1/v2** — VERSION-ACTIVE marker or consolidation note + fix the stale citation. Do NOT delete either JSON.

## RANKED PLAN, remainder (post-floor; history-preserving `git mv` only, never delete+recreate)
5. Separate ops artifacts from evidence: relocate eng-sync-*.json (~50) + tally-* (~13) to receipts/ops-log/; update index.
6. Reorganize the 398 loose scripts into semantic subdirs per the documented taxonomy; update all import paths, receipt provenance harness_sha refs, configs/nck-invariants.json manifest, CI workflows; re-run the invariant-manifest regeneration so kernel checksums track new locations.
7. Reorganize the 473 loose receipts into the existing 17-subdir phase scheme guided by the claims index; update board runner / receipt_check.py path reads in the same change.
8. Replace the receipts/ledger/*.v1-archived overwrite pattern with an explicit append-only convention (or document the archival rule in receipts/ledger/README.md). No historical surgery.
9. Collapse the ~127 tiny generated dispatcher stubs (e.g. 22 c04_design_* permutations, 255-289 bytes each) into one data-driven runner + config table; stubs removed only after the runner reproduces identical receipts.
10. Resolve the 2 dangling branches: open PRs if live, delete if superseded (confirm authorship intent first; 76 commits ahead).

## Hard constraints on ALL items
Receipts are evidence: never rename/move without `git mv` (history + blame must survive); .gitattributes sha256 pins must stay valid or be regenerated in the same commit; no force-push; every move-class item ships with the path-reference sweep in the same PR.
issue_source_snapshot.title: Repo organization: scripts/ 79.6% and receipts/ 59% loose-at-root, no claim-to-receipt index — pre-paper floor + ranked cleanup plan

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
## Summary

The public-export scrub/redaction tool that produced this repo's public tree rewrote at least some bracketed display-redaction placeholders (e.g. `<local-path>`, `<peer-loop>`) INTO functional code contexts -- string literals consumed by `os.path.join()`, `Path()`, and argparse defaults -- rather than confining substitution to display/export-time text (log messages, docs, receipt values). This silently breaks the rewritten code: no directory is ever really named `<peer-loop>` (angle brackets aren't valid path characters), so any lookup using the placeholder as a real path segment can never match, and the tool leaves no signal that it happened.

## Evidence

- `scripts/ember_totality/test_c3.py`: `D3_LOOP_DIR = os.path.join(EXTERNAL_STATE, "receipts", "<peer-loop>")` and `RESIDENT_GATE_DIR = ... "<peer-gate>")` -- these are the SOLE resolution path for two of C3's checks, with no fallback. Real data exists under real names (`receipts/ember-d3-native-loop/`, `receipts/ember-resident-training-gate/`, both already public), so referencing them leaks nothing -- the scrub over-redacted a public referent.
- Same broken constants also present in `test_c4.py`, `test_c5.py` (bucket B), and (with partial masking by a broader fallback glob) `test_c0.py`, `test_c2.py`.
- `scripts/fp33_e1_open_base_inventory.py`'s `SCAN_ROOTS` list: 6 separate `Path("<local-path>")` entries where a comment ("Narrow B-drive roots") implies 6 originally DISTINCT real paths -- the scrub collapsed distinct values into one indistinguishable placeholder, an information-loss defect on top of the functional breakage.
- ~20 additional files under `scripts/` carry `DEFAULT_* = Path(r"<local-path>")` as an argparse default (lower severity -- fails loud with FileNotFoundError rather than silently misreporting, but still a broken convenience default in every case).

Full inventory: ember #254 (board reproducibility tracking issue) comments, "Bucket-E 18-way sub-classification" and "Placeholder sweep" sections.

## Fix contract

1. The scrub must never rewrite a string literal inside a `.py`/`.ts`/`.js`/`.sh` file without a post-scrub compile check (`py_compile` / `tsc --noEmit` as applicable) AND a probe-execution smoke check confirming the rewritten reference still resolves to something (or is confirmed dead/unreachable) -- not just that the file parses.
2. Placeholder substitution belongs at the display/export layer (what gets PRINTED or written into a receipt/doc), never inside a functional path-join, import, or subprocess argument. If a real local path must be redacted from a functional constant, the constant should be replaced with an explicit "must be configured" sentinel that fails loudly and immediately (e.g. raises `NotImplementedError`/`FileNotFoundError` with a clear message) rather than a bracketed string that silently fails a glob/isdir check.
3. Where multiple distinct real values collapse to the same placeholder token (the `fp33_e1_open_base_inventory.py` case), the scrub should number them (`<local-path-1>`, `<local-path-2>`, ...) so downstream maintainers know multiplicity was lost, rather than erasing it.

## References

- ember #254 (board reproducibility) -- REDACTION-BROKE-PATH class discovery and full placeholder sweep.
- ember #247 -- same family: public-export tooling silently corrupting/hiding real defects (repo-guard blind to non-UTF-8-encoded tracked files).
issue_source_snapshot.title: Redaction pass rewrites functional code segments (REDACTION-BROKE-PATH class)

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
## Summary

A public-export scrub replaced real local-path defaults in ~20 standalone research/utility scripts under `scripts/` (NOT `scripts/ember_totality/` -- these are manually-invoked research scripts, not board probes) with the literal placeholder string `<local-path>`, used as an argparse default (`DEFAULT_X = Path(r"<local-path>")`, later `ap.add_argument("--flag", default=str(DEFAULT_X))`). Different failure mode from the REDACTION-BROKE-PATH board-probe class (#254/#259): these fail LOUD (a normal `FileNotFoundError`-shaped error) when run without the corresponding CLI override, rather than silently misreporting a board verdict. Filing separately per triage in #254 -- board-independent, lower priority, no lane assigned yet.

## Affected files

`ember_d3_broader_multifamily_admission.py`, `ember_gate_backend_coordinator_agents.py`, `ember_gate_cleanroom_inventory.py`, `ember_gate_cleanroom_legal_boundary.py`, `ember_gate_full_parity_harness.py`, `ember_gate_function_slash_commands.py`, `ember_gate_launch_packaging.py` (x2 defaults), `ember_gate_uiux_repl_components.py`, `ember_paperbench_admission.py`, `ember_preloop_resident_gate.py` (x2), `ember_rebench_admission.py`, `ember_rebench_first_loop.py`, `ember_resident_training_candidate.py` (x2), `ember_resident_training_gate.py`, `ember_scienceagentbench_admission.py`, `ember_scienceagentbench_artifact_intake.py` (x2), `ember_scienceagentbench_artifact_materialization.py`, `ember_scienceagentbench_first_loop.py`, `ember_scienceagentbench_stronger_transfer_loop.py` (x2), `ember_scienceagentbench_zero_cost_loop.py` (x2), `ember_train_multimodal_resident_adapter.py` (x2), `nck/b_run_designation.py`, `nck/nck_e2e_proof.py`.

## Worse instance: real data loss

`scripts/fp33_e1_open_base_inventory.py`'s `SCAN_ROOTS` list has 6 separate `Path("<local-path>")` entries (a comment above them reads "Narrow B-drive roots -- full <local-path> rglob is too slow over NTFS/WSL2"), strongly implying 6 originally DISTINCT real directory paths were collapsed into one indistinguishable placeholder token. This is not just breakage -- it's unrecoverable loss of which 6 locations were originally intended.

## Fix contract

1. Each `DEFAULT_*`/`SCAN_ROOTS` entry needs its real intended default restored (or, where the real value cannot be recovered, replaced with an explicit `None`/required-argument pattern that fails at argparse-parse-time with a clear message, rather than silently accepting a placeholder string that only fails later inside the script body).
2. For `fp33_e1_open_base_inventory.py` specifically: recover the original 6 distinct paths if determinable from git history predating the scrub, or otherwise convert `SCAN_ROOTS` to a `--scan-root` (repeatable) CLI argument with no baked-in defaults, since the original intent can no longer be verified.
3. Apply the same post-scrub compile+run discipline proposed in #259 to this file population as well.

## References

- #254 (board reproducibility, placeholder sweep) -- where this class was first enumerated and triaged separately from REDACTION-BROKE-PATH.
- #259 (redaction pass rewrites functional code segments) -- the general tool-defect issue; this is a sibling instance affecting research scripts rather than board probes.

GOAL.md now carries exactly four completion conditions (C1-C4) in §2; docs/spec/conditions-v1.md does not exist; the manifest's real data table is 55 rows (M1..M55). Per constitution §9 this is a goal-surface conflict: the affected probe stops until reconciled. It currently reports this exact reason honestly (correct interim behavior).

**Reconciliation ruling (maintainer seat):**
1. The authoritative 'planned pieces' denominator post-refound = **constitution §2 (C1-C4) + the §8 Map entries**, with v1's 17 conditions conserved in docs/goal-clear-protocol.md per its conservation clause. The v1 C-condition enumeration is HISTORY (docs/goal-archive*), never authority.
2. C-MANIFEST's job restated: verify the manifest's M1..M55 module rows each map to a live Map entry or a conserved protocol condition — orphan rows (mapping only to archived v1 conditions) are reported as ORPHANED-BY-REFOUND, not failures.
3. Implementation: probe reads C1-C4 + §8 entries from GOAL.md structurally; legacy-id-map (added in #264) translates v1 ids; docs/spec/conditions-v1.md is NOT to be created (would resurrect a dead surface).
4. Board effect: C-MANIFEST stays RED/AUDIT-PENDING with the honest reason until a PR implements this ruling; board re-run #3 proceeds — an honest RED does not block the re-baseline.

Scope: one probe + its docstring/report strings. Not a license to touch other probes.

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
Surfaced during the #250/#211 live acceptance pass: when ember-cli talks to an EXTERNAL endpoint via EMBER_MODEL_URL, the models.json `maxOutputTokens` (and sampling parameters generally) are NOT applied — they only govern a managed model spawn. There is no app-level knob to bound generation length against an external server; a test or operator wanting a token cap has only server-side options.

Also worth folding into the same seam: EMBER_MODEL_URL takes a bare origin and the code appends `/v1/chat/completions` (entrypoints/session-init.ts), so a value already containing `/v1` produces a silent double-/v1 404. Either normalize (strip a trailing /v1) or document the expected shape at the disclosure line.

Scope suggestion: apply the per-model request parameters (max_tokens, temperature, etc.) to the request body regardless of endpoint provenance; treat managed-vs-external as a transport difference, not a config-scope difference. Related: #196 (endpoint precedence, PR in flight).
issue_source_snapshot.title: ember-cli: maxOutputTokens/sampling caps not applied to external EMBER_MODEL_URL endpoints (managed-spawn-only today)

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
Follow-up from #276 (refs #276, #211). Not a close-keyword issue.

While fixing #276 (the input-ref staleness race that silently skipped the
only continuation poke a freshly-created goal would ever get), a broader
structural gap surfaced: \`core/goal-continuation.ts\`'s engine is purely
event-driven -- every continuation attempt depends on some OTHER code path
calling \`maybeContinueIfIdle\` again. There is no periodic/idle re-check
("re-arm") layer.

Consequence: if a poke is skipped for ANY transient reason (eligibility
gate momentarily false -- \`turn_active\`, \`queued_user_input\`, a race like
#276's, or a future one not yet found) and nothing else happens to poke
again afterward (no further user input, no further turn completes), the
goal sits at \`Active\` forever with zero continuations. #276's specific
race is closed, but the class of bug -- "a skipped poke is a permanently
lost wakeup, with no resurrection layer" -- is not.

Spec (docs/goal-mode-mechanism.md) §6's continue-on-idle promise arguably
requires a low-frequency idle re-check (e.g. a bounded interval poll that
re-evaluates eligibility and pokes if genuinely idle) as a backstop under
the event-driven design, not a replacement for it.

Suggested acceptance: a bounded-interval idle re-check exists, is
disabled by the same \`EMBER_GOAL_CONTINUATION='0'\` kill switch, and a
regression test proves a goal recovers autonomous continuation after an
arbitrary transient skip with no further external poke.
issue_source_snapshot.title: goal-continuation engine has no re-arm: a transiently-blocked poke is a permanently lost wakeup

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
R1 twin-divergence audit result (P1 persistence-law tick, #207 research thread; pre-registered bands frozen before measurement).

**Finding:** the executed rung-1 width-grow (step-730 ff8192 → ff_widening_net2net → step-766 ff16384) produced NO effective capacity. After the 36 stabilize steps, every duplicated twin pair is **bit-identical** (median twin cosine 1.0000001 = float-eps around exact 1.0; relative L2 median exactly 0.0, p5=p95=0.0), across all layers, both ffn projections — while non-duplicated parameters trained normally (checkpoints are distinct files, both sha256-verified against their manifests fail-closed; random non-twin column pairs show the expected ~0.0 cosine null).

**Mechanism (predicted before measurement, now confirmed):** the grow op duplicates exactly (cat([g,g]) per the grow script) with no symmetry-breaking noise. Twin in-proj rows paired with twin out-proj halves receive identical gradients under deterministic training, and Muon's Newton–Schulz orthogonalization is permutation-equivariant over identical columns — nothing in the stack ever breaks the tie. The widened net is functionally the pre-grow model in a larger container: ~467M effective in a 718M shell.

**Pre-registered consequences (K1, from the tick-5 design):**
1. No persistence claim may cite the 730→766 event as a live grow.
2. **Grow-operator respec REQUIRED before any W2 G-arm launch** — this is now a launch gate. Candidate cures for the respec (to be designed, not decided here): small asymmetric noise on duplicated units at grow time (the classic Net2Net prescription); asymmetric weight split; or deliberate per-twin dropout/masking during a brief post-grow window. The respec must add its own receipt: a twin-divergence check at stabilize-end with a pre-registered divergence floor (the R1 audit machinery is reusable as the acceptance test).
3. The P5 commutation-defect (d_comm) measurement on this grow event re-scopes: measurements remain valid as instrument validation, but they characterize a symmetric-duplication operator, not a live capacity event.
4. If the optimizer's split-handling was INTENDED to break symmetry at grow time, that intent silently failed — worth checking the optimizer-side grow handling when designing the cure.

**Instrument note (does not affect the verdict):** the audit's stable-rank metric returned a degenerate 1.0 for all tensors at both checkpoints — implausible for trained weights and flagged as an audit-tool defect to fix before any claim NEEDS stable-rank numbers. The verdict rests entirely on the bit-identity measurements, which are exact.

Receipts: twin-audit JSON with per-layer tables, checkpoint shas, and the grow-script mapping rule (file:line) — landing via the research-receipts PR. Verdict label: PROVISIONAL per the tick-5 prereg discipline (adversary pass pending) — but the operational gate (item 2) applies immediately; launching a G-arm on a null grow operator would burn GPU-hours measuring nothing. Refs #207, #113.
issue_source_snapshot.title: grow operator: exact duplication never breaks twin symmetry — rung-1 grow was capacity-null as-run (K1; gates W2 G-arm launch)

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
The constitutional invariant (operator directive) has been defined by a directed panel (3 seats: content / mechanism / adversary) plus a terminal adversarial verdict leg (verdict: AMEND with six defects, all applied; amended text pre-approved). The candidate text is frozen at 101 lines of canonical ASCII+LF, sha256 `1718e03d683401a3d013450d1ce11c1c6c3945f6563cac7a1c5839da5a1e4abe`. This issue specs the GENESIS mechanization — everything that must land in ONE atomic commit, plus the ceremony order. The text itself arrives via the genesis PR.

## Design principles (from the panel, binding on this implementation)
- The invariant is a DEFINITION, not a command: violating it does not amend ember, it ends it (a disclosed violating act voids dependent claims and is survivable; CONCEALMENT is the identity-ending act — this split removes the cover-up incentive).
- Entrenchment is by construction: the clause lives inside the record it protects (its hash stamped into every post-genesis artifact), plus external anchors that convert quiet revision into visible identity-fork. Detection-over-prevention, stated honestly.
- The existing `invariant_checksum` + PENDING_AUTHORIZATION flow is CHANGE-MANAGEMENT for the amendable enforcement set. The new surface has NO authorization channel at all. The two must never merge, share names, or share code paths.

## The genesis commit (atomic; contents)
1. `INVARIANT.md` at repo root — the frozen canonical bytes. `.gitattributes` gains `INVARIANT.md -text` (same class as the existing GOAL.md pin; hash portability for outside verifiers on autocrlf clones).
2. `GOAL.md` §9 precedence amended: `INVARIANT.md > this constitution > ...` + the literal pin line `invariant_sha256: <H>`.
3. `scripts/lib/invariant.py` — the single stamping chokepoint: `INVARIANT_SHA256` constant; `stamp(dict)` computes the hash FROM DISK, compares to the constant, raises on mismatch (artifact REFUSED rather than written unstamped — fail-closed); `verify(repo_root)`; NO authorization branch by design.
4. Writer integration: checkpoint manifest writers and receipt writers call `stamp()`; `receipt_check.py` extended to REJECT any post-genesis receipt lacking the field or carrying a wrong value.
5. Board probe `test_c_invariant.py` (condition C-INV, registered in the conditions registry): (a) INVARIANT.md bytes hash to the constant; (b) GOAL.md pin present; (c) post-genesis manifests/receipts stamped; (d) INVARIANT-ERRATA.md append-only prefix property (sha of current bytes[0:prev_len] == prev sha, from consecutive board receipts); (e) prior board receipt's invariant status not silently flipped. CONTRACT EXCEPTION, explicit in the probe: MISSING FILE IS BREACH, not UNEVALUABLE — for this one probe, deletion of the input IS the violation. Runner special-case on the breach token: WRITE the receipt anyway (`invariant_breach: true`), force `complete=false`, exit nonzero — a breach observation leaving no receipt would itself be a record gap (deliberately different from REGISTRY_DRIFT's abort-before-write).
6. Board receipts gain `constitutional_invariant` block (expected/observed sha, status, genesis ts, errata sha + length) AND `prev_totality_receipt_sha256` — the chain-link field that turns board history into a hash chain (the runner currently reads the prior receipt but writes no link). F4 of the FORK-TEST depends on this.
7. `receipts/incidents/` — the disclosure ledger (append-only; a violation disclosed within one board run or 72 hours, whichever is later, leaves the system wounded-and-alive per the text; the ledger's existence is what converts silence into a concealment-class act). A C-INV-adjacent check verifies ledger chain integrity and that every incident row's quarantine executed.
8. Annotated tag `invariant-genesis`, message carries H.

## Ceremony order (the commit is step 2 of 5)
1. GENESIS AUDIT (precondition — the anchor does NOT drop until this receipt exists): audit every live track's data/weight/tokenizer lineage against the final wording; the audit receipt NAMES the protected lineage's starting checkpoint (the text binds only from there; earlier artifacts are history, not lineage). Per the verdict leg's livability note this audit MUST also sweep live prompt templates: post-genesis, no externally-drafted prompt may touch the training-signal path — prompts are enumerated path elements with no tool exception.
2. The genesis commit + tag, pushed.
3. Board run → the genesis totality receipt = first chain link; committed.
4. EXTERNAL ANCHORS, same day (all zero-cost; operator-gated as an off-machine act): Software Heritage save-code-now (snapshot must contain the first stamped receipt — the text's genesis condition anchors the hash AND a record snapshot, not the hash alone); OpenTimestamps stamp of H; one named immutable deposit (Zenodo class). Until anchored, the text is — by its own clause 7 — a draft with a hash.
5. HF model cards (front-matter + full text) next upload; the paper carries text + H + genesis identifiers in an appendix.

## Identity-critical hardening (from the verdict leg's D1 residual)
Branch protection on the publication channel becomes identity-critical infrastructure: F2's residual attack surface is credentialed force-push to a channel the record has named as its own. Protect the default branch (no force-push, no deletion) and treat channel-credential hygiene as part of the invariant surface. The repo's history becomes rewrite-forbidden forever — this is a feature, and it is also a commitment; it is named here so it is chosen, not stumbled into.

## Non-goals (explicit)
- No retroactive re-judgment of pre-genesis history (it is evidence under the same verification rules, not lineage).
- No in-repo gate pretends to PREVENT local edits: enforcement code is amendable and detectably-weakened, never unweakenable; the floor is the external anchors + the re-runnable board.
- `tools/fork_test.py` (the six-step outsider test as one command) is desirable but NOT genesis-blocking; file separately after genesis.
issue_source_snapshot.title: INVARIANT genesis: mechanization spec (stamping chokepoint, C-INV probe, receipt chain-link, incidents ledger, ceremony order)

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
## Symptom (found during ember#276/#278 fix-verification, live acceptance leg (b) scenario C)

Typing text and pressing Enter while ember-cli is busy (an autonomous goal continuation or an
ordinary model turn in flight) does not queue the submission for once-idle delivery -- the
keystroke is silently dropped. The typed text stays visibly sitting in the input line
(`<ceil> <text>`) with no submission happening until the user notices and presses Enter again.

**Reproduced twice, same symptom both times**, across two independent live ConPTY runs against
a fresh post-#278 binary (master @ 4cfaf4e32, sha256
bb2cf7ea4e80b1cea2e2bdba407e303ba2bcbdb855f89f94c2a6558e26d8c4b4):
- Run 1 (test-j): typed a preemption-check message while a continuation turn was in flight
  ("Thinking..." on the status bar); the message sat in the live input line, unsubmitted, for
  the entire remaining ~10s of that test run (which exited early on an unrelated harness bug).
- Run 2 (test-k, corrected harness): same message, same situation. Injected at 14.2s into the
  session (right as a continuation turn was active). It sat in the live input line unsubmitted
  until 40.3s -- a ~26 SECOND gap -- during which the harness periodically resent a bare Enter
  keystroke every 5s (mimicking what a real user watching the screen would naturally do once
  they noticed their first Enter didn't submit). Only after a later Enter landed while the app
  was idle did the message actually submit, immediately followed by a genuine, correct reply
  (`You ... PREEMPT-CHECK: ... / ●ACK [operator]`) -- confirming "user always preempts" DOES
  work correctly once the message actually gets through; the defect is specifically that the
  FIRST Enter, pressed while busy, is dropped rather than queued.

## Likely code-level cause (not yet confirmed by reading the exact handler -- flagging for the
fix lane to verify)

`screens/repl.ts`'s Enter-key submit path guards on busy state: `if (busyRef.current ||
!inputState.text.trim()) return;` -- an early return with no side effect. If the raw stdin
listener that dispatches Enter keystrokes (`ink/stdin-bridge.ts`, per the #278 fix's own
description of how keyboard input arrives) calls this same guarded path, an Enter that lands
while `busyRef.current` is true is a pure no-op: the keystroke is gone, not deferred. The typed
TEXT survives (it's already in `inputState`/`inputStateRef` from earlier keypresses), but the
submission intent (the Enter press itself) does not persist anywhere for replay once idle.

## Why this matters

Goal mode's whole value proposition is "work continues autonomously while you can still step
in whenever you want" (GOAL.md #6, docs/goal-mode-mechanism.md #3: "user always preempts").
If a user's first Enter during an autonomous stretch is silently swallowed, from their
perspective they typed a message, hit Enter, and nothing happened -- no error, no queued
indicator, nothing -- until they notice and try again. This is a legitimate operator-facing
paper cut on top of the #276/#278 fix, not a re-opening of it: once a message DOES submit, the
reply is correct and immediate.

## Suggested fix directions

- (a) Queue a genuine Enter-while-busy as "submit as soon as idle" instead of dropping it
  (mirrors how `queuedUserInput` eligibility already treats non-empty input text as
  preemption-worthy -- the submission INTENT deserves the same treatment as the text itself); or
- (b) At minimum, surface a visible "message queued, will send when idle" indicator so the user
  knows their Enter registered, even if actual submission is deferred.

## Evidence paths (this environment, not part of the repo)
- `C:/WINDOWS/TEMP/claude/.../scratchpad/deploy250-harness/runs/test-k-scenario-c/final-transcript.txt`
  (search for the marker text and note it renders first as a `<ceil>`-prefixed unsent input line
  for ~26s, then later as a `You ...` submitted line)
- `C:/WINDOWS/TEMP/claude/.../scratchpad/deploy250-harness/captures/test-k-result.json`
  (`injectedAtMs: 14199`, `markerSubmittedAtMs: 40303`)

Refs #211, #276, #278.
issue_source_snapshot.title: goal-mode: Enter pressed while busy is silently dropped, not queued (found in #276/#278 verification)

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
The genesis audit (full report lands in the genesis PR as `receipts/genesis/genesis-audit-20260706.md`) found that **no existing checkpoint qualifies to begin the invariant's protected lineage**: every from-scratch pretrain draws on the single pinned v0 corpus (`receipts/eng36-assembly-20260611T052337Z.json`), whose FineWeb-Edu component (~29% of corpus bytes, `receipts/eng36-fineweb_edu-20260611T044544Z.json`) was inclusion-filtered by a classifier trained on Llama-3-70B-Instruct annotations (FineWeb paper 2406.17557; `HuggingFaceFW/fineweb-edu-classifier` card). Under INVARIANT clause 3, inclusion/exclusion decisions are protected path elements — an external model's quality judgment shaping the data distribution is soft distillation via curation. This issue is the road to the first protected checkpoint.

## Deliverables
1. **Clean corpus assembly v1**: drop FineWeb-Edu; replace its byte share with sources whose inclusion criteria are deterministic and non-ML (candidates: expanded Wikipedia/Gutenberg slices, additional permissive-license code via the existing deterministic license-field filter, public-domain/government text; each with an eng36-style receipt). Alternative path (b) — re-deriving an edu-quality classifier trained end-to-end inside the receipted chain — is deferred: it requires ember-lineage annotation capability that does not exist yet.
2. **Tokenizer re-freeze** against the new assembly receipt (`scripts/tokenizer_freeze.py` mechanism is already clean — deterministic ByteLevel BPE on ember's own corpus sample; it only needs the new corpus pin).
3. **Fresh pretrain launch** through the existing `timeshare_pretrain.py` / launch-gate harness against the new tokenizer + corpus. The step-0 checkpoint of that run is the genesis-lineage candidate; a receipted lineage audit certifies it against clause 3 (per clause 7 as amended: audit-names-none → first subsequently-certified checkpoint).
4. **Board condition split** (audit ruling 4): a distinct condition for the borrowed-core/adapter track so its GREEN can never be conflated with clause-3 creation claims; C-BASE (or C-INV) gains a corpus-provenance leg.

## Explicitly NOT invalidated
All existing checkpoints, receipts, and experiments remain valid RESEARCH — clause 7 classes them as history, not lineage. No creation-scoped completion claim was ever minted on them (C8/C-SCALE never GREEN), so nothing retroactive breaks. The growth-operator work (#280), persistence-law design, and measurement chains proceed unchanged on existing artifacts as instrument/method development; their eventual clause-3-scoped claims re-run on the clean lineage.

## Sizing note
The v0 corpus was 25.3GB with FineWeb-Edu at ~7.4GB. Replacement share need not be like-for-like educational prose; it needs receipted provenance and deterministic inclusion. The corpus rebuild is CPU/disk work (no GPU gate); the fresh pretrain re-enters the normal GPU queue.
issue_source_snapshot.title: Clean corpus v1: external-model-free assembly + tokenizer re-freeze + fresh pretrain (the road to the first invariant-protected checkpoint)

issue_source_snapshot.body:
Operator-reported (2026-07-06, live screenshot of the running cockpit, wide-short viewport ~208x22): the welcome/status surface fails the field bar badly. Eight named defects from the pixels, each independently checkable in a ConPTY capture:

1. **Fixed-width layout in a wide window.** Welcome box occupies ~55% of columns; the input rule and status bar stop at ~40%; everything left-crammed with a dead right field. This is the same fixed-width class as the earlier live-resize failure — still unfixed at this viewport.
2. **Border/header corruption.** A stray `│` fragment renders beyond the welcome box's right edge; the box's own "ember" border label, a separate floating "▌ ember v0.0.0" header, and an orphaned "Tips for getting started" heading (top-right, with NO content beneath it) are three disconnected header fragments fighting for one identity.
3. **Void dominance.** One thin content strip at top; ~70% of the viewport is empty black below it.
4. **Status bar renders as ragged inverse patches.** Black-text-on-grey highlight runs (looks like accidentally-selected text, not design), and the first item is left-clipped (renders as "o observe").
5. **Unidentified grey filled bar** directly under the input line (~40% width) — reads as a scrollbar/progress artifact; no discernible function.
6. **Tip text truncated with "…"** at fixed width while half the window is empty.
7. **Empty-state is undesigned**: "Recent activity" / "No recent activity" / "/resume for more" as bare dim stacked lines with a stray horizontal rule.
8. **No token discipline**: a lone teal accent, a white heading, grey inverse blocks — vs the charmtone palette + glyph system already distilled in `tools/ember-cli/state/field-ux-map.md` §8b (which remains the binding taste doc).

Acceptance (all receipts, no self-report):
- ConPTY captures at BOTH operator viewports — wide-short ~208x22 AND tall half-screen ~105x55 — plus a live-resize probe between them (reflow required; clipped borders / dead columns / mid-word truncation = fail).
- Before/after rasterized frames side-by-side with the field exemplar's structure (single coherent header, content-sized bordered box, one clean muted status row, designed empty-state).
- Every defect above either cured in the capture or explicitly disclosed as remaining, per-item.

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
Incident receipt (2026-07-06 ~21:22-21:35Z, #193 persisting re-run attempt): the scan's main process died while its multiprocessing workers kept running — worker heartbeat rows continued appearing in scratch/w2-heldout-run/mp-progress-20260706T212233Z.jsonl for ~6+ minutes after the parent PID was gone, and the leaderless workers held ~20GB of system commit. That stranded commit then caused the NEXT launch attempt to fail the W2_DECONTAM_INSUFFICIENT_HEADROOM preflight (9.2GB free < 12GB required) — the leak from the first failure blocked its own retry. Cohort was reaped manually (kill receipts banked externally); free commit recovered 7.3GB -> 27.8GB.

Two defects, one fix each in scripts/w2_heldout/build_decontam_batch_mp.py:
1. ASSERT SCOPE: any headroom/commit assert that can fire after worker spawn converts a refusal into a leak. The assert must run PREFLIGHT (before Pool creation), and any mid-run resource check that trips must go through the same teardown path as normal exit, never a bare raise that kills the parent first.
2. WORKER TEARDOWN ON ANY EXIT: the parent needs a finally/atexit that terminates+joins the pool on every exit path (assert, exception, SIGINT). A worker that can outlive its parent is an orphan-commit bomb — this is the second commit-exhaustion incident of this class in 3 days (2026-07-04: leaked capture/probe processes, 5.8GB).

Acceptance: kill -9 the parent mid-scan in a test harness -> zero surviving workers within N seconds; assert-trip path -> zero surviving workers + nonzero exit + partial receipt written.
issue_source_snapshot.title: decontam mp scan: headroom assert scope + worker teardown on main-process death

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
Split from #286 / PR #291 (disclosed residual, confirmed at gate from the committed captures). After the #291 fixes, the FIRST live resize reflows correctly (208x22 -> 105x55: clean full-width panel, pixel receipts in tools/ember-cli/state/captures-286/). But a SECOND resize back to a previously-seen size (105x55 -> 208x22) is not reliably detected: process.stdout.columns/rows remains stuck at the intermediate size even with an explicit _refreshSize() call, so the app renders a clean 105-wide layout inside a 208-wide window (capture: after-wide-again-208x22.png — left-half panel, right-half void).

Evidence from the #291 lane's isolation work: a minimal Bun+ConPTY repro OUTSIDE the app detects both resize directions correctly — the failure only manifests under the app's heavier repaint I/O, pointing at a Bun/ConPTY interaction (related background: oven-sh/bun#17803, columns/rows never auto-refresh on Windows) rather than a defect in the #291 provider/poller fix itself.

Severity: the operator's default workflow is live half-screen/full-screen resizing — a stuck-width layout in a wide window is a first-class visible defect, not cosmetic. Acceptance: ConPTY capture session with >=3 size transitions including a return to a previously-seen size; every transition reflows to full width within one poll interval; add the wide-tall-wide sequence to the capture battery as a standing regression check.

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
Two operator-observed defects on the LIVE cockpit window (2026-07-07, verbatim-class report):

1. **Zero activity in the window.** The cockpit displayed no activity during a period when the system was demonstrably working (merges landing on master, board run executing, research receipts being produced). The body is the operator's audit channel (GOAL P-C) — an organism that works while its body shows nothing is a P-C violation regardless of internal health. Expected: the window surfaces live signals (journal/receipt/run events) within seconds of them occurring; a quiet-but-alive state must still show liveness (heartbeat/last-event timestamp), never a static void.

2. **Bottom UI region missized/small compared to the top.** Layout defect in the live TUI: the lower portion of the interface renders undersized relative to the upper portion. Acceptance for closing: live demonstration receipts (#242 program bar — unit-green/self-report do not count): (a) a capture showing real-time event flow in the window while a background run produces receipts; (b) before/after captures at the operator viewport showing the bottom region correctly sized, surviving a live resize.

issue_source_snapshot.body:
Found live 2026-07-07: a verification receipt (cbase-gpu-verify-hardened-20260707T053613Z.json, now VOIDED by VOID2) satisfied the #311 anti-degeneracy bar — its 10 losses varied across batches — while verifying nothing: every loss hugged ln(32000)=10.373 within ±0.009, the exact signature of a uniform random predictor (weights never loaded). Variance-hardening without level-hardening admits fabricated verifications.

Hardening spec for test_c_base.py (forward-only, probe-side, no receipt edits):
1. LEVEL check: reject any 'verification' loss trace whose mean sits within a band around ln(vocab_size) (e.g. |mean - ln(V)| < 0.05 with V from the receipt's own model block) — that level is only producible by uniform logits, which no trained-checkpoint verification can emit. If the eval data is random tokens, a real trained model produces CE ABOVE ln(V) (non-uniform q against uniform labels), never pinned AT it.
2. RESOURCE consistency: a receipt claiming device=GPU must carry vram_peak >= a floor derivable from its own model block (params x bytes/param x activation slack); 33MB peak for a 718M model is self-refuting and should auto-reject.
3. TEXT audit: reject verification.loss_function strings containing 'random logits' (a receipt describing its own loss as computed on random logits is not a verification of anything).
4. Regression fixtures: the VOIDED receipt itself becomes the negative test case; the honest-failure shape (a receipt reporting load-failure with no verdict claim) must still be accepted as a non-verdict artifact.

Class note: this is the second C-BASE receipt generation to fail in a NEW way after the previous hardening (bit-identical -> variance bar -> random-level). Each hardening must add its predecessor as a fixture, or the gate only ever blocks last night's fraud.
issue_source_snapshot.title: gate gap: C-BASE degeneracy hardening checks loss VARIANCE but not loss LEVEL — a random-logits receipt passes

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
Research-loop tick 9 artifact. STATUS: PROPOSED — fires only after (a) L3 boundary ruling v2 ratification (#315), (b) the obtainability receipts below, (c) the one governance pick flagged in M1. Full derivation chain + panel adjudication: research-loop lab notebook (leo state, tick 9). Even a full kill is a D4 contribution: no published work reports a synthetic-only OCR seed evaluated on real historical scans (closest prior AT-ST, arXiv 2104.13037, never ran it — its authors document confirmation bias in second self-training rounds).

GOAL: decide with receipts whether ember-lineage OCR (synthetic-rendered training, L3-clean by construction) can convert scanned-PD books into training tokens — the gate on the 100B+ scanned-PD text universe (current clean ceiling: 10-30B human-keyed).

## Measurements (in order; each receipted; kill criteria BEFORE any run)

M0 — EDITION INTEGRITY (new, panel FATAL-1 cure): pilot books = PG texts WITH edition evidence only; per book: title-page match receipt; where multiple PD printings exist, scan-vs-scan diff on the M1 line sample — inter-edition disagreement >= the registered M3 delta drops the book. Track-kill if no 3 edition-pinned dual-observation books can be receipted.

M1 — CALIBRATION NOISE FLOOR F (PG-vs-scan CER on ~100 hand-transcribed lines; 9-strata sampling: book x page-third, RNG seed frozen in this issue before any scan is inspected; segmentation failures are the only permitted exclusions, logged; >10% segmentation failure = W3 blocks the pilot). Bootstrap CI on F mandatory; any downstream delta inside F's CI = INCONCLUSIVE by rule. Dual scoring under a PRE-REGISTERED normalization map (long-s->s, ligature expansion, u/v) — raw AND normalized (FATAL-2 cure). Bands: F<=0.5% usable; 0.5-2.0% expand to 300 lines + ground truth switches to hand-corrected subset; F>=2.0% with fallback failing = track-kill.
GOVERNANCE PICK (operator, at ratification): the transcription actor. An agent-lane transcriber places an external model in the calibration chain that sets the admission threshold tau — selection-adjacent under a strict L3 reading. Options: (A) operator hand-transcribes ~100 lines (~2-4h), or (B) ratify measurement-only calibration as outside L3's token-selection chain. Spec ships with both; neither is enacted here.

M2 — SYNTHETIC-SEED CER on the calibration set, TWO ARMS differing ONLY in font inventory (A modern-only / B +period-face revivals) to decompose degradation-shift (W1) vs typeface-gap (W2). Decision bands (disclosed as anchored to AT-ST's DIFFERENT regime — real-data seed at 1.03% — so these are decision rules, not truth claims; arithmetic per verify leg: kill bound = 19.42x that anchor): arm-B <=3% proceed; 3-20% proceed flagged; >=20% track-kill.

M2.5 — DIRECT S1 TEST (new, panel MAJOR-4 cure; pure inference, minutes): per-line confidence vs correctness on the calibration set -> ranking AUC + precision-at-tau curve. AUC <= 0.5+eps kills M3 UNRUN (confidence-filtered self-training cannot work if confidence does not rank correctness).

M3 — ONE self-training round (AT-ST recipe: transcription-posterior ranking, masking augmentation), REPEATED 3x with different pseudo-label subsamples; spread >= registered delta = INCONCLUSIVE by rule (FATAL-3 cure). Regime bands conditional on M2 seed CER: <5% AT-ST-comparable; 5-15% novel-regime (exploratory, own bands); >15% M3 void. Promote decisions from n=3 books are BANNED — the only promote is promote-to-larger-pilot (10-20 books). Kill: CER increases on majority of repeats, or top-confidence-decile CER >= overall seed CER. Per-book reporting mandatory; pooling banned.

## L3 toolchain law (hard, receipted BEFORE M1 fires)
- Segmenter NAMED + deterministic: projection-profile + Otsu + connected components; probe-gated (<10% line-failure on a real pilot scan, 20 spot crops receipted).
- IA/LoC bundled OCR text layers, confidence scores, and boxes: BANNED from every selection, cropping, edition-matching, and verification role.
- Font receipts per period face: license + fontTools glyph-coverage dump (U+017F, ct/st ligatures) + digitization-method disclosure.
- Degradation family: enumerated deterministic ops only (mirrored-page alpha bleed-through, morphological ink spread/erosion, threshold jitter, geometric warp, blur, JP2 recompression); implementation audited against the enumeration (no learned/GAN degraders).
- Toolchain audit receipt EXECUTED (every stage enumerated with provenance), not promised.
- Renderer determinism contract: (font, text, degradation-seed) provenance per line; identical seed -> identical pixels, hash-checked.

## Resource bill (designer estimate, verify-corrected; unverified engineering numbers flagged)
3 books, ~4.5K real lines, 2x100K synthetic lines, ~10 GPU-h (budget 15; wall-clock estimates unverified against any grounded 4090 timing), disk 10-14GB (well under the 100GB escalation), 3-5 days.

## Obtainability prerequisites (receipts before anything fires)
1. >=3 edition-pinned dual-observation books (IA/LoC scan id + PG id + title-page evidence).
2. Period-face revival fonts: free-license artifacts with verified long-s/ligature coverage.
3. Renderer determinism probe; segmentation probe on one real scan.
4. Downloads under the 2026-07-07 public-source standing authorization; sizes logged.

## Corpus-stage honesty clauses (bind any later build, not the pilot)
- L4 verifier field for confidence-admitted tokens: 'ember-ocr-confidence>=tau, calibration-CER=X at tau' — never 'verified'.
- Distribution audit: selected-vs-rejected line composition (typography density, page position) reported — ember-confidence selection biasing the realized corpus toward easy lines is the named science risk.
issue_source_snapshot.title: T1 pilot pre-registration v1.1-PROPOSED: ember-lineage OCR bootstrap (M0-M3, panel-hardened)

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
Research-loop derivation (zero compute; Monte Carlo verification leg dispatched separately). The P5 v1.2 headline measurement d_comm = 1.1352 (receipt p5-ratio-audit-OK-20260707T034951Z) is currently a number without a null. Derivation of the null, from the harness's own formula (run_p5_audit.py::compute_d_comm):

d_comm = ||U_{k+1}(G(th)) - G(U_k(th))||_RMS / ||U_k(th) - th||_RMS

## Null model (independent update directions)
Write U_k(th)=th+u, U_{k+1}(ph)=ph+v, G linear (net2net widen = duplication map P; exact for the production widen_state_dict on weight tensors). Then numerator = ||v - Pu||_RMS and:

  d_comm^2 = r^2 + q^2 - 2 c r q,   r = rms(v)/rms(u),  q = rms(Pu)/rms(u),  c = cos(v, Pu)

INDEPENDENCE NULL: c=0 (the cross term vanishes under independence irrespective of marginals — robust to Muon's non-isotropic orthogonalized steps). So d_comm_null = sqrt(r^2 + q^2).

## Reference points at the real geometry (rung-1: ff 8192 -> 16384, hidden 1024)
- Naive equal-norms (r=q=1): sqrt(2) ~ 1.414.
- Muon width scaling: rms of an orthogonalized (m,n) step = sqrt(min(m,n)/(m*n)); for gate/up (min = hidden = 1024 at both widths, n doubles) => r = sqrt(n1/n2) * (lr_post/lr_pre) = 1/sqrt(2) at equal LR. Duplication preserves rms on gate/up (q=1); down_proj's outgoing halving gives q=1/2 on that tensor.
- Gate/up-dominated refined null at equal LR: sqrt(1/2 + 1) = sqrt(1.5) ~ 1.2247.
- Degenerate reference: v -> 0 (post-grow step vanishing) gives d_comm -> q ~ 1.0.

## The interpretation problem (the actionable finding)
Measured 1.1352 sits BETWEEN the vanishing-step reference (~1.0) and the refined independence null (~1.2247). Two qualitatively different regimes produce numbers here:
(a) near-null independence with the exact r,q mixture (down-proj + LR ratio pulling 1.2247 down), i.e. the grow event does NOT preserve update-direction structure beyond width bookkeeping; or
(b) smaller post-grow step with partial alignment (c>0), i.e. genuine partial commutation.
The current receipt CANNOT distinguish them: it carries numerator_rms and denominator_rms but not rms(v), rms(Pu), or c — all three computable for free from tensors compute_d_comm already holds.

## Proposed spec addition (PROPOSED; additive, receipts immutable, prereg measurement status unchanged)
compute_d_comm returns three more fields: step_rms_post = rms(U_{k+1}(G(th)) - G(th)), pushforward_step_rms = rms(G(U_k(th)) - G(th)), cos_alignment = <v, Pu> / (||v|| ||Pu||). Then d_comm decomposes exactly as d_comm^2 = r^2 + q^2 - 2 c r q against its own null sqrt(r^2+q^2) inside the receipt — the measurement becomes self-interpreting. Verification: Monte Carlo at the real shapes (independent Muon-orthogonalized random momenta, production widen semantics incl. down-halving) must reproduce sqrt(r^2+q^2) and c ~ 0; dispatched as a separate receipted leg, results to be attached here.

No pass bar is proposed — v1.1/v1.2's measurement-only status is conserved; this adds interpretability, not verdict.
issue_source_snapshot.title: d_comm null model derived: the 1.1352 measurement needs two free receipt fields to be interpretable (P5/P0 composition law)

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
Found during the 2026-07-07 W1 refusal forensics (launch lane's window-count reconciliation; the 84-window delta between the runner's recheck and the decontam receipt decoded exactly as 12*(n_groups-1) with n_groups=8).

DEFECT: contamination_recheck_mp (and the same pattern wherever build_decontam_batch_mp.py distributes shards) assigns shards to workers ROUND-ROBIN (group_idx = shard_idx % n_groups), so no worker ever holds two corpus-consecutive shards; each worker's boundary-join logic therefore joins round-robin-adjacent shards, scanning 26-n_groups FAKE boundaries while missing 7 of the 25 TRUE physical shard boundaries entirely. A 13-token window straddling one of those 7 boundaries is never hashed by the MP path.

IMPACT: narrow — only windows physically straddling the missed boundaries escape scanning (dozens of windows per boundary). Tonight's held-out receipt is UNAFFECTED (all 16 selected windows sit deep in shard-16's interior, receipts unchanged). But the gap is systematic: every MP scan to date shares it, and any future held-out window near a missed boundary would get a false CLEAN.

CURE (builder-dispatchable): distribute shards to workers as CONTIGUOUS ranges (worker k gets shards [k*g, (k+1)*g)) so intra-worker joins are true boundaries, and pass each worker its successor's first window-length tokens for the seam; OR keep round-robin and add a dedicated boundary pass that hashes the 25 true seams explicitly. Either way: a regression test that plants a duplicate straddling a true shard boundary and asserts the scanner finds it (fails at current head, passes at fix); and the window-count convention (boundary windows included) stated in the receipt so count deltas stop being forensic surprises.
issue_source_snapshot.title: MP contamination scanner: round-robin shard distribution skips 7 of 25 true shard boundaries (boundary-window coverage gap)

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body: Follow-up from PR #330's gate (non-blocking finding). Current: is_self = any(gstart < c_end and gend > c_start ...) — interval OVERLAP. A foreign 13-token exact match partially straddling a candidate range boundary (shifted alignment, requires periodic/repeated content) would be excluded as self, theoretically masking a genuine boundary-adjacent duplicate. Fix: strict containment (gstart >= c_start and gend <= c_end); matches that overlap-but-exceed a candidate range must count as NON-SELF and refuse. Add a regression test for the straddling case (the PR's foreign-duplicate test only covers far-away, no-overlap). Does not affect the 2026-07-07 refusal forensics (all 16,208 matches were exact full self-matches).

# W1 interpretation pre-registration: reading rules for the control-arm tokens_to_match receipt

Filed against issue #121 (prereg governs). Reading RULES only — no verdicts about reality. All dispositions key on the CLEAN in-process receipt (L2); the attempt-2 crash trail (preserved at `B:/M/ember/scratch/w1-control/live/w1-live-20260707T091615Z/`) is a measurement trail, never a claim basis.

## §1 The measurement + provenance

Attempt-2 (receipt-less, crash-terminated) from-scratch control — rung-1 architecture, 1.22B params, bf16, batch 16 × seq 1024 — on the certified 16-window held-out batch: eval loss step0=10.5625 → step25 (409,600 tok)=10.0 → step50 (819,200 tok)=9.25 ≤ target 9.375; early-stop fired; terminal receipt crashed (path bug, fix in flight). Trajectory is steepening between intervals (−0.5625 then −0.75 per 409,600 tok), i.e. the control was nowhere near its own asymptote at stop. Grow-arm comparison bill: 12,550,144 tokens is the CUMULATIVE lineage bill (seed-pretrain 9,994,240 + pre-grow 983,040 + stabilize 1,572,864 = 96 steps × 16,384), NOT the grow step's marginal cost. Control ceiling 2.0× = 25,100,288 tok. Throughput 6665.66 tok/s.

Target provenance (runner lines 546–667): target_eval_loss computed once AT LAUNCH by evaluating the rung-1 grown checkpoint on the SAME 16-window batch, SAME eval_loss_fn, in bf16 — `loss.item()` quantized to 1 ULP = 0.0625 at magnitude ~10 (all four recorded values sit on that grid). The match margin 9.375−9.25 = 0.125 = exactly 2 bf16 ULPs on one 16-window batch against a single-evaluation target. Eval batch stratum: window indices 4,194,305–4,194,351 (~47 windows), decontam-certified (receipt 055843Z, 0 non-self matches / 6.98B windows). Training stream = corpus FRONT (windows 0..24527 at ceiling); that region's duplication saturation is UNMEASURED.

## §2 Outcome → claim ladder

| Clean-receipt outcome | Licensed claim | Rung |
|---|---|---|
| Match at ~same tokens (~819K, within one eval interval of step 50) | Replicated: from-scratch rung-1 control reaches the grown checkpoint's target (9.375, bf16, 16-window batch) in ~819,200 tok ≈ 6.5% of the 12.55M CUMULATIVE lineage bill. Caveats named in-claim: prices the whole lineage (seed-dominated), not the grow step; margin is 2 bf16 ULPs on 16 windows — equality is coarse until the §3 paired re-eval passes. Consistent with Ash & Adams warm-starting prior. | replicated-measurement |
| Match later (>2× tokens, ≤25.1M ceiling) | Measurement disagreement: crash trail and clean run bracket the crossing (0.8M–N). Only the clean run's N is claimable; seed/data-order variance becomes a named unknown; no "X% cheaper" number licensed. | interpretation-pending-checks (seed probe + discrepancy note required) |
| No match within 25,100,288 tok | Clean receipt contradicts the trail; only the clean run counts. From-scratch does NOT reach target within 2× the cumulative bill — evidence the rung-1 lineage carries value. Caveats: 16-window bf16 eval, training-front duplication unmeasured; attempt-2 becomes an anomaly requiring explanation before hardening. | measurement / interpretation-pending-checks |
| Match earlier (<409,600 tok) | Replicated in direction, stronger in magnitude (≤3.3% of bill); raises suspicion the TARGET is weak, not the control strong. Claim: rung-1 grow lineage's eval advantage is small-or-nil at THIS resolution; finer eval (fp32, larger batch) is the named next check before any "grow adds no value" promotion. | replicated (direction) / pending-checks (magnitude) |

## §3 Alternative explanations + discriminating checks (verifier-passed, rail-clean)

| Name | Check | Cost | Kills the collapse reading if |
|---|---|---|---|
| Eval noise + bf16 2-ULP margin (strongest attack; noise-floor figure "std≈0.7, cbase attempt-3" is UNSOURCED in this pack — trace to a receipt before it anchors anything) | Paired eval of step-50 control ckpt and grown ckpt on K fresh certified 16-window batches, fp32 loss accumulation; paired mean diff + bootstrap 95% CI. FEASIBILITY AMENDMENT (verifier): the certified stratum is ~47 windows ≈ 2–3 non-overlapping batches — a new decontam-certification pass over additional clean windows is REQUIRED to reach K≥10; budget that pass into the check | Minutes GPU forward-only + one certifier run (CPU); haiku-buildable off eval_loss_fn | Paired CI excludes zero in the grown checkpoint's favor. Conversely, collapse reading survives only if CI includes zero or favors control |
| Target self-comparison bias (single bf16 launch eval may be ULP-inflated) | Re-evaluate grown ckpt 10× on the same batch, fp32 accumulation, fixed seeds; diff launch-time vs in-loop eval code paths for mode/dtype asymmetry | Seconds GPU + code read (cheapest check) | fp32 re-eval lands materially below 9.375 — control never matched; early-stop fired on a quantization-inflated target |
| Trivial target (both arms in cheap early-descent regime; note: attempt-2 curve is STEEPENING, strengthening "pre-asymptotic") | Extend control (early-stop off, max_steps~200, existing runner/config) + continue grown ckpt; compare token-matched curves past the cheap region | ~10–30 min single-GPU, zero new code | From-scratch flattens sharply post-step-50 while grown arm sits on a better token-matched trajectory |
| Wrong comparison: cumulative bill vs grow-step marginal value | (a) eval PRE-grow ckpt on the certified batch (one forward pass); (b) continue-train pre-grow ckpt UNWIDENED for exactly 1,572,864 stabilize tokens, eval; marginal grow value = (b) − post-grow on paired batches | (a) seconds; (b) rung-0-width run, ~1.6M tok, minutes | Post-grow beats unwidened continuation at matched marginal tokens — the grow STEP added value; the match indicts seed/lineage economics, not the growth mechanism |
| Training-front duplication triviality | Run the existing decontam/duplication scanner (055843Z tooling) over windows 0..24527; report dup/near-dup fraction vs clean-stratum rate | CPU-only, tooling exists, <1h, haiku lane | Front region is duplication-saturated — control's descent partially memorization; collapse claim needs a rerun on certified-clean training data |
| Generalization vs single-stratum fit (Ash & Adams inversion) | Eval both ckpts on 3 out-of-region strata (different depth bands, 16–64 windows each, newly certified); per-stratum paired deltas | Forward-only minutes GPU + certifier runs (CPU) | Grown ckpt wins consistently out-of-region — single-stratum tie masked a generalization advantage |

All GPU checks run under the resource governor: VRAM-fraction cap + headroom assert on every launch. Agent routing: haiku default, budget caps apply.

## §4 P2 rung-1 lever decision rules (L7-shaped: park with a path, never kill)

1. **Match at ≤~1.6M tok (≤2× attempt-2) AND the §3 paired fresh-batch fp32 re-eval confirms** (CI includes zero or favors control) → PARK the rung-1 grow lever. Park-exit paths, filed on #121's successor: (a) a rung where from-scratch control cost exceeds the cumulative grow bill; (b) a specced shrink-perturb variant (Ash & Adams remedy). AMENDMENT (verifier finding 6): a bare token-match without the statistical confirmation licenses NO park — the paired re-eval is a mandatory gate, not an optional check.
2. **Match but >2× attempt-2 tokens** → HOLD: one more seed; disposition follows the 2-of-3 majority bracket; hold receipt names seed variance as the blocking unknown.
3. **No match within 25,100,288 tok** → HOLD the lever as provisionally-valuable. Required before promotion to "earns its bill": explain the attempt-2 discrepancy + measure training-front duplication (§3 rows 3, 5).
4. **Match <409,600 tok** → PARK with escalated path: before park-exit, re-measure the TARGET at finer resolution (fp32 accumulation, ≥128-window certified batch — requires the new certification pass from §3 row 1). A 2-ULP margin on 16 bf16 windows is too coarse to price a pillar.
5. **Always:** no disposition executes off the crash trail alone; every disposition files against #121's prereg and is disclosed in the window ledger same turn. Only the operator kills the lever (L7).

## §5 W2 G-arm inheritance (#113)

Unconditional: (1) from-scratch control as a co-launched leg BY CONSTRUCTION, never a follow-up; (2) target provenance fixed — computed at launch on the destination checkpoint, same eval_fn, upgraded to fp32 loss accumulation on a ≥128-window certified batch (bf16 2-ULP margin was W1's weakest joint; certifying that batch is a named pre-launch task, per the ~47-window stratum limit); (3) receipt schema splits grow-STEP marginal tokens from lineage cumulative — W1's billing caveat cannot recur; (4) training-region duplication measured for the G-arm's stream region before launch. Outcome-conditional: if W1 replicates the cheap-match (post-§3-confirmation), the G-arm carries a shrink-perturb third leg (test the field's remedy, not re-measure the pathology); if W1 fails-to-match, two-leg shape stands, control ceiling stays 2.0× cumulative.

## §6 What this prereg does NOT cover

- Any claim about growth at rungs >1, other architectures, or other data mixtures — this prices ONE lever at ONE rung on ONE stream.
- Generalization/downstream quality beyond the eval strata named in §3 (the 16-window batch measures next-token fit on a narrow slice).
- The grow STEP's marginal value unless §3 row 4 executes — absent it, all readings price the lineage, seed-dominated (9.99M of 12.55M).
- The noise-floor magnitude: the ~0.7 batch-std figure has no receipt in this pack; §3 row 1's paired design is chosen precisely so no reading depends on it.
- Net2Net's limitations section (abstract-only fetch — unverified) and L3 compliance (rail text absent from the grounding pack; flagged as a pack gap, not resolved here).
- Whether the training-front region is clean — unmeasured until §3 row 5 runs; every §2 claim inherits that caveat.

---
## Addendum (filed with the prereg, closing the verifier's headline gap)
The ~0.7 eval-noise figure the panel flagged as unsourced HAS a receipt: receipts/cbase-verify-attempt3-20260707T073843.json, field loss_std = 0.7059 (per-batch std across 10 seq-512 batches of the C-BASE checkpoint on real shards). Cross-checkpoint transferability to the W1 pair remains the named caveat (panel finding b3) - the sec.3 row-1 paired design is chosen so no reading depends on it.

Panel provenance: RESEARCH-LOOP-FABLE-PANEL workflow (2 fable seats blind-parallel + sonnet arithmetic verify + fable synthesis), run wf_043dbb9c-c88, 2026-07-07. Filed BEFORE the confirmation re-run receipt was read (the fix PR was not yet merged at filing time) - this issue IS the pre-registration.
issue_source_snapshot.title: W1 interpretation pre-registration: reading rules for the control-arm tokens_to_match receipt (filed before the confirmation receipt)

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
C-BASE's evaluability status is not stable across consecutive board runs on the
same rig with zero code changes in between.

## The 180s harness timeout is a global, uniform parameter

`scripts/ember_totality/ember_totality_spec.py:103`:

```python
PROBE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 180
```

Applied identically to every one of the 39 probes via `subprocess.run(...,
timeout=PROBE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS)` at line 792; on expiry it writes
(`ember_totality_spec.py:798`):

```python
"reason": (f"HARNESS TIMEOUT: {fname} exceeded "
```

There is no per-probe override -- C-BASE gets the same 180s budget as every
other condition, despite doing real GPU-checkpoint load/verify work that
other probes don't.

## Two consecutive receipts, same rig, no code changes between them

**ember-totality-20260707T095800Z.json** -- C-BASE completed within the
window:

```json
{
  "condition": "C-BASE",
  "status": "RED",
  "is_process_invariant": false,
  "reason": "RED C-BASE: owned checkpoint B:\M\ember\models\cbase-grow-rung\rung1-20260703T155447Z\stabilize\checkpoints\step-00000766 exists with hashes (model.pt sha256 verified vs manifest in receipt cbase-gpu-verify-trainable-clean-20260707T015633.json), but CHK clause (d) is UNMET -- no grow-operator dry-run receipt produces a valid larger-shape checkpoint that replays (function-preserving net2net/layer-stacking/expert-addition); the growth operator exists only as a decision-record doc that does NOT authorize a build => invalid_calcified_seed: the seed graph cannot be shown growable. Artifact genuinely ABSENT"
}
```

**ember-totality-20260707T101540Z.json** (the very next chained receipt) --
same rig, same tree, C-BASE hit the timeout:

```json
{
  "condition": "C-BASE",
  "status": "UNEVALUABLE",
  "is_process_invariant": false,
  "reason": "HARNESS TIMEOUT: test_c_base.py exceeded 180s -- probe did not complete"
}
```

Both receipts chain correctly (prev_totality_receipt_sha256 verified). No
commits landed on the C-BASE probe or the checkpoint it reads between these
two runs -- the only variable is wall-clock probe duration versus a fixed
180s ceiling, i.e. classic flakiness from a tight timeout against variable
load/verify time (disk I/O contention, GPU driver warm state, or general
machine load at run time), not a logic change.

## Ask

Not filing a fix here -- narrow issue only, per team-lead's ask. Worth
deciding: raise C-BASE's specific budget (per-probe timeout override rather
than the uniform 180s), or make C-BASE's checkpoint verify path itself
faster/more deterministic (e.g. skip a full re-hash if a recent verify
receipt already covers the same checkpoint). Either cures the flakiness;
which one is a call for whoever owns the probe's design.
issue_source_snapshot.title: C-BASE evaluability is timing-flaky: 180s harness timeout recurs non-deterministically

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
# Renderer emits NUL-cell runs under a [7m style stack at ~190x85 — visible grey bars + inverted status row at the operator's real viewport

## What the operator sees (live window, screenshot-verified)
At the primary operating viewport (~190 cols x 85 rows = left half of a 3440x1440 display), the
bottom of the cockpit renders: a THICK solid grey bar where the separator line below the input row
should be, and the status row ("o observe · ...") as dark text on a grey background ending after
"tasks" — the same visual class as the original #310 complaint, on the build that carries the #310
cure (#325, merged).

## Byte-level receipts (pipe-pty capture at exactly 190x85, cwd=B:/M/ember, build c99d0d6)
Capture: `scratch/clirebuild/capture-190x85/frame-190x85.ansi` (18,024 bytes).

Two `ESC[7m` spans in the frame tail (zero at 100x32, 130x60, 220x60 — all three earlier sizes clean):

1. byte 16638: `o \x1b[7m \x1b[22m\x1b[27m` — single inverse SPACE, properly closed = the block
   cursor cell. Legal.
2. byte 16848: `\x1b[1m\x1b[2m\x1b[7m` followed by a run of **raw 0x00 (NUL) bytes** — an
   inverse+bold+dim style stack opened over a NUL-cell run. A styled run over blanks paints a solid
   filled bar; that is the grey bar / inverted status visual.

Additionally the frame contains long runs of NUL bytes as cell content in multiple places
(e.g. the ~78 NULs preceding span 1's context). A rendered frame should emit spaces (0x20) for
blank cells — NUL bytes in the output stream are never legal cell content.

## Two defects, likely one emission site
- D1: the renderer emits uninitialized/NUL cells as padding at this size (size-dependent buffer or
  diff-renderer path; absent at the three smaller/other test sizes).
- D2: the style state active when that padding is emitted includes the cursor's `[7m` stack — the
  same style-state-discipline family as #44/#310 (style leaking across an emission boundary), but a
  DIFFERENT site: NUL-padding emission, not last-cell trailing reset (which #325 fixed and whose
  regression tests still pass at the three original sizes).

## Repro
Pipe-pty at exactly 190x85, cwd=B:/M/ember, boot + settle; grep the stream for `\x00` and `\x1b[7m`.
Rig: `scratch/clirebuild/capture-190x85/capture-190x85.mjs`.

## Acceptance for the fix
- No NUL bytes anywhere in the emitted stream at ANY size (property test across a size sweep,
  e.g. {100x32, 130x60, 190x85, 220x60, 250x90} minimum).
- No [7m outside single-cell cursor spans at any swept size.
- Regression test locks the 190x85 case specifically (the operator's real half-screen viewport).

## Process defect banked with this (coordination side, for the record)
The capture matrix called 130x60 "halfscreen" without deriving it from the operator's actual
display (3440x1440 => half = ~190x85). Viewport arithmetic must be computed from the enumerated
display, never assumed.
issue_source_snapshot.title: Renderer emits NUL-cell runs under a [7m style stack at ~190x85 — grey bars + inverted status at the operator's real viewport

issue_source_snapshot.body:
## Incident (2026-07-07, receipts in scratch/w1-control/live/w1-live-20260707T101234Z + scratch/renderfix context)

W1 collapse-control attempt 3 (1.22B bf16 training leg) launched 10:12:34Z with a passing VRAM preflight (93.7% free). At 10:13:46Z the ember-cli cockpit was launched visibly with cwd=B:/M/ember; its boot path unconditionally spawned llama-server (Qwen3.6-27B-Q4_K_M, port 8082), loading ~10.5GB into VRAM. At 10:39Z the training leg's first backward pass failed: torch.OutOfMemoryError (tried 512MiB; 13.42GiB physically free but pool contested/fragmented under the process's 19.19GiB governor cap). The training leg died after a step-0 eval that exactly reproduced the prior attempt (10.5625).

## Defect
The cockpit's boot loads the resident model unconditionally. The body ate the organism's compute: L6 (earned compute) and the standing 1-model-at-a-time serialization both imply a training leg owns the GPU while alive.

## Proposed cure (product side)
- Model lazy-load: boot the TUI without spawning llama-server; load on first inference-requiring interaction.
- GPU-lease awareness: before spawning the model server, check a lease surface (a running training process holding a launch receipt, or a simple lease file under scratch/ named by the live run) and boot model-less with a visible 'GPU leased to training: <run-id>' line in the status area instead. Observe mode (board pane, activity feed, receipts browsing) needs no resident model.
- The status line should always disclose whether a model is resident and how much VRAM it holds — the operator's audit channel should never hide a 10GB tenant.

## Coordination side (already mechanized, for the record)
Work-loop GPU-LEASE clause: no VRAM consumer launches while a training leg is live; training preflights assert no-inference-holder (no llama-server / :8082 listener) in the launch receipt.
issue_source_snapshot.title: Cockpit boot loads the resident inference model unconditionally — needs GPU-lease awareness (OOM-killed a live training leg)
