Executes the discriminating checks pre-registered in #339 §3, in cost order, the moment the W1 clean terminal receipt lands. Reading rules are #339's; this issue is the frozen builder spec. All runs governed (VRAM fraction cap + headroom assert + no-inference-holder assertion in every launch receipt, per the GPU-lease rule).

## Check 1 — target self-comparison bias (#339 §3 row 2; cheapest, first)
Re-evaluate the rung-1 grown checkpoint (models/cbase-grow-rung/rung1-20260703T155447Z/stabilize/checkpoints/step-00000766) on the certified 16-window held-out batch 10×, fp32 loss accumulation (model may stay bf16; accumulate/reduce in fp32), fixed seeds enumerated in the receipt. Also diff the launch-time vs in-loop eval code paths in scripts/w1_collapse_control_run.py for mode/dtype asymmetry (lines ~546-667 vs ~1524-1542). Output: receipt with the 10 values + mean/std + the code-path diff finding. Kills the collapse reading if fp32 re-eval lands materially below 9.375 (early-stop fired on a quantization-inflated target).

## Check 2 — paired fresh-batch eval feasibility prerequisite (#339 §3 row 1 amendment)
The certified stratum spans ~47 windows ≈ 2-3 non-overlapping 16-window batches; K≥10 needs a new decontam-certification pass over additional clean windows (tooling: the 055843Z certifier). Deliverable: the certification receipt for ≥160 fresh clean windows (10 batches), then the paired eval (step-50 control ckpt vs grown ckpt, per-batch paired diffs, bootstrap 95% CI). Decision rule per #339 §4.1: a bare token-match licenses NO park without this CI.

## Check 3 — grow-step marginal value control (#339 §3 row 4; the sharpest)
(a) Eval the PRE-grow checkpoint on the certified batch (one forward pass, receipt). (b) Continue-train the pre-grow checkpoint UNWIDENED for exactly 1,572,864 tokens (the stabilize segment's bill: 96 steps × batch16 × seq1024), same stream discipline as W1's control, then eval. Marginal grow value = (b) vs the post-grow target on paired batches. Kills the 'grow event worthless' reading if post-grow beats the unwidened continuation at matched marginal tokens — the match would then indict the seed-dominated lineage bill (9,994,240 of 12,550,144 tokens), not the growth mechanism.

## Eval-noise context (recorded, not assumed)
Per-batch eval std 0.7059 exists receipted for a DIFFERENT checkpoint (receipts/cbase-verify-attempt3-20260707T073843.json, 10 batches, seq512) — cross-checkpoint transferability is a named caveat (#339 addendum); check 2's paired design is chosen so no reading depends on it.

## Ordering + gates
Check 1 runs first (seconds of GPU); its receipt is required context for reading the W1 number at all. Check 2's certification pass is CPU-side and can start immediately. Check 3 is a rung-0-width training run (~minutes) and fires only after checks 1-2 are receipted. Every receipt cites #339. No check runs while the W1 leg itself is on the GPU.

issue_source_snapshot.body:
## Finding (surfaced during the spend-annex refresh, 2026-07-07)

repo-guard's absolute-local-path check uses a regex of the shape `[A-Za-z]:[/\](Users|M|Downloads)` — one separator character between drive letter and first segment. In JSON files, backslashes are escaped: a local path embeds as `B:\M\...` (two characters per separator), which the regex does NOT match.

Receipts: an annex draft embedding `"root": "B:/M/ember"` (forward slash, unescaped in JSON) WAS caught by the guard; the already-merged spend-annex-20260707T105959Z.json embeds the equivalent in backslash form and passed. The guard therefore only catches the forward-slash spelling of the exact same leak.

## Cure
Extend the pattern to tolerate 1-2 separator characters (escaped backslash pairs): e.g. `[A-Za-z]:(?:[/\]|\\){1,2}(Users|M|Downloads)` or normalize the scanned text (unescape JSON) before matching. Add regression fixtures for both spellings.

## Scope note
This is a guard-integrity item, not a data incident: the leaked values are machine-local directory roots (no personal names), already present in multiple merged receipts as shard/checkpoint paths. The hardening prevents the CLASS from growing.
issue_source_snapshot.title: repo-guard path regex misses JSON-escaped backslash forms — local absolute paths leak through once escaped

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
## Cost receipt
Attempts 2, 3, and 4 tonight each spent ~15-27 minutes in the launch-time contamination recheck before training started — single-core CPU-bound, GPU at 1-2% — against the SAME decontam receipt (w2-heldout-decontam-20260707T055843Z) and the SAME held-out batch. Four launches were needed tonight (gate refusal, receipt-writer crash, OOM, relaunch), so the recheck tax compounded to roughly an hour and a half of wall-clock, most of it GPU-idle. L6 prices this directly.

## Defect shape
The recheck is correct to exist (it caught a real gate gap at attempt 1) but it re-derives a result that is a pure function of (batch content, corpus content, classifier version). None of those changed between attempts 2-4 — the rebuilt batch .npy is byte-identical across attempts.

## Cure
Content-addressed recheck cache: after a PASSing recheck, write a small receipt keyed by sha256(batch npy) + decontam-receipt sha + classifier code sha. On launch, if the triple matches a cached PASS receipt, skip the recheck and cite the cached receipt (path + sha) in the launch receipt instead. Any mismatch = full recheck as today. The cache entry is itself a receipt; the skip is disclosed, not silent.

## Bar
The gate's semantics must not weaken: a cache hit requires ALL THREE shas identical, and the cached receipt must itself chain to the original in-process recheck PASS. Regression test: modified batch => full recheck fires.
issue_source_snapshot.title: W1 runner: contamination recheck re-derives an unchanged certified batch on every launch (~25 GPU-idle min per attempt)

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
## Two defects, one mechanism (surfaced by PR #350's honest re-run of the real generator)

**Defect 1 — attestations are not durable.** PR #348's 17 evidence-backed coverage upgrades were produced by an uncommitted build-time helper rewriting a frozen annex snapshot, not by the scanner. Any real regeneration (PR #350 is the receipt) re-derives them back to unresolvable. Verified evidence is being stored in a file the next generator run overwrites.

**Defect 2 — the scanner has no supersession semantics.** A receipt VOIDed per the VOID discipline stays in the decisive-claim set forever as unresolvable (and the VOID receipt joins it, +1). Withdrawn claims are not live claims; counting them as coverage gaps misstates what the board rests on — but the scanner must decide this by ITS OWN rules, not by post-hoc edits.

## Mechanism (all changes in spend_annex_scan.py + tests; consumer test_c_neg1.py unchanged)
1. **Attestation sidecars**: `receipts/spend-annex/attestations/*.json` — hand-authored rows, each carrying: target receipt path, target sha256 (PINNED — a changed receipt invalidates its attestation), evidence class `attested`, the evidence pointers (paths/shas/commits verified), attester + date. The generator INGESTS sidecars at scan time, verifies the sha pin, re-runs its own content scan on the target (content-dirty overrides attestation), and emits matching rows as `attested` with citations copied into the annex.
2. **VOID supersession**: a receipt named in a VOID receipt's `supersedes` list (path+sha match) is EXCLUDED from the decisive-claim set, disclosed per-row in an `excluded_superseded` list carrying the VOID pointer. The VOID receipt itself remains IN the set (classified via its own evidence; VOID-family receipts are hand-authored governance text — convention-classifiable + content-scanned).
3. **Idempotence regression test**: generate twice from the same corpus — attested rows and exclusions survive; plus a sha-pin invalidation test (mutate a target, attestation must drop with a named reason).

## Bar
- Content-dirty ALWAYS wins: an attestation cannot cover a receipt whose own content trips the scan (the uiux original stays unresolvable-or-excluded, never attested).
- No special-casing of specific filenames; family rules only.
- Consumer-path verification in the PR: expected end state = the 17 evidence-backed rows attested durably, the uiux pair resolved via supersession semantics, C(-1) count = whatever the rules yield — no target number is pre-committed.

## Provenance rule for annex PRs (gate-side, banked with this issue)
Every annex-bearing PR states the exact generator invocation (command, root, sha of scanner code) and declares any post-processing. A hand-post-processed annex is a different artifact class and must say so in the PR body.
issue_source_snapshot.title: spend_annex_scan: attestation sidecars + VOID-supersession semantics — make evidence-backed coverage durable across regenerations

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
## Summary

Related to #343 (PR #352 fixes the styled-bar half of that defect at the render-pipeline
level). This ticket is the remaining, separate half: raw NUL (0x00) bytes are injected into
the terminal stream by the Windows ConPTY/conhost layer itself, for specific styled-glyph
content, on a real pty — outside this codebase's write path entirely.

## Evidence (three independent, receipted experiments)

All against the same real-pty repro (node-pty on Windows, 190x85, a Homescreen border/rule
composition plus a bottom status-adjacent element — reliably reproduces 408 NUL bytes across
runs) and the issue's own capture rig (`scratch/clirebuild/capture-190x85.mjs`, 976 NUL bytes
across 8 runs at a slightly larger, more complex composition):

1. **Pre-write instrumentation (decisive).** `process.stdout.write` was wrapped inside the
   real pty-hosted child process to check every string passed to it for a literal NUL
   character before it goes anywhere near the pty. Result: 0 NUL bytes seen pre-write across
   repeated runs, while the SAME run's pty-side capture (`p.onData`) showed ~400+ NUL bytes.
   The corruption is added strictly between our `write()` call and the pty's read side.

2. **Chunk-size invariance.** Forcing all writes through small (64-byte) chunks vs. one
   large single write produced an identical NUL count. Rules out "a chunk boundary splits a
   multi-byte UTF-8 sequence" as the mechanism — if that were it, changing where chunk
   boundaries fall should have changed the outcome.

3. **Boot-defer invariance.** Deferring the first paint by 0ms / 500ms / 1500ms after process
   start (letting process startup and stdin raw-mode negotiation fully settle before anything
   is painted) produced an identical NUL count in all three cases (408/408/408). Rules out
   "boot-time write contention/interleaving" as the mechanism.

## Deterministic, content-dependent pattern

The NUL run-length pattern is identical across separate process launches and closely tracks
the border panel's own `rightFill` math (the horizontal-rule fill computed in
`logo-homescreen.ts`'s `paintBorder` title-centering logic) — e.g. one run is exactly 180
NUL bytes, matching a `rightFill=180` computed for a 190-wide border title at that viewport.
This points at long, identically-styled runs of a non-ASCII glyph (the box-drawing `─`,
U+2500, under a truecolor style) as the specific trigger, not a general/random corruption.

## What #352 already fixes (do not re-litigate)

#352 fixed a real, separate, in-code bug: a style-tracking defect that let a prior write's
style (e.g. the prompt cursor's inverse) leak forward onto unrelated content, producing the
`\x1b[1m\x1b[2m\x1b[7m` (bold+dim+inverse) stack the operator originally saw as a solid
grey/inverted bar. After that fix, the NUL bytes described here still occur (unchanged byte
count and run-length pattern), but are now preceded by nothing worse than plain dim — with
no inverse/bold, ConPTY-injected NULs render as unstyled blanks, which is invisible/benign at
the operator's viewport. This ticket is only about the underlying byte-level corruption
itself, which is now believed cosmetically inert but not eliminated.

## Candidate directions (none committed — needs its own investigation)

- Try a different pty backend / library (alternatives to node-pty's ConPTY wrapping on
  Windows) to see if the same content reproduces the same corruption.
- File an upstream report against Microsoft's conhost/ConPTY (or node-pty, if the wrapping
  layer itself is implicated) with the reproduction steps and byte-level evidence above.
- Identify and document an "avoid conditions" workaround (e.g. does breaking up a long
  identically-styled non-ASCII run into shorter styled segments change the outcome? untested
  so far) as a cheaper mitigation if upstream fixes are slow.

## Repro

`scratch/clirebuild/capture-190x85.mjs` (spawns a compiled `ember.exe`, cols=190 rows=85,
captures via `p.onData`, settles 10s) reliably reproduces this against any build, including
one with #352's fix applied.
issue_source_snapshot.title: ConPTY injects NUL bytes into styled non-ASCII glyph runs (Windows console-host layer)

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
## Why (the strongest alternative left standing after the fp32 check)
The fp32 paired re-eval (receipt w1-fp32-check-20260707T114517Z) CONFIRMED the W1 margin on the continuous grid (grow 9.3680 vs control-step-50 9.2452, margin 0.1228 vs bf16's 0.125): the token-match measurement is real, not a bf16 quantization artifact. Per issue #339's pre-registered ladder, the strongest remaining alternative is BILLING SEMANTICS: W1's ratio (819,200 / 12,550,144 = 6.53%) prices the grow arm's CUMULATIVE lineage (9.99M seed + 0.98M pre-grow + 1.57M stabilize). The from-scratch control beating the CUMULATIVE bill may say more about the seed's token-inefficiency than about the grow step. The grow STEP's marginal bill is 2,555,904 tokens (post-seed).

## The discriminating run (pre-registered shape, #339 §alternatives)
Continue the UNWIDENED pre-grow seed checkpoint (v0-seed terminal, step 610 — the exact checkpoint the grow operator widened) with the SAME matched recipe (loader stream, cosine-warmup formula, batch16 seq1024, mtp settings per the W1 terminal receipt's disclosures), NO widening, for up to the grow arm's marginal bill (2,555,904 tokens = 156 steps), evaluating on the SAME certified 16-window batch (sha 91069e33...) at the same cadence, early-stop on eval_loss <= 9.375.

- **Outcome A (matches within the marginal bill):** continued training alone reaches the grow target — the grow step added nothing the tokens didn't; the collapse reading strengthens and shifts to the WHOLE lineage.
- **Outcome B (does not match):** the widening did real work continued training can't do at matched marginal tokens — the collapse reading WEAKENS to 'the cumulative path is token-inefficient' and the grow step retains demonstrated value.
Either way the number lands in the #339 ladder; no verdict language in the receipt (same discipline as W1).

## Mechanics
- Runner: extend scripts/w1_collapse_control_run.py with a resume-from-checkpoint-unwidened mode (no from-scratch init; loads the seed terminal checkpoint; everything else identical — same eval_loss_fn, same receipt schema + provenance pinning, contamination recheck citation per #351's cache design if landed, else full recheck).
- Bill: ~2.56M tokens ≈ 6-7 min of training at the receipted 6665 tok/s + gate overhead. GPU-lease admission preflight mandatory (no llama-server, VRAM headroom assert).
- Receipts: launch receipt with dual preflight, progress JSONL, terminal receipt with the SAME anti-poison lr disclosure, landing PR per the W1 convention.
- Prereg: this issue IS the pre-registration for W1b's reading — outcome semantics above are frozen BEFORE launch; deviations require a disclosed amendment comment BEFORE the receipt is read.
issue_source_snapshot.title: W1b: unwidened-continuation control — the marginal-vs-cumulative billing discriminator (#339 alternative 4)

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
## First occurrence (PR #356 landing, 2026-07-07)
The W1 terminal-receipt writer embeds the raw --shard-dir string. The production corpus lives at an absolute path containing a founder name, so repo-guard (correctly) blocked the landing; the lane had to sanitize 6 receipt files post-generation (paths relativized, shard-dir redacted to external-corpus/shards-v0; no numeric/sha/outcome values touched, re-diff verified — disclosed in the PR).

## Why source-level cure
Post-generation sanitization is a per-landing manual step that will silently recur on EVERY future terminal receipt from this launcher (W1b #355, W2 G-arm #113 inherit the same writer), and editing receipt files after the instrument writes them — however carefully — is a pattern the receipts discipline should not normalize.

## Cure
The receipt writer references the corpus by (a) repo-relative paths for anything under the repo, and (b) a name-safe logical identifier + manifest sha for external corpora (e.g. corpus_id: shards-v0, corpus_manifest_sha256: <sha>) instead of the raw filesystem path. The sha keeps provenance binding STRONGER than the path string did (paths don't pin content; shas do). Regression: a unit test greps a generated receipt for absolute-path patterns + the repo-guard denylist before any landing.
issue_source_snapshot.title: W1/W2 runner: receipt writer embeds raw --shard-dir absolute path (founder-named) — repo-guard blocks every future landing

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
## Problem (jun-sim tick 20, 2026-07-07)

Tonight's cockpit chain — deliberate teardown, relaunch contract, CreateProcess corpse visible on the operator's screen for ~27 minutes, cured relaunch — was entirely hand-coordinated lane work. There is NO standing mechanism that keeps the body's liveness true. P-C says the body 'never lags the organism' and is 'the operator's audit channel on every other claim'; a corpse error pane occupying the cockpit's screen slot for half an hour is the named failure state, and it was caught by a coordinator poke, not by a loop.

## Spec floor
A watchdog probe, cadence ~2-5 min, that asserts the COMPOSED liveness predicate:
1. window exists with the ledgered title/HWND (UIA/enumeration tier, not process listing — wt is single-process-multi-window),
2. backing ember.exe process alive and parented to that window,
3. renderer heartbeat (the activity-event transport from #309 gives a cheap pulse; a frame counter or event timestamp newer than N s),
4. model residency consistent with declared mode (VRAM tenant present in inference mode, ABSENT during a GPU-lease training leg — the watchdog must be lease-aware and treat 'cockpit deliberately down' as a healthy state when the lease ledger says so).

## Policy on failure
- corpse/wrong-state detected -> capture (PrintWindow) + classify (error pane vs hung vs missing) -> receipt row.
- Restore policy is CONFIGURABLE and defaults to REPORT-ONLY escalating to auto-restore only for the unambiguous cases (no window + no process + no lease = relaunch with the known-good command shape). NEVER auto-relaunch during a training lease; never kill anything (clean-exit only, receipts-first).
- Every detection and action is a receipt (JSONL), and the board's body-pillar conditions may consume them.

## Constraints
- Launch command shape is receipted: single-token --title, direct wt invocation (PS5.1 Start-Process array marshaling mangles multi-word titles - 2026-07-07 corpse receipt).
- Kill-discipline and window-hygiene rules bind: PID-cohort verified, ledger rows updated in place, WM-close-class primitives only from an agent context.
- The watchdog itself must be visible in the ledger (a headless loop that dies silently recreates the problem one level up).
issue_source_snapshot.title: Cockpit liveness watchdog: standing loop for the body's up/corpse/wrong-state detection

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
## Context

#362 (cockpit liveness watchdog v1) shipped legs 1 (window, UIA enumeration),
2 (backing process, parented-to-window match), and 4 (VRAM residency vs the
`state/gpu-lease.json` convention). Leg 3 (renderer heartbeat) was deferred
with disclosure per the frozen spec addendum on #362 -- this issue names the
exact surface the watchdog needs from ember-cli to close that gap.

## Problem

Without a renderer-alive pulse, a genuinely **hung** cockpit (window exists,
backing process alive, but the UI is frozen) is indistinguishable from
healthy in the current composed predicate -- `classify()` in
`scripts/cockpit_watchdog.py` folds that case into `"healthy"` because legs
1 and 2 both pass. This is the disclosed v1 limitation, not a bug.

Checked: #309 (activity event transport) shipped the emit/render *transport*
only -- `scripts/lib/activity_log.py::emit()` is not currently called from
anywhere in the live TypeScript app (only Python board-runner code and tests
call it); wiring emitters into the actual running CLI was explicitly out of
scope for #309's increment 1 ("CLI integration/display" listed under "Out of
scope (increment 2)"). So there is no live render-alive pulse today.

## Concrete ask

`tools/ember-cli/src/entrypoints/process-entry.ts::main()` (delegated to
from `entrypoints/main.ts::boot()`) -- or wherever the actual render/tick
loop of the running app lives -- needs to stamp a lightweight, dedicated
liveness pulse on a fixed cadence (~2-5s, matching the watchdog's own cycle
band), independent of user activity or new activity-log events.

Two candidate mechanisms (either is acceptable; pick whichever is cheaper to
wire correctly):

1. **Reuse the #309 transport**: emit a `kind="status"`,
   `actor="ember-cli-renderer"` event on a timer inside the render loop.
   Reuses existing infra, but is a TS component calling into a Python-shaped
   convention -- worth checking the wiring cost (TS port of `emit()`, or a
   thin shell-out).
2. **Dedicated minimal heartbeat file** (lower surface, no cross-language
   call): e.g. `state/ember-cli-render-heartbeat.jsonl`, one line
   `{"ts": "<live ISO8601Z>"}` appended (or the file's mtime touched) once
   per render tick, written directly from the TS render loop.

## Leg 3's consumption contract (frozen once the surface exists)

The watchdog reads the file's mtime (or last JSONL row's `ts`) and asserts
`now - last_pulse < N seconds`, where `N` is configurable and matched to the
chosen cadence. This becomes leg 3 in `cockpit_watchdog.py`'s composed
predicate; `classify()`'s `"healthy"` state then splits into `"healthy"` and
`"hung"` once the pulse is available.

## Out of scope here

Legs 1/2/4 themselves (done, see #362) -- this issue is scoped to exposing
the renderer-alive pulse surface from ember-cli only.
issue_source_snapshot.title: Cockpit watchdog leg 3: renderer-alive heartbeat pulse needed from ember-cli

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
jun-sim tick 21 (2026-07-07). During a GPU-lease training leg the cockpit is deliberately down — and the operator's left half is simply EMPTY. Broken and working look identical from the chair; the explanation lives in a briefing file he would have to open. The visible-living-system bar (P-C) fails exactly here.

Spec sketch: when a lease teardown begins, paint a minimal placeholder in the cockpit's slot — a tiny always-on-top text pane or console banner: 'EMBER — GPU leased to <purpose> since <t>, cockpit returns ~<expected_end> (receipts: <path>)'. It reads state/gpu-lease.json (the #362 convention) and closes itself on cockpit relaunch. Constraints: ledgered like any visible window (window-ledger row), single-token wt title if wt-hosted, zero GPU/VRAM use, never a live terminal that only exists to be screenshotted — a static banner is the point, its PURPOSE is to be looked at. The teardown/relaunch choreography (tonight's W1b window is the template) gains one paint + one close step.
issue_source_snapshot.title: Lease-window placeholder: the cockpit's screen slot must say WHY it is empty

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
Operator probe 2026-07-07: the GPU sits near-idle (~2%) for ~25 minutes of CPU recheck to gate a ~7-minute training leg — a 3.5:1 gate-to-work inversion. The #359 cache only kills REPEAT rechecks (same batch+receipt+code triple); every new triple pays the full scan again. The corpus itself changes ~never.

Cures, in preference order (receipts to decide):
1. **Persistent corpus window-hash index**: build the n-gram/window hash structure over shards-v0 ONCE, sha-pin it to the corpus manifest (combined_sha256), store beside the shards; every recheck loads the index (seconds) instead of rescanning 6.98B windows. Invalidate on corpus sha change. This converts EVERY future recheck — any batch, any code version — to seconds. Est. index size and build cost to be measured first (one lane, one receipt).
2. **Overlap, not just speed**: recheck runs on CPU while the GPU leg's model load + optimizer init + checkpoint load proceed concurrently, with the train loop blocked on the recheck verdict (fail-closed: refusal tears down before the first step). Cheap to implement, saves minutes even with cure 1.
3. (Rejected unless 1 fails) GPU-accelerating the scan itself — more code for less win than a persistent index.

Constraints: fail-closed semantics unchanged (index-missing or sha-mismatch → full scan, disclosed in receipt); the receipt must state which path ran (index-hit / full-scan / cache-hit) — a silent fast path is indistinguishable from a skipped check; L2 receipts-only.

Origin: tonight's W1b window — two launch attempts, both spending their wall-clock in CPU recheck while the GPU idled; the operator caught the shape from the chair.
issue_source_snapshot.title: Contamination recheck must not cost 25 CPU-minutes per launch: persistent corpus n-gram index + GPU overlap

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
Research tick 13 cross-examination finding (2026-07-07): tonight's W1b launch refusal — W1_LIVE_CONTAMINATION_REFUSED, confirmed_non_self_matches=53554 (self_matches_excluded=16257 of 69811 raw) — exists ONLY as a line in a scratchpad launch log. No receipt artifact anywhere under receipts/ or scratch receipts. Every downstream use of those numbers is UNVERIFIED by our own standard; a gate that refuses without a receipt makes its own honesty un-auditable (L2).

Spec floor:
1. On refusal, the runner writes a refusal receipt (same out-dir rules as #364: dry-run/refused receipts go to scratch/w1-control/receipts/, never the canonical tree) carrying: the full match counts, the candidate-window derivation MODE (decontam-receipt-indices vs contiguous-default — tonight's root cause was exactly this mode being wrong silently), the first N matches with shard+offset, batch identity (sha if derivable), and the resolved args.
2. **Direction structure** (cross-exam's promoted demand): the receipt must let an auditor judge whether the refusal was CONSERVATIVE (refusing a run that should not proceed) or a false block — i.e. it records what the self-exclusion excluded and why the remainder counts as non-self.
3. The candidate-window derivation mode belongs in EVERY receipt (accepted runs too) — tonight a silent fallback to the naive contiguous mode produced an uninterpretable-if-passed run; the mode line makes that impossible to miss.
4. Fail-closed unchanged; this is disclosure-only.

Origin: the missing --decontam-receipt incident (root-caused by the launch lane, code refs w1_collapse_control_run.py:2264-2317) + the tick-13 panel treating the refusal numbers as brief-relayed/UNVERIFIED because no artifact carries them.
issue_source_snapshot.title: Contamination-gate refusals must write receipts: refusal evidence currently exists only in launch logs

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
Pre-registration, frozen BEFORE any batch is built or eval run. This is #339 §3 row 1 — the mandatory park gate (#339 §4.1: 'a bare token-match without the statistical confirmation licenses NO park') — extended to also generalize W1b's finding (#355 result + fp32 addendum).

## Design
1. **Batches:** K=10 fresh certified 16-window batches from the clean held-out stratum. Each batch: disjoint from the training front (window index > max training index at ceiling, re-derived per batch), disjoint from every other batch in the set, disjoint from the original certified batch (sha 91069e33…8929). Each passes the SAME certification as w2-heldout-decontam-20260707T055843Z: full-corpus contamination recheck with self-location exclusion, 16/16 clean windows, deterministic re-derivation inside the receipt.
2. **Evals:** paired fp32 (and bf16, disclosed) eval of THREE checkpoints on every batch: seed step-610 (cbase-v0, model.pt sha 1ec99451…), grown terminal step-766 (model.pt sha 58e8e989…), from-scratch control step-50 (reconstructed per the bit-exact replay protocol of w1-fp32-check). Forward-only; minutes of GPU total.
3. **Statistics:** per-batch margins M1 = grown − control, M2 = seed − grown. Bootstrap 95% CI (10k resamples) on each margin's mean across the K batches.

## Frozen outcome semantics
- **Q1 (the park gate):** M1 CI entirely > 0 (control strictly below grown across batches) → W1's collapse measurement is CONFIRMED multi-batch; the §4.1 gate is SATISFIED (park becomes operator-available, never automatic — L7). M1 CI containing 0 → W1's margin is single-batch-unconfirmed; no park; the W1 claim drops to 'single-batch measurement' wherever it appears.
- **Q2 (W1b generalization):** M2 CI entirely > 0 → the grow segment's small fp32 gain generalizes. M2 CI containing 0 or < 0 → the 0.036 single-batch gain is noise-level; the bf16-bounded 'zero grid points' reading gains multi-batch support.
- No other claims move on this receipt. Single-seed caveat remains regardless (seeds=1 everywhere).

## Kill criteria (stated now)
- Certification cannot produce K=10 clean batches → report achieved K with per-batch receipts; K in [5,9] = run with disclosed reduced power; K < 5 = the gate CANNOT run as registered — stop, receipt, operator decides (no silent redesign).
- Any batch failing sha-pinned re-derivation at eval time voids that batch only, disclosed.

## Price (disclosed)
- Certification: the recheck cache (#359) keys on batch sha, so each NEW batch pays a full ~25-min CPU scan → ~4h CPU for K=10 UNLESS the builder amortizes one persistent corpus window-hash index across all K (exactly #370 cure 1 — this prereg is its first paying customer). Either path is receipted; the index, if built, is sha-pinned to the corpus manifest.
- Eval: 3 checkpoints × 10 batches, forward-only fp32 — minutes of GPU inside one lease window.

## Provenance interlocks
Every receipt carries: corpus combined_sha256 (aa48f6ee…), per-batch sha + decontam receipt path, checkpoint model.pt shas as above, candidate-window derivation MODE (per #371's disclosure floor), and the classifier code sha.
issue_source_snapshot.title: W1c prereg (FROZEN): K>=10 fresh-batch paired fp32 CI — the #339 §4.1 mandatory gate

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
## What

During the W1b landing (PR #373), the terminal receipt for the corrected
live run (receipts/ember-c-scale/w1-collapse-control-20260707T135344Z.json)
was found to verify the GROW arm's checkpoint (sha256 against the rung
receipt/manifest) but never verify the LOADED CONTINUATION checkpoint
(the seed-610 source `load_continuation_checkpoint()` reads from) against
its own manifest's sha256.

This landing's continuation-source sha match (model.pt) was confirmed by
hand, out-of-band, rather than by the receipt itself:

    manifest sha256 (models/cbase-smoke-run/checkpoints/step-00000610/manifest.json)
    == actual model.pt sha256 on disk

## Why this matters

`load_continuation_checkpoint()` (scripts/w1_collapse_control_run.py) already
does a structural verification (`verify_checkpoint_key_shape_parity` +
`load_checkpoint()`'s own internal sha re-verify against ITS OWN manifest),
so the checkpoint that gets loaded IS the one its manifest claims. What is
missing is a receipted, first-class field asserting that identity in the
terminal receipt itself -- currently a reader must independently locate the
continuation checkpoint's manifest and diff shas by hand to get the same
assurance the grow arm already gets for free.

## Proposed fix

Add a `continuation_source_verification` block to the terminal receipt,
populated at the same point `load_continuation_checkpoint()` runs, mirroring
the shape of the existing rung/grow-arm verification block:

```json
"continuation_source_verification": {
  "checkpoint_dir": "<continuation checkpoint_dir>",
  "manifest_sha256": "<from manifest.json>",
  "on_disk_model_pt_sha256": "<re-hashed at receipt-write time>",
  "match": true
}
```

Scope: receipt-shape change only, additive field, no change to load/refuse
semantics (the existing checks already fail closed on a real mismatch --
this only makes the match auditable from the receipt alone, without a
manual out-of-band check).
issue_source_snapshot.title: W1b runner: continuation-source sha-verification block missing from receipt

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
Two independent discoveries today (2026-07-07):
1. receipts/v0-live-20260623T105829Z.json — the seed segment's only run receipt, cited by every W1/W1b bill row — missing from canonical receipts/; survived ONLY in a seed-export staging copy; restored via PR #373.
2. receipts/c9-cadence/ — the ENTIRE directory, including code-vs-docs-20260702T180521Z.json (the C9 witness that July 4-5 boards cite verbatim as AUDIT-OK) — gone; the fresh board (152259Z) honestly reports the class empty and C9 lost its witness. Three byte-identical copies survived in an older session's sandbox fixture trees; content verified against the board's own quoted values (code_fraction 0.3113 exact match); restoration queued (annexcure lane, one PR, WITH spend-annex sidecars for both since both predate the annex convention — the v0-live restoration without a sidecar is exactly what flipped C(-1) RED today).

Neither file was ever git-tracked (no git history exists) — they vanished via filesystem operations invisible to git; the deleting op is unidentified and likely unidentifiable. The CLASS FIX, not the whodunit:
- **Rule: any receipt CITED by a board receipt, bill row, or other receipt MUST be git-tracked.** Untracked = one filesystem op from silent loss, and it has now happened twice.
- **Probe: cited-path custody check** — walk the newest board receipt + every verdict-bearing receipt's internal citations; every cited receipts/ path must (a) exist and (b) be tracked. Missing/untracked = RED row (or a C(-1)-style disclosed exclusion), because a claim whose witness can silently vanish is a claim without a witness.
- Backstop: sandbox/fixture seeding (which is what accidentally saved c9-cadence) is luck, not custody.
issue_source_snapshot.title: Custody class: UNTRACKED cited receipts vanished from receipts/ twice (v0-live, c9-cadence) — cited receipts must be tracked + probed

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
Mechanism gap (jun-sim tick, 2026-07-07): the custody rule (#378) is prose in an issue; the only thing that catches violations today is C(-1)'s annex accounting — indirect, and only for spend coverage. The morning arc left 13 receipts untracked in canonical (board 162255Z) AFTER the rule was filed: a rule without a standing loop is not a mechanism.

Spec floor (builder-dispatchable):
- New board CHK (or extension of the receipts-custody surface): every board run enumerates receipts/ recursively and fails the row RED for (a) any file untracked in git (git ls-files check), (b) any file that fails json.load (utf-8 then utf-8-sig; the truncated Class-A pair in #378 are the live instances), (c) any receipts/ path cited inside a verdict-bearing receipt or board receipt that does not exist on disk (the vanished-witness class — v0-live and c9-cadence were the live instances).
- Disclosed allowlist for intentionally-uncommitted staging (if any lane needs one, it names it in the receipt; silent untracked = RED).
- The CHK's own receipt names every offender path — the cure lane's worklist is the receipt, zero forensics needed next time.
- Probe-verify: synthetic fixtures for all three failure shapes + a clean pass, in scripts/tests/.

Prior instances receipted in #378 (2 vanished, 2 truncated, 3 BOM'd, 13 untracked). This CHK converts the class from forensic archaeology to a standing gate.
issue_source_snapshot.title: Custody probe as a board CHK: untracked-in-canonical + unparseable + cited-path-missing fail LOUD every board run

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
## Defect class (found 2026-07-07 during custody forensics)

The board's disconfirmation evaluation writes timestamped run receipts (receipt_type: disconfirmation_evaluation, ticket EMBER-TOTALITY-DISCONFIRMATION) into canonical `receipts/` as untracked files — two appeared during a single board run window (receipts/disconfirmation-eval-20260707T173924Z.json, ...174158Z.json).

This is the exact class #377 named and #383 cured for the C-INV probe: board machinery producing fresh untracked files inside canonical receipts/ on every run, which the C-CUSTODY condition (#381/#382) now correctly flags as custody violations. The two conditions fight forever unless run receipts move.

## Cure (mirror #383 exactly)
- Disconfirmation run receipts write to `scripts/ember_totality/receipts-disconfirmation/` (outside canonical; the same pattern as receipts-c-invariant/ and receipts-totality/).
- Any consumer reading newest-by-timestamp updates its path.
- Two-run test: no new untracked files under receipts/ after consecutive board runs; two distinct timestamped receipts in the new location.
- Sweep while there: grep the board suite for ANY other writer targeting canonical receipts/ at run time (the class likely has more members — enumerate them in the PR body, cure all found).

## Existing strays
The two receipts above stay on disk as evidence until this lands; the cure PR's body should name them so the custody row's count change is attributable.
issue_source_snapshot.title: Board disconfirmation probe writes untracked run receipts into canonical receipts/ (same class as #377)

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
## Defect (board 183856Z, 2026-07-07)

C(-1) flipped RED(13/274 unannexed decisive receipts) -> GREEN between receipts 173556Z and 183856Z with NO cure landing. The cause: the 13 offending receipts were DELETED from the working tree between the runs (a lane's branch-exit checkout removed them — custody incident, salvage PR #393 in flight). The C(-1) scanner passes because its evidence SET emptied, not because coverage was achieved.

Meanwhile C-CUSTODY (same receipt) correctly reports cited_missing=10 for those very files — the board simultaneously says 'spend-proof complete' (C(-1) GREEN) and 'the receipts that proof depends on are missing' (C-CUSTODY RED). A condition whose GREEN can be MANUFACTURED BY DELETING EVIDENCE is a theater hole: a future all-green claim could ride a deletion.

## Cure
C(-1) must fail-closed on absent-but-referenced evidence: the scanner's decisive-receipt universe = receipts present on disk UNION receipts cited by any tracked artifact (annex rows, attestations, board history). A cited-but-missing decisive receipt counts as UNPROVEN (RED contribution), mirroring C-CUSTODY's cited_missing semantics. Regression fixture: delete a fixture decisive receipt that an annex row cites -> C(-1) must stay RED with a missing-evidence message, not flip GREEN.

## Ordering note
#393 (salvage) restores the 13 tracked+annexed and should make C(-1) HONESTLY green; this issue is about the scanner's counterfactual behavior, which stays wrong even after #393 lands.
issue_source_snapshot.title: C(-1) scanner passes vacuously when cited decisive receipts are DELETED from disk (deletion-induced GREEN, board 183856Z)

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone

The #396 PR's sweep claim ('no other board-time writers to canonical receipts/ root') was false — these two probe families write at board time, same class as the disconfirmation writer cured in #396 (and #377 before it).

Also in scope (custody stragglers found in the same enumeration):
- Pre-cure disconfirmation-eval receipts from earlier runs today (1739xxZ, 1741xxZ, 1849xxZ) + their milestone-reconciliation/publication-gate siblings — need tracking (same treatment as the 13 in the C(-1) annex landing).
- Six receipts/ember-m10-surface3/**/fib.py scratch artifacts from 2026-06-28 — code files inside receipt bundles, untracked since June; disposition = track them (they are part of their bundles' evidence).

Acceptance: (1) both writers redirected to scripts/ember_totality/ side (receipts-milestone/, receipts-publication/ mirroring the #396 pattern) with consumers updated; (2) a consecutive-runs test proving no new untracked files appear under canonical receipts/ after a board run (extend the existing two-run custody test to assert on the WHOLE canonical tree, not one family); (3) stragglers tracked via the PR; (4) C-CUSTODY untracked count drops to 0 on the next board run.
issue_source_snapshot.title: Board-time writers to canonical receipts/ round 2: milestone-reconciliation + publication-gate (the #387 sweep missed them)

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
Found during the C-BASE clause (d) dry-run rerun (PR #402 diagnosis lane).

**Defect:** `cbase_grow_live._function_preservation_check()` crashes with SIGSEGV (exit 139) deterministically when exercised at real rung-2 scale: the pre-grow (~1.19B param) and post-grow (~2.2B param) models are held resident simultaneously, uncollected, during the check. The helper was never previously exercised at this scale.

**Evidence (from the diagnosis lane, reproducible):**
- 6+ isolated hand-bisected repros; deterministic 2/2 crashes on the full script
- Fix confirmed 3/3 clean: release the pre-grow model before building the post-grow model
- The dry-run PR carries a local low-memory variant (same math, same imports of build_model/widen_state_dict, same PASS_TOL) with a module docstring explaining the divergence — the shared helper itself is intentionally unedited pending this issue
- Measured on the fixed path: fp_diff 5.72e-06 vs tolerance 1e-4 (PASS; rung-1 precedent 2.38e-6)

**Acceptance:**
1. The shared helper releases the pre-grow model (or otherwise bounds peak residency) before building the post-grow model; the fix must keep the check's math identical (same tolerance, same comparison set).
2. A regression test at a scale that reproduces the original crash shape (can be a reduced-but-representative residency test if full rung-2 scale is impractical in CI), named with the *_test.py suffix convention.
3. The dry-run's local variant is then retired in favor of the fixed shared helper (follow-up PR may do this).
4. PR stop-at-open; no close-keywords adjacent to issue numbers in title or commit headlines.

Repro script path: will be cited from the PR #402 branch once the diagnosis lane pushes (its report includes the isolated-repro script).

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
Found during the build-1059671 swap census: the operator's cockpit pane had been a CORPSE for up to ~11h — the cockpit binary had exited, only the `cmd /k` wrapper kept the pane open, and the last-rendered frame (board summary included) sat frozen at the operator's screen position looking exactly like a live cockpit. Nothing detected it: the board kept updating on disk, the receipts stayed fresh, and every green condition was invisible at the only surface that matters (P-C: the body IS the audit channel — a dead body showing a fresh-looking frame is a fabricated receipt in visual form, per the constitution's own words).

The staleness badge (#392/#404) does not cure this class: a dead process freezes the badge too — a frozen 'board: 2m ago' looks fresh forever.

**Acceptance (two halves):**
1. IN-APP: the cockpit renders a visible liveness signal that decays WITHOUT re-render — the cheapest honest form is a wall-clock (HH:MM:SS, ticking every render cycle) in the header/status line: a frozen clock is visible death at one glance. A heartbeat FILE (cockpit writes ts+pid every cycle, e.g. state/cockpit-heartbeat.json) accompanies it so machine checks don't need pixels.\n2. EXTERNAL: a standing check (census tooling) compares pane-existence vs process-liveness vs heartbeat age and flags PANE-WITHOUT-PROCESS and HEARTBEAT-STALE as loud defects.

Rails: *_test.py suffix fixtures, PR stop-at-open, no close-keywords near issue numbers anywhere.
issue_source_snapshot.title: Cockpit process death is invisible: frozen pixels pass for a live body (liveness gap)

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
Twice on 2026-07-08 (06:33Z and ~06:5xZ, two different lanes) the same trap fired: a lane hits repo-guard's <type>/<slug> branch-name check on a PRE-EXISTING non-conforming branch, reaches for the GitHub branch-rename API, and the rename DELETES the old ref and AUTO-CLOSES the open PR instead of migrating it (headRefName never changes). Both lanes recovered (recreate ref at same sha + gh pr reopen), but the recovery is manual and the trap is silent.

**Cures, either/both:** (1) repo-guard exempts branches that already have an open PR (check is advisory for pre-existing branches, binding for new ones); (2) document in GOVERNANCE.md: never rename a branch with an open PR via the raw API — commit in detached HEAD (repo-guard allowlists HEAD) and push to the existing ref, as finisher lanes now do. Note: master has no GitHub branch protection, so the CI branch-name failure is cosmetic today — if that changes, this becomes a hard wall. PR stop-at-open, no close-keywords.
issue_source_snapshot.title: repo-guard branch-name check + GitHub rename API footgun: renaming a branch with an open PR auto-closes the PR (2 occurrences 2026-07-08)

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
## Corpus defect: late-region massive near-duplication in shards-v0 (two independent receipts) — repair-vs-certify decision tree

**Evidence (both landed 2026-07-08, independent lanes, independent instruments):**
1. **Shard-19 concentration** (`w1c-knee-sweep-20260708T112944Z.json`, histogram run): the fwd_1m pool's 16 needle windows match ~1,044 corpus positions EACH (per-row counts dead flat, 1013–1083) and **100% of all 16,472 matches lie in one shard, v0-00019.bin** — zero in the other 25. The needle positions themselves sit inside shard 19's window range: the shard contains ≥89-token spans repeated ~1,044×.
2. **Tail zero-clean** (P1 decontam builder run, exit log banked by the sweep lane): in default tail-mode (held_out_window_start 6,814,292 ≈ shard v0-00025.bin), **0 of 192 candidate windows were clean at W=13** across 6 rounds — every candidate's windows appear elsewhere in the corpus. (The banked W1 control batch at pool-start 2^22 ≈ shard 16 found 16/16 clean in round 1 — that region is fine.)

**What survives:** the W1 control receipt (its 16 windows verified clean under the strict any-match convention — internal corpus repetition does not invalidate a clean-region batch). **What is now suspect:** (a) effective corpus size — if whole shards are near-duplicate content, every capability-per-token and per-corpus-pass claim carries an inflated denominator; (b) the 10/10 DIRTY region verdicts from the W1c scout (`w1c-scout-master-20260708T080858Z.json`) — those scans predate per-shard histograms; their match masses (10.8M mid_corpus, 53.6M back_1m) may ALSO concentrate in the duplicated shard set, in which case the "corpus-wide contamination" read collapses into a small excisable shard set.

**In flight:** decode probe (prose-duplication vs degenerate-filler at matched positions in shard 19 + a shard-25 tail sample) + shard-19 internal structure (contiguous vs scattered), assigned to the scan lane.

**Decision tree (pre-registered now, before the probe lands):**
- Decode = degenerate filler (whitespace/format blocks) → corpus-assembly defect; cure = **dedup/excise → shards-v1 manifest** with a receipted diff (window counts before/after, sha chain), then re-run the 10-region scout against v1 with per-shard histograms; K-batch certification returns as plain binary absence against v1.
- Decode = real prose repeated ~1,044× → document-duplication defect; same cure path but the dedup is document-level (harder); interim: certification predicate = absence outside the quarantined shard set (already receipted clean for fwd_1m at W=13).
- Per-shard histogram re-run on 2–3 heavy regions (mid_corpus, back_1m, back_50k) decides whether the scout's DIRTY verdicts are shard-concentrated: ≥90% of matches in ≤3 shards → excision certifies everything; diffuse → true corpus-wide duplication and the frequency-accounting predicate (#374 thread) returns from the archive.

**Constraint carried:** corpus manifest sha (aa48f6ee…) is pinned by existing receipts — v0 is never edited in place; any repair lands as a NEW manifest (shards-v1) with lineage, and existing receipts keep citing v0 truthfully.

Refs: #372 (scan harness arc), #374 (cert re-spec thread — frequency framing now conditionally superseded), #118 (P1 sweep — tail finding source), #435 (decontam regen).
issue_source_snapshot.title: Corpus defect: massive late-region near-duplication in shards-v0 (shard-19 x1044 concentration + tail zero-clean) — repair-vs-certify decision tree

Third instance today (2026-07-08) of the same class: a call site reaches for w1_collapse_control_run.py's RAW serial contamination_recheck and dies on a contiguous-alloc failure, while build_decontam_batch_mp.py's adaptive-chunked, MemoryError-splitting wrapper sits proven one module over.

Instances: (1) the pre-fix W1c scan worker (cured by chunking, then superseded by #302's adaptive path); (2) p1_envelope_sweep.py:440 calling w1c.contamination_recheck directly — killed P1 point 3 at the FINAL recheck with numpy ArrayMemoryError (2GiB contiguous, 268M-element uint64) after the corpus+model already occupied RAM (traceback banked in the P1 lane; cure = swap to the wrapper, ruled + in flight); (3) the EQUIV harness's n_workers default silently resolving to the serial path on low-core boxes (flagged in PR #443's body).

Cure direction (one of, maintainer's pick at implementation): (a) make the adaptive wrapper the module-level default export and rename the raw serial function to _contamination_recheck_serial_unsafe (grep + fix the 4 known call sites), or (b) add the adaptive-split guard INTO the serial function itself so there is no unsafe entry point at all. Option (b) is stronger — no future call site can pick wrong. Regression bar: the like-for-like equivalence receipts already exist (16,472 exact reproduction through the chunked path, PR #443 body; contamination=0 agreement on the regen batch).

Refs: #440 (corpus work that surfaced the class), #443 (footgun flag), #118 (P1 sweep, instance 2).

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
Pre-registered BEFORE any rung-2 grow executes (rung-2 machinery in flight on #429; this freeze must precede the real grow event or the result is post-hoc). Supersedes the retracted #327 interpretation (see the correction comment there); derivations panel-verified (2 independent seats + arithmetic-verify leg with code-read receipts).

## The observable
d_comm per #327's definition, measured with the #448 decomposition fields (step_rms_post, pushforward_step_rms, cos_alignment) — MANDATORY; a rung-2 d_comm without the fields does not test this prereg.

## Frozen inputs (derivation chain in the tick-18 note)
- q is exact and distribution-independent per class: q_gate = q_up = 1; q_down = 0.5 under exact duplication. Under the #280 antisymmetric-perturbation operator, q_down acquires an O(eps) correction (parameterization arrives with the #280 implementation PR); q_gate/up unchanged. Every receipt pins the operator version.
- r by LR convention, dimension-invariant across a strict doubling (max dim doubles; 16384>1024 holds at rung-2): flat-LR r = 1/sqrt(2) all classes; repo scale-convention (scale=max(1,m/n)^0.5, code-confirmed in run_p5_audit.py:1899-1932) r_gate/up = 1.0, r_down = 1/sqrt(2).
- OPEN INPUT to pin before measurement: which convention the PRODUCTION training loop's Muon applies (the audit harness uses the scale convention; the production loop must be code-read and quoted — builder item below).

## Predictions (gate-only, comparable to rung-1; per-class values in the tick-18 note)
Under the scale convention, gate-only independence null = sqrt(2) = 1.41421. Rung-1 measured 1.13526 implies c = +0.356 (flat-LR: null sqrt(1.5)=1.22474, c = +0.149).

Bands, frozen now:
- (i) ALIGNMENT REPRODUCES: rung-2 gate-only c in [0.25, 0.45] (scale convention, decomposed via #448 fields) — partial commutation is real, stable, and function-preservation-predicted; the law becomes d_comm(geometry, c) with c the physics term. Claim-ladder: promote to L2-candidate (measured cross-rung regularity).
- (ii) ALIGNMENT VANISHES: |c| < 0.05 — rung-1's c was a reconstruction artifact (its pre-grow checkpoint was inverse-net2net-derived, no optimizer state); the independence null stands for genuine snapshots. Claim: measurement-hygiene finding, D4.
- (iii) OTHERWISE — attribution via the decomposed r vs q vs c (which input broke names the follow-up; no post-hoc band invention).

## Measurement conditions (all mandatory)
1. GENUINE pre-grow snapshot saved WITH optimizer state immediately before the rung-2 grow (rung-1's reconstruction confound must not recur — this is actionable now because rung-2 has not grown).
2. Layer 0, gate_proj primary (rung-1 comparability) + per-class breakout (gate/up/down separately — down carries the only q≠1 term and is the sharpest semantics check).
3. #448 fields emitted; optimizer-state provenance recorded; operator version/sha pinned; LR convention of the applied update quoted from the code that ran.
4. Measurement occurs before any post-grow training beyond the rung-1 protocol.

## Decision clause (what this changes)
If band (i): momentum TRANSPLANT (pushforward optimizer state through the widen map) is predicted to beat momentum reset on post-grow loss-spike recovery; rung-3's grow procedure adopts whichever a paired A/B receipt supports. If band (ii): reset stands, no transplant machinery is built. The observable buys a procedure decision, not bookkeeping.

## Builder items (queued)
- Pin the production Muon LR convention (code-read + quote; NOT the audit harness).
- Low-rank-matched MC null (EXP-C1b spectra) — secondary to c-attribution.
- Full-text novelty pass over the adjacent literature (2605.15435, 2605.13405, 2604.04281, 2406.02469, 2305.02869) before any public claim beyond this repo.

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
Measured receipt (Win32_OperatingSystem + Win32_PageFileUsage, 15:3xZ): physical 63.6GB; pagefile fixed-init 16GB (max 32GB), peak usage today 13.4/16GB; commit limit 79.6GB; commit USED 60.6GB while physical-in-use was only ~31GB; commit AVAILABLE 19.0GB at the same instant 'free physical' read 31GB.

**Unified mechanism for the day's entire crash record:**
- Clean ArrayMemoryErrors (13GB corpus concat at two free-RAM levels; 2GiB recheck; 512MiB per-shard read at '28.7GB free') = allocators that check commit charge upfront and fail honestly. Free-physical was never the binding metric; commit-available was.
- Native crashes (widen ACCESS_VIOLATION x3 under the contended window; clone() SIGSEGV at cpu_offload_adamw.py:106 on the first-ever offloaded opt.step()) = reserve-then-commit-on-touch paths: reservation succeeds, first touch cannot be committed, access violation instead of a clean exception. CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 + healthy post-crash GPU/RAM on the clone crash rule out async-CUDA and leak mechanisms.
- The quiet-window widen success (the #446 discriminator) = lower commit charge, exactly as this mechanism predicts. #446's machine-state closure stands; this issue names the machine state precisely.
- Why the memmap cures worked: file-backed pages charge NO commit. The 'every bulk read becomes memmap' posture (#455) was the right cure adopted under a wrong label (fragmentation).
- The clone() trigger quantified: first opt.step() of the offloaded 2.2B config initializes ~26GB of fresh CPU-side state (fp32 shadow + exp_avg + exp_avg_sq) against a 19GB commit-available ceiling.

**Cures (engineering-first, no system-settings dependency):**
1. cpu_offload_adamw.py: optimizer state becomes FILE-BACKED (np.memmap-backed torch tensors, mode r+, sha-keyed under scratch/) — eliminates the commit ask AND makes optimizer state checkpointable (feeds the rung-3 momentum-transplant decision on the d_comm prereg). Lane on it.
2. Commit-aware preflight everywhere a launch gate exists: assert commit_available > planned_new_commit + margin; receipt carries BOTH commit-available and free-physical. Free-physical alone is banned as a launch gate (the governor's current ram.free_ram_gib check reads the wrong counter for this class).
3. Optional box-level lever, operator-owned, NOT blocking either cure: the 16GB fixed-init pagefile is undersized for a 63.6GB heavy-commit ML box; system-managed or larger init would raise the ceiling. The engineering cures above stand alone without it.

Acceptance: (a) file-backed optimizer state lands with a test proving zero large commit delta across opt.step() first execution; (b) probe + governor preflights print commit numbers; (c) one full instrumented probe step completes at rung-2 scale (the #429 merge-bar receipt). refs #429 #446 #455
issue_source_snapshot.title: Commit-exhaustion crash class: Windows commit limit (16GB fixed-init pagefile) unifies all 2026-07-08 native crashes + clean MemoryErrors; cures = file-backed optimizer state + commit-aware preflights

Today's receipts: the cockpit died 4x (commit exhaustion, root-caused and cured via the #457-class work) and the model server was stopped/relaunched 4x for planned probe outages — every recovery was a coordinator-dispatched lane with hand-carried kill-receipts. That works during an operated session; it leaves both operator surfaces dark if a death lands outside one (the cockpit was once ~11h behind frozen pixels before today's heartbeat work).

WHAT EXISTS NOW: cockpit heartbeat file (state/cockpit-heartbeat.json, 1Hz, pid-stamped) + a session-scoped external monitor; the server has /health but nothing watches it.

SPEC SHAPE (single small daemon or two schtasks-style loops, owner: cockpit body track):
1. Cockpit watchdog: heartbeat age > N cycles -> relaunch via the instrumented launcher (stderr capture retained), append one ledger/log row, exponential backoff after 3 rapid deaths (a crashloop must surface as a visible failure, not a silent restart storm). Root cause of today's deaths is KNOWN and cured (commit exhaustion), so an auto-restart can no longer mask an undiagnosed kill — the arming precondition set on 2026-07-08 is satisfied.
2. Server watchdog: /health poll; two consecutive failures -> relaunch with the exact receipted cmdline (the same one the planned-outage recoveries used 3x today, PID lineage 3264->39540->40652->7120), same ledger row + backoff discipline.
3. Both watchdogs REFUSE to act while a planned-outage marker file exists (the probe-outage pattern needs a way to say 'I own this gap') — otherwise the watchdog fights receipted planned kills.
4. Every restart row carries: dead pid, age of last heartbeat/health, relaunch pid, backoff state. Receipts, not silence.

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
One pipeline, one runner, receipts at every boundary. The capture law is the frozen protocol addendum on #449 (comment 4918052395) — this issue makes it runnable and attaches the production stabilization leg that PR #429 proved feasible. Prereg bands (#449) are FROZEN; this spec may not touch them.

## Preconditions (all now satisfied — receipts named)
- Fit config proven: receipt cbase-grow-rung2-gpu-offload-probe-20260708T172949Z (MEASURED_PASS): micro_batch=1, grad_accum=8, grad-checkpointing OFF (effective_readback asserted False), CPU-offload memmap optimizer, peak 18.668 GiB, margin 4.519.
- Genuine pre-grow state EXISTS ON DISK: seed checkpoint models/cbase-grow-rung/rung1-20260703T155447Z/stabilize/checkpoints/step-00000766 carries model.pt + optimizer.pt + rng.pt (attested sha 58e8e989...). No warm leg needed IF the provenance block verifies genuineness (momentum-buffer nonzero-fraction stats per class; a zeroed/reconstructed optstate fails B1 and the runner aborts).
- Perturbed operator merged (#452), estimator promoted (#429), decomposition fields merged (#448).

## Pipeline (strict order, each phase gated on the prior's receipt)
0. PREFLIGHT: commit-aware (GlobalMemoryStatusEx.ullAvailPageFile, floor 10 GiB), GPU headroom assert, disk headroom >= 40 GiB for the snapshot copies.
1. B1: quiesce-proven snapshot of step-766 per the #449 addendum (double-sha manifest across a wait; provenance block; RNG numbers explicit). The seed checkpoint is already at rest — the double-sha is cheap and still mandatory.
2. B1m: u_pre on the pinned measurement batch — gate_proj layer-0 via the existing build_real_d_comm_closures instrument; per-microstep ordered 8-tuple sha over (input_ids, attention_mask, position_ids, labels); dataloader bypassed (serialized tensors); dropout-free deterministic forwards; QAT mode receipted.
3. B2: FRESH widen at eps_sigma > 0 (the #452 live default; 0.0 refused by the operator itself). Cache key must carry eps params — the eps=0 dry-run artifact grown-58e8e989.pt is BANNED from this run. Realized receipts fail-closed: per-pair eta RMS vs tau, twin-cosine < 1 for every split pair, computed from LOADED post-grow weights. Known trap: do not copy the gate-only G() closure's widen call — it omits eps kwargs (defaults 0.0).
4. B3: on a FORKED copy of the B1 snapshot + B2 weights — RESET-arm u_post (explicit zero-momentum assertion, no silent fallback) = the band-(i) measurement; TRANSPLANT-arm u_post captured as the second disclosed measurement (pushforward momentum through the widen map; instrument pre-registration only, does not gate the band). Emit #448 fields; d_comm gate-only vs the frozen scale-convention null sqrt(2); band adjudication is READ OFF the prereg, never re-derived post hoc.
5. STABILIZATION: production training of the grown 2.2B from the B2 weights + reset optimizer under the proven config, 30 steps / 491,520 tokens per docs/spec/rung2-grow-spec-v1.md D1 fixed-FLOPs floor. Receipt: per-step losses, VRAM peak vs the promoted estimator's prediction (mb=1 band: measured within +-15% of 18.253 GiB — this doubles as the estimator's second out-of-sample point), checkpoint at end with full optstate (this becomes rung-3's genuine pre-grow candidate).
6. SERVER WINDOW: the llama-server outage follows the receipted planned-outage routine (kill-receipt first, exact cmdline captured, relaunch + /health verify after) and writes the planned-outage marker per #464's shape so any future watchdog stands down during the window.

## Abort bands
- B1 provenance fails (momentum zeroed) -> abort, report; the warm-leg fallback (resume seed training ~50 steps to regenerate genuine momentum) is a SEPARATE decision, not auto-fired.
- B2 realized-eta or twin-cosine check fails -> abort before B3; nothing measured.
- B3 d_comm lands OUTSIDE all prereg outcomes -> still record (band (iii) attribution path); never re-derive bands.
- Stabilization VRAM exceeds the estimator band -> DEV-002 rule fires exactly as in the probe receipts (kill + attribution, never fix-forward on low headroom).
- Any phase receipt missing -> the next phase refuses to start (fail-closed chaining).

## Runner shape
One script under scripts/ (pattern: cbase_grow_rung2_gpu_offload_probe.py, which routed around run_v0_segment deliberately — with #465 merged the direct path is also viable; builder's call, receipted either way), CLI-driven phases with per-phase receipt JSONs under receipts/, resumable at phase boundaries via the receipts. No board coupling — board conditions consume the receipts later.

refs #449 #429 #452 #448 #464 #411

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
Each totality receipt already carries prev_totality_receipt_sha256, but nothing verifies the chain. Tonight's incident proves the gap: a lane reported a board receipt (172923Z, 9/40 GREEN) that does not exist on disk and whose numbers match no receipt; the coordinator repeated the number twice before catching it by opening artifacts manually. A chain verifier would have caught it mechanically: any receipt whose prev-sha does not match the sha256 of the actual newest prior receipt in receipts-totality/ is either out-of-order, orphaned, or fabricated.

SPEC: a small check (natural home: the C0/receipt_ts_authority tooling family) that walks receipts-totality/ in ts order and asserts (1) each receipt's prev_totality_receipt_sha256 equals the file-sha256 of its predecessor, (2) no gaps/forks, (3) the newest receipt is the chain head. Run it inside the board run itself (append a chain_ok field to the summary) so every board render self-verifies its lineage. Fail-closed: chain break -> the receipt carries chain_ok:false and the incident is visible on the board, not silently rendered.

refs the 2026-07-08 phantom-receipt incident (coordinator-side extraction: success reports carrying numbers get the artifact opened; this issue is the machine-side half).
issue_source_snapshot.title: totality receipt chain-continuity check: prev_totality_receipt_sha256 is recorded but never verified

## The incident (board receipt 20260708T182326Z)
C0 flipped to AUDIT-INCIDENT: two d3-native-loop receipts (20260704T161315Z, 20260704T235144Z) sit in the audit window with zero matching C14 RESIDENT_TRAINING_GATE_PASS receipts in the canonical gate directory. The detector is CORRECT about the canonical evidence surface — this issue is the receipted disposition.

## The trace (read-only, two passes)
- Gate receipts DO exist in git objects, content-verified against test_c0's own criteria: resident-training-gate-20260704T062951Z-issue69-cured.json and resident-training-gate-20260704T065507Z-intree-issue70.json — both verdict RESIDENT_TRAINING_GATE_PASS, status PASS, all components PASS, no disqualifying tokens, plus resident-gate-conflation-audit-20260704T063019Z.json reconciling cleanly (RESIDENT_GATE_CONFLATION_GUARD_PASS). No later BLOCKED/revocation supersedes them anywhere in history.
- Both live exclusively in commits e466e6a / fa73765 on the orphaned goalforge lineage. Lineage fate: ORPHANED, not rejected — no PR rejected these receipts for cause; master pivoted to the clean consolidation (58ddf8d onward) and the consolidation imported the two loop receipts (as *-redacted-edition) WITHOUT their same-day authorization receipts. The custody asymmetry was created by the migration, not by an unauthorized loop.
- Timeline: gate PASS 06:29–06:55Z July 4; loop runs 16:13Z and 23:51Z the same day. The loop receipts do not cite the gate receipts internally (a gap the fail-closed cure below makes structural).

## Ruling (acting operator, receipts-based)
1. **Custody import, narrowly scoped and fully disclosed:** land EXACTLY the three receipt files above into receipts/ember-resident-training-gate/, extracted verbatim from git objects (git show <commit>:<path>), each with a sibling custody note recording: recovered-from commit sha, verified-against-criteria date, and that this import carries NO other claim from the orphaned lineage (in particular none of fa73765's board-percentage claims, which belong to the superseded overstatement era). The import makes the canonical surface match what receipts prove was true at run time.
2. **The incident record stays public** — this issue is the disclosure; the board's AUDIT-INCIDENT window and its resolution are both part of the record. No history rewrite, no receipt backdating: file mtimes/landing dates will honestly show the late import.
3. **Fail-closed launcher cure (the structural half):** the loop launcher must refuse to start when no in-window canonical PASS receipt exists (pre-hoc), and every loop receipt must cite its authorizing gate receipt by ts+sha (making the C0 join mechanical). Post-hoc audit catching this 4 days later is the detector working; the launcher refusing at T0 is the class dying.

## Acceptance
- PR landing the 3 files + custody notes (refs this issue).
- C0 re-evaluation on the next board run showing the incident resolved (or the disposition-assembler path if test_c0 requires an explicit disposition receipt — the assembler exists only on the orphaned lineage; port it narrowly if needed).
- Follow-up item for the launcher gate + loop-receipt citation field.

issue_source_snapshot.author: wordingone
issue_source_snapshot.body:
The rung-2 grow-event PART-B1 preflight receipt measured required=30.903GiB against TOTAL=23.988GiB — the spec'd production stabilization leg exceeds the card even with the cockpit server down. The GPU-window question is therefore moot; the path is a config re-spec priced against the wall receipt, filed per docs/deviations.md discipline.

issue_source_snapshot.body:
The ICML-2026 harvest surfaced a live theory fork that our rung-2 event data can resolve with zero new capture:

- **Zheng et al. (2603.00541, Spectral Condition for muP under Width-Depth Scaling):** at a width-doubling event (r_n=2), Muon hidden-layer updates need an explicit LR correction eta_l = eta_base/sqrt(r_n) — i.e. the post-widen update operator norm should shrink ~1/sqrt(2) ≈ 0.707 relative to pre-widen if no correction is applied and the framework's premise holds.
- **Gupta et al. (2602.20937, extending muP across optimizers):** Muon's NS-orthogonalized step is inherently width-independent (scaling exponents c1=c2=0) because the aspect-ratio factor sqrt(m/n) already sits inside the orthogonalization — predicting the ratio stays ≈ 1.0 with NO correction. Applying both prescriptions would double-scale the update.

**The measurement (b3s phase, addendum to scripts/cbase_grow_rung2_event.py):** compute the operator (spectral) norm ratio ||u_post||_* / ||u_pre||_* for the gate layer-0 Muon update across the widen, on the pinned batch — matched step, matched data, r_n=2.

Everything needed already persists from run_id=grow-rung2-20260708-real:
- u_pre recomputes deterministically from the b1m cache (receipts/.rung2-event-cache/: theta-gate-pre.pt, grad-pre-gate.pt, pre-momentum.pt) via the same _muon_step_in_copy closure the event used.
- u_post recomputes from the b3 fork (models/cbase-grow-rung/rung2-event-grow-rung2-20260708-real/b3-fork) + the b2 grown-weights cache + the pinned batch (sha 2e56e349…, match receipted in b3).
- Spectral norms via torch.linalg top singular value — trivial for one layer's matrices.

Pre-registered read (frozen here, before the number is computed): ratio ≈ 1.0 (within the RMS-jitter band already observed, r=1.013 in RMS convention) = Gupta account confirmed — ember's existing scale=max(1,sqrt(m/n)) term IS the aspect-ratio correction, functioning; NO further LR correction at widen (adopting Zheng's eta/sqrt(r_n) on top would be the double-scaling error). Ratio ≈ 0.707 = the scale term is not functioning as advertised at the widen; Zheng's explicit correction is missing and stabilize's LR convention must be revisited before launch. Intermediate values = both accounts partial; publish the number with the fork as the finding (the commutation paper gains a theory-discriminating axis either way).

Receipt: cbase-grow-rung2-event-<run_id>-b3s.json with {u_pre_spectral, u_post_spectral, ratio, recompute_provenance (cache shas, fork path, batch sha), rms_crosscheck (must reproduce b3's step_rms values exactly — proves the recompute path is faithful)}. Fail-closed: if the RMS cross-check misses b3's persisted values, the receipt is INVALID — never publish a spectral number whose recompute path can't reproduce the known scalars.

GPU: recompute rides a short sliver (single forward+backward on the pinned 8-microstep batch, two model configs); acceptable under L6 as an addendum to the already-earned event window. Serialize behind the resident server per the planned-outage marker contract if VRAM requires.

refs #449 #466
issue_source_snapshot.title: rung-2 spectral addendum (b3s): resolve the Muon width-scaling fork (Zheng vs Gupta) on the already-captured event tensors

Operator, 2026-07-08, confirmed as law: **repo size/growth ≠ ember completion/progress, and repo size/growth ≠ elite research repository quality.** Tonight's measured accretion, no cleanup rule anywhere: 2,272 tracked files; 205 docs; 601 scripts; 939 tracked receipts + 1,637 more untracked on disk; 156 open issues; stale tmp packs in .git. Every mechanism this program builds ADDS files; nothing ever removes one. Elite research repos are lean: every file load-bearing and current, deletion a first-class operation (git history is the archive).

**The rules (land in GOVERNANCE.md as one short section via this PR chain):**
1. **Docs:** every doc under docs/ declares what supersedes/invalidates it (the GOAL §8 map pattern, generalized). A superseded doc is DELETED in the superseding PR — never left beside its replacement. Version-suffixed spec files (v1, v2) may keep at most the live version + the frozen prereg editions the claims cite.
2. **Receipts retention:** receipts cited by the board, the credibility battery, an open claim, or a frozen prereg are PROTECTED. Uncited receipts older than 30 days move to the annex pattern (custody model already supports annex_attested) in one quarterly sweep PR; the working receipts/ set stays readable end-to-end by a stranger.
3. **Scripts:** a script referenced by no playbook, board probe, test, or doc is dead — each hygiene pass proposes its deletion with the reference-scan as evidence.
4. **Issues:** consolidation cadence — issues silent >14d get one disposition comment: folded into a carrier issue (pointer), parked-with-path in the floor contract, or surfaced for operator kill (L7: kill stays operator-only; consolidation with a pointer is not a kill).
5. **The metric (receipts, not vibes):** the totality board run appends a working-set line — tracked files, docs count, scripts count, tracked receipts, open issues — to the board receipt. The SIM/review watches the TREND against battery-grade movement: working-set growth across a window where no battery row improved = a named wince. Growth must buy graded evidence or it is clutter.
6. **Issue creation discipline (binds the coordinator too):** extend an existing carrier issue over opening a new one whenever the work shares a track — six new issues in one night is itself a data point this law exists to correct.

**First cleanup pass (lane-executed, evidence-per-file, deletions via reviewed PR — nothing auto-deleted):** reference-scan docs/ and scripts/ for unreferenced/superseded candidates; propose the deletion manifest with per-file evidence (what referenced it last, when, superseded-by); triage the 1,637 untracked receipts into cited/annex/delete; prune .git tmp packs. Acceptance: the manifest PR lands with GOVERNANCE rules + the board working-set line, and the follow-up deletion PR shrinks the working set while every battery grade holds or improves.
issue_source_snapshot.title: repo hygiene law: growth is not progress — retention rules, consolidation cadence, size-vs-progress metric, first cleanup pass

## Frozen spec v1 (coordinator-authored; S5 constitutional clause gets its measurement)

GOAL.md §5 makes nativization a DRIVE ('which layer comes home next is earned by receipts on where borrowed code costs most') — but no receipt series measures borrowed surface. This runner ends S5 as an unmeasured clause.

### Runner: scripts/nativization_motion.py
Pure-local static census, no GPU, no network. For each LAYER in the substrate map (docs/ember-owned-substrate-diagnostic.md — parse its layer list; if headings drift, fail loudly rather than guessing):
- **borrowed_deps**: count of distinct external packages imported (stdlib excluded; ember-owned modules excluded) across the layer's file globs
- **borrowed_loc**: total lines in files whose imports include external packages, split into owned_loc vs borrowed-touching loc
- **borrowed_binaries**: named external executables the layer shells out to (llama-server, docker, git, bun) — regex over subprocess/exec call sites
- **delta_vs_prior**: numeric diff vs the previous receipt in the series (first receipt: delta null, disclosed)
- **next_home_candidate**: v1 proxy = the layer with the highest borrowed_deps not yet marked 'home' in the diagnostic map; the receipt states the proxy is a RANKING HEURISTIC, not a wall-receipt measurement (v2 upgrades to wall-receipt weighting per §5's own text)

### Receipt: receipts/nativization-motion/nm-<UTCts>.json
Schema: {ts, invariant_sha256, map_source_sha (sha256 of the diagnostic doc consumed), layers: [{name, borrowed_deps: [names], borrowed_deps_count, borrowed_loc, owned_loc, borrowed_binaries}], deltas, next_home_candidate, method: 'static-import-census-v1', limits: [named blind spots — dynamic imports, vendored code, binary deps of deps]}

### Tests (TDD, CI, no network)
Fixture mini-tree with known imports → exact expected counts; map-drift failure case (missing heading → loud error); delta computation vs a fixture prior receipt.

### Rails
Worktree lane; PR stop-at-open; refs-only body; runner is read-only over the tree (writes ONLY its receipt).

- New ember-cli capability module: GitHub client authenticating as a **GitHub App installation** (App JWT -> installation access token, cached with expiry, auto-refresh).

- Receipts: every WRITE action appends a JSONL receipt row (actor=ember-cli-bot, action, target, ts) — provenance discipline extends to the body's outward actions.

App registration/installation itself (browser leg, tracked separately). Multi-repo scope. Any use of a personal PAT.
